title: Impact of multidimensional self-disclosure on review helpfulness from the perspective of the elaboration likelihood model
affiliations: Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, Tilburg University and Harbin Institute of Technology

detail.title: Impact of multidimensional self-disclosure on review helpfulness from the perspective of the elaboration likelihood model
detail.abstract:
Purpose-This paper employed the elaboration likelihood model (ELM) to investigate the effects of multidimensional self-disclosure on review helpfulness, focusing on three forms of self-disclosure: identity disclosure, picture disclosure, and text self-disclosure. Moreover, the moderating effects of review sentiment considering the effect of potential negativity bias were included in the model. Design/methodology/approach-A substantial dataset was collected from Ctrip.com, comprising 2,671,744 reviews of 6,862 distinct hotels in Beijing. Tobit regression models were employed in the empirical analysis. 
Findings-The results revealed that, after controlling for the other factors, reviewer identity and picture disclosure, which had been categorized as peripheral cues, had significant positive impacts on review helpfulness. By contrast, there was an inverted U-shaped relationship between the depth of textual self-disclosure, a central cue, and review helpfulness. Furthermore, the results indicated that negative sentiments in reviews could strengthen the influence of multidimensional self-disclosure on review helpfulness, outweighing the impact of positive sentiments. 
Originality/value-This study is the first attempt to examine review helpfulness from the perspective of consumer multidimensional self-disclosure, providing a distinctive viewpoint. It advances the literature by utilizing the elaboration likelihood model to explicate the mechanism behind the impact of multidimensional self-disclosure on review helpfulness and expands the literature on negativity bias by revealing how review sentiment moderates the relationship between self-disclosure and review helpfulness.

Personality Traits Scale Based on Ptolemy's Four Elements Theory
(According to the Sun Sign): A Psychometric Study on Jordanian Society

declarations.funderStatement: It was funded at my own expense

detail.abstract:
This study developed and validated a personality traits scale based on Ptolemy’s Four Elements Theory (Fire, Earth, Air, Water), specifically categorized according to the Sun Sign. The research utilized a descriptive-analytical approach with a sample of 564 participants from Jordanian society. 
Psychometric properties were established through expert judgment and factor analysis. Results showed high correlation with the MMPI subscales, supporting the scale's validity. The study demonstrates that the Four Elements model, when applied through Sun Signs, provides a robust framework for understanding personality in a modern context.

title: Neuro marketing in Virtual Reality Shopping: Understanding Consumer Behaviour in Immersive Environments

detail.title: Neuro marketing in Virtual Reality Shopping: Understanding Consumer Behaviour in Immersive Environments
detail.abstract: In the era of digital transformation, Virtual Reality (VR) has emerged as a powerful tool in redefining consumer experiences. Neuromarketing, which studies consumers' cognitive and emotional responses, plays a crucial role in understanding behaviour in immersive environments. This research explores how neuromarketing techniques influence consumer decision-making within VR shopping experiences. Adopting a quantitative and conceptual approach (inspired by your reference paper structure), the study analyses key factors such as emotional engagement, sensory stimulation, and personalization. Findings indicate that immersive VR environments significantly enhance consumer attention, emotional connection, and purchase intention. However, challenges such as ethical concerns, high costs, and data privacy issues remain.

title: AI Agents and the Shifting Landscape of Hotel Distribution: A Practitioner-Research Perspective

detail.title: AI Agents and the Shifting Landscape of Hotel Distribution: A Practitioner-Research Perspective
detail.abstract: The hospitality distribution landscape is entering a period of structural change. For two decades, online travel agencies (OTAs) have occupied the dominant intermediary position between hotels and travelers. The emergence of AI agents-systems capable of autonomously searching, evaluating, and executing bookings on behalf of travelers-introduces a fundamentally different dynamic. This research note, informed by the author's nearly decade-long experience in international hotel distribution strategy and current postdoctoral research, identifies three observable market signals that suggest the intermediary landscape may be shifting. The scope of this note is limited to documenting these signals as practitioner observations; it does not propose a theoretical framework, develop analytical models, or advance methodological claims. A separate academic study addressing the structural and theoretical dimensions of these developments is in preparation.

title: Creating a Theory-Based Research Agenda for Gamification
affiliations: Upper Austria - University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria and MODUL University Vienna

detail.title: Creating a Theory-Based Research Agenda for Gamification
detail.abstract: Gamification is a topic which has recently gained significant attention in the IS community due to its relevance for both practitioners and academics. Being a boundary-spanning subject by nature, it also attracts interest from scholars from diverse non-IS communities, including education, marketing and business administration. In this paper we develop a research agenda for gamification which explicitly takes into account the important role of theory. An interdisciplinary expert panel evaluated and selected theories being relevant for gamification and subsequently derived research questions. Based on the respective theoretical background the resulting questions cover different aspects of the gamification domain. We conclude that taking a multi-theoretical perspective in the creation of a research agenda helps to produce a holistic picture, which allows classifying subsequent research and helps in structuring a domain.

title: Rectification Difficulty and Optimal Sample Allocation in LLM-Augmented Surveys
affiliations: University of Washington - Michael G. Foster School of Business and University of Washington

detail.title: Rectification Difficulty and Optimal Sample Allocation in LLM-Augmented Surveys
detail.abstract: Large Language Models can generate synthetic survey responses at low cost, but their accuracy varies unpredictably across questions. We study the design problem of allocating a fixed budget of human respondents across estimation tasks when cheap LLM predictions are available for every task. Our framework combines three components. First, building on Prediction-Powered Inference, we characterize a question-specific rectification difficulty that governs how quickly the estimator's variance decreases with human sample size. Second, we derive a closed-form optimal allocation rule that directs more human labels to tasks where the LLM is least reliable. Third, since rectification difficulty depends on unobserved human responses for new surveys, we propose a meta-learning approach, trained on historical data, that predicts it for entirely new tasks without pilot data. The framework extends to general M-estimation, covering regression coefficients and multinomial logit partworths for conjoint analysis. We validate the framework on two datasets spanning different domains, question types, and LLMs, showing that our approach captures 61--79% of the theoretically attainable efficiency gains, achieving 11.4% and 10.5% MSE reductions without requiring any pilot human data for the target survey.

title: The Effect of Word-of-Mouth Marketing on Customer Loyalty & Product Sales

detail.title: The Effect of Word-of-Mouth Marketing on Customer Loyalty & Product Sales
detail.abstract: Word of Mouth (WOM) communication has emerged as one of the most influential factors affecting consumer behavior and sales performance in modern markets. With the rapid growth of digital platforms, WOM has evolved from traditional interpersonal conversations into a powerful online phenomenon capable of shaping brand perceptions at scale. This research explores the impact of WOM on sales by analyzing how consumer opinions, trust, and social influence contribute to purchase decisions. The study highlights that WOM, both offline and online, significantly enhances brand credibility, reduces perceived risk, and ultimately drives revenue growth. The findings suggest that businesses that strategically leverage WOM can achieve a sustainable competitive advantage.

title: THE INDIVIDUAL'S REACTION TO INFORMATION OVERLOAD AND THE NEED FOR SEGMENTATION THROUGH PSYCHOGRAPHIC PROFILES

detail.title: THE INDIVIDUAL'S REACTION TO INFORMATION OVERLOAD AND THE NEED FOR SEGMENTATION THROUGH PSYCHOGRAPHIC PROFILES
detail.abstract: The electronic stage of communication has put the individual's consciousness in conditions of extreme overload. The human nervous system is not able to process the enormous amount of information. In order to function normally, a person must have ways to 'sift' it, focusing their attention on only a part of it. The hypothesis is that due to their psychological specifics, users form groups with similar features of information acceptance. In order to verify the existence of such groups and to highlight their characteristics, in the period 2001-2023, more than 130 quantitative surveys were conducted, nationally representative of the country's population or certain groups of it, by the method of direct personal interviews with the application of an identical set of indicators, allowing through correlation, factor and cluster analyses to distinguish the groups according to the Psychographic Profiles. As a result, 4 groups were found, identical for Bulgaria and for other countries, which react to information in a similar way by directing their attention to that part of it that most fully corresponds to the essence of the personality. This made it possible for entities producing information-companies, state and public structures-to refine their communication, make it more effective and more economical by orienting it towards a dominant Psychographic Profile for their purposes.

title: Empathetic Leadership in Managing Generation Z

detail.title: Empathetic Leadership in Managing Generation Z
detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper examines the relationship between leadership style, feedback practices, and the mental well-being of younger employees in contemporary organizations. It focuses particularly on Generation Z and analyzes how empathetic management and future-oriented feedback may better address the psychological and professional needs of this cohort. The study also considers intergenerational differences in the workplace and their implications for leadership effectiveness.. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts a conceptual research approach based on a critical review of literature on generational diversity, emotional intelligence, mental well-being, and feedback practices. The analysis integrates perspectives from leadership studies, organizational behavior, and employee well-being research. Particular attention is given to empathetic leadership and the Feed Forward model as tools for supporting younger employees. Findings: The analysis suggests that effective management in the 21st century requires adapting leadership styles and communication practices to the distinct expectations of different employee generations. Generation Z appears to be more vulnerable to stress, anxiety, and reduced psychological resilience, which increases the importance of supportive leadership and psychologically safe work environments. The findings indicate that empathetic leadership and future-oriented feedback may enhance motivation, engagement, and mental well-being among younger employees. Research limitations/implications: The study is conceptual and based primarily on literature analysis rather than empirical testing. Future research could include cross-generational comparative studies, industry-specific analyses, and empirical assessments of the impact of empathetic leadership and Feed Forward practices on employee well-being and performance. Additional research could also explore the long-term effects of feedback style on resilience and retention among younger workers. Practical recommendations: Organizations should adapt leadership and communication practices to the needs of a multigenerational workforce. Managers should strengthen empathetic leadership competencies and use feedback methods that reduce defensiveness and support growth, particularly in relation to younger employees. Regular, constructive, and future-oriented feedback may improve employee development, workplace relationships, and mental well-being.

title: Who Is Speaking Within You? Identity Multiplicity and Psychological Flexibility
affiliations: and International Institute for Applied System Analysis

detail.title: Who Is Speaking Within You? Identity Multiplicity and Psychological Flexibility
detail.abstract: The traditional view of identity as a unified and stable construct has been increasingly challenged by contemporary psychological theories emphasizing multiplicity and context-dependence. Dialogical Self-Theory (DST), developed by Hubert Hermans, conceptualizes the self as a dynamic system of interacting "I-positions," each representing distinct internal voices. This article examines identity multiplicity as a foundational feature of human cognition and explores its relationship with psychological flexibility. Drawing on theoretical perspectives from narrative psychology, self-schema theory, and flexibility research, the paper argues that adaptive functioning depends on the ability to shift, integrate, and regulate internal voices rather than maintain a rigid, singular identity. A conceptual framework for mapping identity multiplicity and enhancing flexibility is presented. The article concludes that recognizing "who is speaking within" is essential for fostering resilience, adaptive decision-making, and coherent selfdevelopment.

title: The Solvency Margin: A Speed-Limit Metric for Capital-Constrained Organizations Under Stress

detail.title: The Solvency Margin: A Speed-Limit Metric for Capital-Constrained Organizations Under Stress

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors are affiliated with Poisson Consulting, LLC, a supply chain strategy firm. Poisson Consulting has advised clients in the manufacturing sectors analyzed in this paper. No client commissioned, funded, or reviewed this research. All empirical analysis uses publicly available data from SEC filings, FDIC disclosures, and published industry sources. The authors declare no other competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The authors conducted all analysis independently.

detail.abstract: The most widely used bankruptcy predictor, Altman's Z-Score, assigns a positive coefficient to asset turnover: faster firms are rated safer. Under crisis conditions, that assumption reverses. We introduce the Solvency Margin (SM), a diagnostic calculable from standard financial statements that measures, in dollars, how far an organization is from the threshold where operations become impossible. Unlike static liquidity ratios, the SM yields a concrete speed limit: the maximum operating velocity at which an organization can survive a defined shock. We validate the SM against pre-crisis financial data across three crises in two domains. In the automotive sector, SM computed from FY2019 filings showed directional predictive power among ten major automakers in both the 2021 semiconductor shortage (ρ = 0.50, p = 0.14) and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic (ρ = 0.53, p = 0.12; ρ = 0.70, p = 0.036 excluding one governance-driven outlier). In the 2023 U.S. banking crisis, SM augmented with a Deposit Stability Factor predicted crisis outcomes among eighteen regional banks (Spearman ρ = 0.62, p = 0.006), correctly ranking three of four failed institutions in the bottom three positions. Monte Carlo simulation (450,000+ runs) confirms threshold behavior across a wide range of conditions. We present a five-step calculation method and a three-lever decision framework for practitioners.

title: The Anatomy of Self-Doubt: Competing Internal Narratives and Their Behavioral Impact
affiliations: and University of Saskatchewan - Interdisciplinary Studies

detail.title: The Anatomy of Self-Doubt: Competing Internal Narratives and Their Behavioral Impact
detail.abstract: The psychological phenomenon of self-doubt is overwhelmingly and incorrectly conceptualized as a singular, uniform state characterized by generalized uncertainty and reduced self-efficacy. This monolithic perspective categorically fails to capture the extreme internal complexity and precise behavioral consequences of doubt. Leveraging Dialogical Self-Theory (DST), developed by Hubert Hermans, this analysis dismantles the traditional paradigm, redefining self-doubt as a highly volatile ecosystem of competing internal narratives. Doubt does not emerge from a single cognitive deficit, but from the severe friction generated when distinct, autonomous narrative voices violently contest the interpretation of reality, emotional valence, and subsequent action. By integrating advanced insights from cognitive psychology, narrative identity theory, and selfregulatory neuroscience, this paper systematically maps how these narratives dictate behavior through the mechanisms of monological dominance, cognitive conflict, and behavioral reinforcement loops. A comprehensive anatomical framework of self-doubt is established, providing the exact operational mechanics required to improve executive decision-making, optimize high-stress performance, and engineer psychological resilience. The analysis concludes that the objective is never the elimination of doubt, but the strategic dialogical orchestration of the narratives that construct it, thereby transforming a paralyzing limitation into a highly functional mechanism of adaptive self-regulation.

title: Agent-Facing Information Design in LLM Tool Registries
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and University of Chicago

detail.title: Agent-Facing Information Design in LLM Tool Registries
detail.abstract: LLM tool registries function as unregulated advertising platforms: providers write free-text descriptions that agents use for selection, yet no measurement infrastructure-no viewability standard, quality score, or outcome audit-exists to make this market accountable. We provide the first systematic framework, combining 17,700+ trials across five LLMs and ten domains with a constructive registry design prescription. Legal puffery alone (subjective superlatives, benefit framing) captures 100% of the optimization effect; fabricated claims add zero incremental bias-rendering FTC enforcement of deceptive advertising rules ineffective against the active mechanism. Disclosure fails structurally: system-prompt warnings produce zero measurable effect for four of five models, and behavioral ceilings leave no headroom for label-based correction. Superlatives are the dominant single feature (SBC = +0.35). Registry-layer description normalization achieves first-best welfare model-independently. We propose separating selection-facing descriptions (structured, registrycontrolled) from marketing-facing descriptions (provider-authored, shown post-selection), and introduce the Agent Attention Quality Score to distinguish capability from copywriting.

title: Mapping the Scholarly Landscape of TikTok (Douyin): A Bibliometric Exploration of Research Topics and Trends
affiliations: Széchenyi István University, Kautz Gyula Faculty of Economics, Department of Logistics and Forwarding, Students, Higher Institute of Computer Science of El Manar, University of Rome Tor Vergata, MODUL University Vienna and Edith Cowan University

detail.title: Mapping the Scholarly Landscape of TikTok (Douyin): A Bibliometric Exploration of Research Topics and Trends
detail.abstract: The TikTok platform has become widely popular among younger generations and has influenced various industries and aspects of life. This systematic literature review, using bibliometric methods, aims to examine the evolution of TikTok research from its initial development to its current status. A total of 402 journal articles from 2019 to 2022 were systematically selected from the Web of Science Core Collection. Descriptive statistical analysis identified the most contributing academic institutions, nations, journals, scholars, and influential studies. Using CiteSpace, three visualization types were implemented: cluster views, timezone views, and timeline views. The study results indicate that several TikTok research clusters exist, which summarize important topics such as the platform's overall impact on society, politics, culture, as well as human-centric issues such as social attachment, functional tics, and their implications for public health. According to the co-word analysis, TikTok research revolves around body consciousness, social behavior, consumer behavior, and news media. The comprehensive mapping of TikTok research provides valuable insights into the current state of knowledge and identifies numerous relevant technical and social areas for future investigation. As the first bibliometric review of TikTok research, this study offers an important foundation for future scholarly inquiry in various areas.

title: What is the complete journey that festival memories take, from their creation to their impact on engagement?

detail.title: What is the complete journey that festival memories take, from their creation to their impact on engagement?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on voluntary participation. All participants were informed about the purpose of the research and gave their consent. No personal or sensitive data was collected.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
It is difficult to exist in an increasingly competitive music festival sector. The major challenges posed by modern issues continue to multiply. We are seeing a change in consumer habits and a drastic increase in production costs that make it difficult for organizing structures to survive. 

In order to respond to these issues, it is no longer possible to simply offer events or concerts one after the other; festival-goers are looking for real experiences that are thought out and considered to be as memorable as possible. Thus, memorability becomes a key aspect to consider when we want to generate strong and lasting engagement among festival-goers. 

The objective of this thesis will be to capture the nuances of what represents a memorable memory by chronologically tracing the complete journey that Generation Z’s festival memories take. Thus, this path will begin with their creation and will end by addressing the impact they can have on post-festival engagement.

To address these issues, I interviewed 21 festival-goers during semi-structured interviews about their memories, their evolution, and their involvement with festivals. Among these festival goers, some have already been volunteers, artists, or service providers during these events. These different points of view will allow me to obtain a global, complete, and objective spectrum of what a memorable experience represents.

The study allowed me to understand the levers that allowed an event to remain anchored in memory. Also, this research highlights the major role played by the community, through remanence, recitation, and socialization in the evolution of memories. Finally, post-event engagement is examined to understand what drives it or hinders it.

The study confirms a large number of previous studies such as Durkheim’s on collective effervescence, Collins’s on the importance of rituals, or Pine and Gilmore’s, who propose a conceptual model for creating memorable experiences. The theoretical implications of this study will be discussed in order to provide concrete practical managerial advice to music festival organizers.

reference: University of Illinois Law Review, Issue 3, expected 2027.
title: WORKING NOTICE
affiliations: University of Nevada, Las Vegas, William S. Boyd School of Law

detail.title: WORKING NOTICE

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Illinois Law Review, Issue 3, expected 2027.

detail.abstract:
Wage theft experienced by our nation's low-wage workers remains extraordinarily high-upwards of $13 billion dollars goes unpaid each year. While federal and state enforcement of wage rights continues to wane, private enforcement has become increasingly difficult: courts have undermined the federal wage protection law (the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 (FLSA)) by restricting worker participation, and that result is neither textually nor historically defensible.
A current five-Circuit split highlights the schism in our judicial system that restricts the ability for low-wage workers to timely participate in collective action. In the absence of U.S. Supreme Court guidance, lower courts routinely limit the number of workers able to prosecute their wage exploitation claims by judicially gatekeeping if and when notice of collective action lawsuits is sent to workers. This results in expiring claims and diminishing deterrent effects on unscrupulous employers.
This Article provides a path forward to harmonize the current Circuit split and for courts to recognize and revive the legislative purpose of federal wage protection laws by providing sufficient notice to workers on vindicating their wage rights. In essence, courts should recognize that notice is proper so long as “any question of law or fact common to all plaintiffs will arise in the action.” This realigns a notice standard with the prevailing permissive joinder framework of the time of FLSA’s enactment, and allows it to effectuate the FLSA’s remedial purpose, as recognized by the Supreme Court decades ago: “to aid the unprotected, unorganized, and lowest paid of the nation’s working population.” Such aid is needed now more than ever.

title: The AI-Native Venture Studio Operating System A Practitioner Framework for Systematic Venture Creation

detail.title: The AI-Native Venture Studio Operating System A Practitioner Framework for Systematic Venture Creation

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper sets out a practical model for building ventures in a world where AI is no longer just a feature inside products, but part of the operating machinery of the venture itself. The argument is straightforward. Venture studios work because they systematise discovery, launch, learning and resource sharing across multiple bets. Their weakness is cost. They remain people-heavy, capitalintensive organisations. Recent advances in AI orchestration suggest a different structure is now possible: a lean operating model in which AI works at two levels at once. At the venture level it powers analysis, coordination and service delivery where useful. At the portfolio level it supports market scanning, launch decisions, monitoring, knowledge capture and cross-venture learning. The result is not a traditional studio with AI tools added on top. It is an operating system for venture creation in which the shared infrastructure is intelligent by design and the ventures themselves can remain comparatively thin. The model described here emerged from practical work on a difficult two-sided marketplace problem and then widened into a broader framework for venture creation. The paper is deliberately positioned as a working paper and practitioner framework. Its purpose is to define the model, explain why it matters, and place a public timestamp on the concept.

title: Strategic Deadlock in the Second Iranian War: Dynamics of "Safe Exit" and Re-engineering Regional Balances

detail.title: Strategic Deadlock in the Second Iranian War: Dynamics of "Safe Exit" and Re-engineering Regional Balances

keywords: Arab Joint Force . JEL Classification Codes:
Economic Nationalism Energy and the Macroeconomy International Agreements and Observance
Geopolitics of the Strait of Hormuz

detail.abstract: The military operations of the "Second Iranian War" (Operation Epic Fury) have surpassed their eleventh day without achieving the structural collapse of the Iranian regime, primarily due to the swift institutional transition of power to Mojtaba Khamenei. This transition aborted the "sovereign vacuum" hypothesis, shifting the conflict from a "shock and awe" tactic to a complex environment of "strategic attrition." While U.S. and Israeli operations-such as "Operation Roaring Lion"-focus on maximizing geopolitical shifts and dismantling infrastructure, Iran has adapted through decentralized asymmetric warfare and naval mine deployments in the Strait of Hormuz, causing severe geoeconomic shocks to global energy markets. Amidst mounting financial costs and declining domestic support in the U.S., indicators point to an American desire to engineer a "safe exit" through diplomatic channels and potential "Trump-Putin" grand trade-offs. Concurrently, Egypt assumes a central sovereign role anchored in the "Regional Exclusivity" doctrine, rejecting external security arrangements in the Red Sea, and advocating for a joint Arab force to safeguard the national state and secure long-term regional stability.

title: Climate Risk and Financial Stability: The Strategic Role of Credit Unions in Sustainable Finance and Risk Mitigation in the United States

detail.title: Climate Risk and Financial Stability: The Strategic Role of Credit Unions in Sustainable Finance and Risk Mitigation in the United States
detail.abstract: Climate change has emerged as a material financial risk with profound implications for asset valuation, credit performance, operational resilience, and systemic stability. Financial institutions are increasingly exposed to both physical risks, such as extreme weather events, and transition risks associated with regulatory, technological, and market shifts toward a low-carbon economy. Credit unions, as community-based financial institutions, face unique vulnerabilities due to their geographic concentration and close ties to local economies. At the same time, they possess distinctive capabilities that position them as critical actors in advancing climate resilience and sustainable finance. This article develops a leadership-driven framework that integrates climate risk into enterprise risk management (ERM), organizational strategy, and governance structures within credit unions. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature from financial economics, sustainability, and risk governance, the study argues that climate risk must be treated as a core financial risk rather than a peripheral environmental issue. The article contributes to the literature by linking climate risk governance to financial stability and by identifying leadership, culture, and institutional strategy as key enablers of resilience. Implications for policymakers, regulators, and financial institutions are discussed, with a focus on aligning local financial practices with national economic priorities.

title: ESG Scores and Downside Risk Resilience: Evidence from S&P 500 Equities (2024-2025)

detail.title: ESG Scores and Downside Risk Resilience: Evidence from S&P 500 Equities (2024-2025)

keywords: portfolio risk JEL Codes: G11 (Portfolio Choice)

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether higher Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) scores are associated with greater stock return resilience during periods of market stress among S&P 500 constituents. Using daily price data for 410 firms over the period January 2024 through December 2025, combined with firm-level ESG scores from 2023, we define market stress days as trading sessions in which the S&P 500 index return falls within the bottom tenth percentile of the empirical return distribution. A Welch two-sample t-test reveals that High-ESG firms experience average daily losses approximately 0.28 percentage points smaller than Low-ESG firms on these extreme negative market days, a difference that is statistically significant (t = 8.48, p < 0.001). A supplementary analysis of market beta-a measure of a firm's sensitivity to overall market movements, where a beta greater than 1 indicates amplified market swings-reveals that High-ESG firms carry significantly lower betas than their Low-ESG counterparts (mean difference of 0.075, t =-13.43, p < 0.001), suggesting that part of the observed stress-day resilience is structurally embedded in the lower systematic risk profile of High-ESG firms. Threshold sensitivity analysis confirms this finding is robust across alternative stress definitions (5th, 10th, and 15th percentiles). However, sector-level decomposition reveals that the aggregate ESG resilience effect is substantially explained by the disproportionate concentration of High-ESG firms in structurally defensive sectors-specifically Consumer Staples, Utilities, and Health Care-which account for 75.5% of the High-ESG group whereas in cyclical sector High-ESG groups constitute 41.3% only. Among High-ESG firms alone, those in defensive sectors lose 0.42% on stress days compared to 1.63% for their cyclical-sector counterparts. Ordinary least squares regressions controlling for market beta and sector fixed effects confirm that a modest, statistically significant residual ESG effect persists after controlling for these confounders. We conclude that ESG characteristics are associated with downside resilience, but that sector composition is the primary structural driver of this association. These findings carry implications for sustainable investment portfolio construction and risk management.

title: Solo Decision Architecture (SDA) Framework: An Operating System Powered by the Dual Lens Principle

detail.title: Solo Decision Architecture (SDA) Framework: An Operating System Powered by the Dual Lens Principle

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Both authors are co-founders of BC-DS, Business Consultants for Digital Solutions, LLC, the company that operates the Convoking4 platform documented as the implementation context for the Solo Decision Architecture framework in this paper. BC-DS holds commercial interests in the Convoking4 platform's tier structure, which monetizes platform capability and credentialing, and in the forthcoming Decisiontect certification program. The framework specification itself is released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) and is operable independently of the Convoking4 platform, as documented in the paper's Companion Documents section. The authors received no external funding for the research presented in this paper. The authors declare no other financial or non-financial relationships that could be perceived as influencing the work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted by the authors at BC-DS, Business Consultants for Digital Solutions, LLC, using internal company resources.

detail.abstract:
The Solo Decision Architecture (SDA) framework operationalizes the foundational technique documented in the Methodological Layer of the Decision Architecture discipline (Hernandez and Montero 2026b) at the individual scale, where a single Decision Architect is the unit of accountability for a consequential commitment. The framework is currently implemented on the Convoking4 platform, and this paper documents that implementation. The Diagnostic Layer of the discipline (Hernandez and Montero 2026a) establishes that consequential decisions are distorted by the compounding interaction of human cognitive bias, organizational dynamics, and the technical properties of generative artificial intelligence, with distortion forming inside one person's thinking before it ever reaches a team. The Methodological Layer establishes the technique that responds to the diagnostic, backcasting and the dual lens with a decision architecture artifact as its output, and the five constraints any framework operationalizing the technique must meet.

The implementation captures the practitioner's frame in a Brain Dump phase conducted human-only, extracts four coordinates under the Honest Extraction rule, and proceeds through a nine-phase session that holds aspiration and constraint together through the dual lens. Structural mechanisms enforce the methodology's conditions at specific gates: the Camera Test on milestone inspectability, the ADICE Matrix on stakeholder assumptions, the Flinch Test on commitment acceptance, and the bidirectional Verification on artifact convergence.

The paper documents the implementation's structural answers to the methodology's five constraints, with platform-design enforcement of the four AI participation conditions producing the methodology's required conditions during the practitioner's normal use of the system rather than relying on the practitioner to maintain the conditions through self-discipline. The implementation does not eliminate the diagnostic's failure modes; it bounds their reach into the artifact through structural mechanisms documented across the paper. Practitioner discipline at specific points where the platform structures but does not strictly enforce remains essential, and the paper names honestly the failure modes the implementation can exhibit when applied dishonestly and the failure modes the implementation does not address.

The SDA on Convoking4 is one of two platform-anchored implementations of the technique on a shared methodological foundation. The Business Decision Architecture (BDA) framework, forthcoming as the companion publication, operationalizes the same technique at the organizational scale. The two implementations interlock through practitioners who move between scales: the SDA produces audited individual frames that the BDA process integrates, and the BDA produces organizational decisions that individuals execute through their own SDA practice.

The paper closes with empirical research questions specific to the SDA's claims, offered to the broader research community as a structured agenda for testing what the framework asserts about artifact examinability, the Stage 1 / Stage 2 boundary, milestone inspectability, commitment accountability, and the implementation's bounded scope.

title: Financial Inclusion as Economic Infrastructure: The Strategic Role of Credit Unions in Reducing Inequality and Strengthening U.S. Economic Stability

detail.title: Financial Inclusion as Economic Infrastructure: The Strategic Role of Credit Unions in Reducing Inequality and Strengthening U.S. Economic Stability
detail.abstract: Financial inclusion has traditionally been framed as a social or developmental objective; however, emerging evidence suggests that it should be reconceptualized as a foundational component of economic infrastructure. Access to affordable financial services-particularly credit, savings, and payment systems, plays a critical role in enabling economic participation, supporting entrepreneurship, and fostering long-term financial stability. Credit unions, as cooperative financial institutions, occupy a uniquely strategic position within this framework due to their member-centric governance, community orientation, and mission-driven approach to service delivery. This article develops a leadership-driven framework that positions financial inclusion as economic infrastructure, integrating insights from institutional economics, resourcebased theory, and financial intermediation. It argues that expanding inclusive financial systems is essential not only for reducing inequality but also for enhancing national economic resilience. The article contributes to the literature by reframing financial inclusion as a systemic economic function and by identifying leadership, organizational culture, and governance as critical enablers of scalable inclusion. Implications for policymakers, financial institutions, and national economic strategy are discussed.

title: Artificial Intelligence Governance in Credit Unions: Balancing Innovation, Risk, and Consumer Protection in the U.S. Financial System

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance in Credit Unions: Balancing Innovation, Risk, and Consumer Protection in the U.S. Financial System
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming financial services by enabling advanced analytics, automation, and data-driven decision-making. While these capabilities enhance efficiency and expand access to financial products, they also introduce complex risks related to bias, transparency, accountability, and systemic instability. Credit unions, as cooperative financial institutions serving over 135 million Americans, face a unique challenge: adopting AIdriven innovation while maintaining their foundational commitments to fairness, trust, and member-centric service. This article develops a leadership-driven framework for AI governance that integrates enterprise risk management (ERM), ethical accountability, and regulatory alignment. Drawing on interdisciplinary research across financial technology, organizational theory, and risk governance, the study argues that AI must be governed as a strategic capability rather than a technical tool. The article contributes to the literature by bridging the gap between AI implementation and leadership-based governance while providing actionable insights for aligning innovation with national priorities related to consumer protection and financial system stability.

title: Did Newspaper Competition Promote Rebellion? The case of the 1837-38 Rebellions in Quebec *

detail.title: Did Newspaper Competition Promote Rebellion? The case of the 1837-38 Rebellions in Quebec *

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicnt
declarations.ethicsApproval: No participants were used
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract:
We investigate the relationship between media competitiveness and political mobilization during the Quebec Rebellion of 1837-38. We argue that the rebellion was shaped by newspaper coordination of political action. Drawing on a new spatial dataset of newspaper agents, we test whether local media competitiveness predicts the intensity of rebel mobilization, independent of the partisan alignment of the press. The effect is magnified in areas where seigneurial (i.e., feudal) tenure persisted, suggesting a complementarity between institutionally concentrated grievance and competitive press exposure. Adding newly created human capital controls-school enrollment and literacy-does not attenuate the competition effect. Globally, media competition transformed latent discontent into active participation in the conflict. These results offer insight into the economics of rebellions and uprisings.

Nous étudions la relation entre la compétitivité médiatique et la mobilisation politique durant la rébellion du Québec de 1837--38. Nous soutenons que la rébellion a été façonnée par la coordination de l’action politique par les journaux. À partir d’un nouvel ensemble de données spatiales sur les agents de journaux, nous testons si la compétitivité médiatique locale prédit l’intensité de la mobilisation rebelle, indépendamment de l’alignement partisan de la presse. L’effet est amplifié dans les zones où le régime seigneurial (c’est-à-dire féodal) persistait, ce qui suggère une complémentarité entre des griefs institutionnellement concentrés et l’exposition à une presse concurrentielle. L’ajout de nouveaux contrôles de capital humain — taux de scolarisation et alphabétisation — n’atténue pas l’effet de la concurrence. De manière générale, la concurrence médiatique a transformé un mécontentement latent en participation active au conflit. Ces résultats apportent un éclairage sur l’économie des rébellions et des soulèvements.

title: When Trade Raises Fertility: The Role of Women's Labor Market Attachment
affiliations: , Bates College - Department of Economics  and Centro de Investigacion y Docencia Economicas

detail.title: When Trade Raises Fertility: The Role of Women's Labor Market Attachment
detail.abstract: This paper shows import competition can raise fertility when women's market attachment is weak. Across Mexican local labor markets, Chinese import exposure raised birth rates, increased women with children, and reduced singlehood. These effects are driven by exposure in female-intensive industries. Male-intensive exposure generates smaller opposite effects. Female-intensive exposure pushes women out of the labor force, consistent with lower childbearing opportunity costs. Female exposure has strongest effects on female labor force exit and fertility where baseline female labor force participation was lowest. This pattern helps explain why demographic effects were positive in Mexican local labor markets despite negative evidence elsewhere.

title: 0D-2D: The Knower's First Steps Restore -Renew -Resource

detail.title: 0D-2D: The Knower's First Steps Restore -Renew -Resource
detail.abstract:
This paper renews the powers of the Knower and derives the first two spatial dimensions 1D: The Point, and 2D: The Line from the pre-dimensional Conscient Field established in Paper 1 of this series (0D: The Conscient Field, SSRN 6479979). The derivation operates under two governing postulates: Conservation as the sole operative law, and the Founding Axiom attributed to Dr. John R. A. Mayer, that unified conditions seek separation and separated conditions seek unification. Each step is the logical outcome given the prior conditions and postulates.

The Nomad Knower undertakes a four-step preparatory sequence: Restore, Renew, Resource  initiating six quanta of conscient before the first dimension is expressed. The critical architectural asymmetry established in this phase is foundational: Beta alone holds the nested binary relationship of 0 and 1 required for pre-mass design. Delta holds equivalent power without binary. This asymmetry governs every subsequent dimensional step.

1D, The Point, is derived at T.00.00.005 as the minimum necessary proof that something in the neutral field has become other than 0D. 2D, The Line follows at T.00.00.006 through Delta's redeployment in negative polarity, thrusting two Conscients to the extremities of the bounded field. The Temporal Address Principle is introduced: Time as active witness and recorder of ontological identity.

Convergences with Peirce's triadic semiotics, Tononi's Integrated Information Theory, Strømme's pre-Bang consciousness field, Whitehead's primordial nature, Causal Set Theory, and the quantum vacuum are each noted as resonance. The derivation is sequential, cumulative, and recursive. 3D awaits.

title: Algorithmic Pricing When Capacity Turns Over: Competition, Collusion, and Information Sharing
affiliations: Vanderbilt University - Owen Graduate School of Management, Vanderbilt University - Department of Mathematics and USC Gould School of Law

detail.title: Algorithmic Pricing When Capacity Turns Over: Competition, Collusion, and Information Sharing

declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: In markets such as rental housing, self-storage, equipment leasing, and cloud computing, capacity turns over rather than depletes as customers arrive randomly, occupy units for uncertain durations, and eventually leave. Pricing low may fill a unit today but forgoes the option of renting it at a higher price tomorrow. Firms at full capacity drop out of consumers' choice sets, altering substitution patterns in real time. We model this setting as a continuous-time Markov process and compute dynamic equilibria under three regimes: firms price based on their own occupancy, on all firms' occupancies, or to jointly maximize profits. Three results emerge. First, sharing occupancy information intensifies competition, as firms compete in each realized state rather than on average. Second, as occupancy rises, it becomes more difficult to absorb diverted rival demand, so firms become worse substitutes for each other, shrinking the gains to collusion. Third, scale pools demand risk, raising occupancy and lowering prices Together, these findings identify a structural channel through which algorithmic pricing in capacity-constrained markets generates efficiency gains rather than collusive overcharges. Instead of asking whether trigger strategies can sustain supra-competitive prices, we ask the prior question, whether the prize is large enough to justify the antitrust risk. The results yield practical guidance on which pricing algorithm to adopt and what information to feed it.

detail.abstract: Access to property investment at scale in Tanzania has historically been the preserve of wealthy individuals, institutional investors, and large development firms, a function of high capital requirements and the near total absence of accessible investment vehicles for ordinary savers. At the same time, Tanzania possesses a rich and demonstrably functioning tradition of collective financial participation through Savings and Credit Cooperative Societies (SACCOS), Village Community Banks (VICOBA), and community fundraising practices. The cultural infrastructure for pooled investment already exists; what is missing is the formal architecture to channel it into productive assets. This paper employs a qualitative, document-based conceptual policy analysis, combining comparative regulatory analysis of three international jurisdictions with a close examination of Tanzania's cooperative financial ecosystem and an illustrative financial modelling exercise. The study does not claim to produce generalisable empirical findings; its contribution is the development and plausibility evaluation of a regulatory and investment framework. The paper argues that fractional real estate ownership can be institutionally adapted to Tanzania not by importing foreign property finance models wholesale, but by aligning Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)-based crowdfunding structures with the country's existing cooperative savings culture, the 2023 Crowdfunding Guidelines (GN No. 732), and TANAPA's tourism concession framework. A hub-and-spoke trust model distributing investment through established SACCOS institutions is proposed as the mechanism for bridging the gap between relational and institutional trust in emerging markets. An illustrative hospitality development requiring US$5 million, financed through 5,000 investment units at US$1,000 each, anchors the analysis. The paper's principal conclusion is that Tanzania already possesses the regulatory tools necessary for fractional property investment and that implementation requires coordinated administrative action rather than new legislation.

title: Multipolar Currencies in a Fractured World: Scenario Mapping, Monetary Transmission, and Policy Playbooks

detail.title: Multipolar Currencies in a Fractured World: Scenario Mapping, Monetary Transmission, and Policy Playbooks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest to this work
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not contain any studies with human or animal subjects performed by any of the authors.
declarations.funderStatement: The research is not funded.

detail.abstract:
The international monetary system is under mounting strain from geoeconomic fragmentation, repeated sanctions episodes, and accelerating digital innovation, yet the U.S. dollar remains structurally dominant across reserves, trade invoicing, and cross-border finance.
This paper develops a scenario-based, narrative/quantitative hybrid framework to map alternative futures of a multipolar currency order and to assess their implications for monetary policy transmission, global imbalances, and financial stability. 
Drawing on IMF COFER data, the 2025 External Sector Report, and the Federal Reserve's 2025 assessment of dollar international usage, we identify four stylized scenarios for 2026-2040: (1) Sticky Dollar Dominance, (2) Balanced Multipolarity, (3) Fragmented Bloc Multipolarity, and (4) Digital Balkanization. We anchor these narratives in quantitative indicators-including reserve concentrations, indices of currency usage, and FX turnover (especially the renminbi's rising share)-and in a stylized three-bloc DSGE model that links safe-asset provision, trade fragmentation, and equilibrium real interest rates. management tools, and scenario-based stress tests of their external balance sheets. Strategic recommendations include institutionalizing multipolar scenarios in Monetary Policy Reports, deepening regional safety nets and swap lines, and designing CBDCs and cross-border payment systems for interoperability rather than bloc exclusion.
Our anticipated contribution is to provide a tractable, policy-oriented framework that integrates geoeconomics, monetary transmission, and financial architecture design, offering central banks a tool to prepare for-not simply react to-the coming currency order.

title: Monetary Transmission Capacity and Inflation Dynamics in Sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence from Panel Data

detail.title: Monetary Transmission Capacity and Inflation Dynamics in Sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence from Panel Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known financial, personal, or professional relationships that could have influenced the research, analysis, interpretation, or conclusions presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it does not involve human participants, patients, personal data, interviews, surveys, or experimental procedures. The analysis is based on secondary macroeconomic data and publicly available sources.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agency. The study was independently developed by the authors.

detail.abstract: Inflation remains a persistent macroeconomic challenge in Sub-Saharan Africa, where monetary policy transmission is often weakened by shallow financial systems, fiscal dominance, exchangerate pass-through, and limited central bank credibility. This paper examines how monetary and institutional conditions are associated with inflation outcomes across 31 Sub-Saharan African economies between 1995 and 2022. It proposes a Monetary Transmission Capacity Framework, which argues that monetary policy effectiveness depends partly on financial depth and central bank credibility. Using a complete-case panel of 434 country-year observations, the paper estimates fixed-effects models with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors to account for cross-sectional dependence, heteroskedasticity, and serial correlation. The results show that money supply growth and exchange-rate depreciation are positively associated with inflation, while financial depth, central bank independence, and fiscal balance are negatively associated with inflation. A lagged squared inflation term provides evidence consistent with non-linear inflation persistence. The findings suggest that inflation management in Sub-Saharan Africa depends not only on monetary policy stance but also on the structural and institutional capacity through which policy is transmitted. The results should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal estimates, given potential endogeneity between inflation, monetary aggregates, and institutional variables.

title: Impact of Short-Form Video Content on Attention Span and Memory Retention
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, NSB World Business School and NSB World Business School

detail.title: Impact of Short-Form Video Content on Attention Span and Memory Retention
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of short-form video platforms such as Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok has significantly transformed the way individuals consume digital content. These platforms are designed to deliver brief, engaging videos that capture attention quickly, often leading to prolonged usage. While such content provides entertainment and easy access to information, concerns have been raised regarding its potential impact on cognitive functions, particularly attention span and memory retention. This study aims to examine how frequent exposure to short-form video content influences the attention span and memory of users, with a primary focus on students. The research adopts a descriptive design and utilizes a survey-based methodology to collect data from participants regarding their usage patterns, concentration levels, and memory-related experiences. The findings indicate that excessive consumption of reels is associated with reduced attention span and lower levels of memory retention. Participants who spent more time on short-form video platforms reported difficulties in maintaining focus on longer tasks and retaining detailed information. However, moderate usage showed minimal negative effects, suggesting that the impact varies based on consumption habits. The study concludes that while short-form video content offers convenience and engagement, overexposure may lead to cognitive challenges. It highlights the importance of mindful usage and balanced digital habits to minimize potential negative effects on attention and memory.

title: Beyond the Picks and Shovels : Why ASML and TSMC Represent More Durable AI Infrastructure Investments Than Fabless Designers

detail.title: Beyond the Picks and Shovels : Why ASML and TSMC Represent More Durable AI Infrastructure Investments Than Fabless Designers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This author has no financial relationships with ASML, TSMC, NVIDIA or any other company discussed in this paper. The author holds personal investment positions in publicly traded securities including but not limited to QQQ and is a retail investor. This paper represents independent academic research and should not be construed as investment advice.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author without institutional support.

detail.abstract: The AI boom has drawn multiple widespread comparisons between the dot com bubble of the early 2000s, most notably the comparisons between the NVIDIA Corporation and Cisco Systems at the peak of the bubble. Both are dominant infrastructure suppliers priced for sustained perfection. This paper accepts that parallel but advances beyond it, arguing that the most durable investment opportunity in the current semiconductor cycle does not lie with fabless chip designers like NVIDIA or AMD but with the foundational infrastructure layer beneath them : ASML Holding N.V. and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. Using a hierarchical supply chain framework: lithography equipment → fabrication → chip design → end application, we demonstrate that ASML and TSMC derive a competitive advantage from this framework that extends beyond cyclic demand. ASML maintains a de facto global monopoly on extreme ultraviolet (EUV) Lithography machines, without which no advanced semiconductor can be manufactured at scale. TSMC fabricates chips for competing designers simultaneously, making its revenue stream structurally indifferent to which AI architecture wins the market. We compare valuation multiples across NVIDIA, TSMC and ASML against the Cisco 1998-2002 precedent and assess Taiwan specific geopolitical concentration as a key variable. Our findings suggest that investors seeking long-term AI Infrastructure exposure would be better served by the foundational layer than by current market sentiment.

title: Regulatory Asymmetry and the Protective Reconstruction of Liability: A Proportionality-Based Framework for Governing Third-Party AI Fine-Tuning

detail.title: Regulatory Asymmetry and the Protective Reconstruction of Liability: A Proportionality-Based Framework for Governing Third-Party AI Fine-Tuning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency

detail.abstract:
This paper examines a structural weakness in emerging AI governance: the disproportionate compliance burden placed on small and medium‑sized enterprises (SMEs) when liability frameworks are applied uniformly to all third‑party fine‑tuning actors. As the AI supply chain evolves from a developer‑user dyad to a tripartite structure—foundation model developers, third‑party fine‑tuners, and downstream deployers—traditional liability models no longer reflect the actual distribution of functional control. The concept of “capability reconfiguration liability” correctly identifies fine‑tuning as a transformative act that alters a model’s behavioral boundaries, but its uniform application produces fixed compliance costs that SMEs cannot absorb.
The paper argues that these burdens function as structural displacement pressures. First, they create cost displacement: dynamic duties of care—risk auditing, data governance, monitoring, and documentation—become fixed expenditures that crowd out R&D budgets and reduce SMEs’ capacity for iterative experimentation. Second, they generate behavioral distortion: SMEs increasingly rely on large platforms for “compliance shelter,” a rational adaptation that nonetheless concentrates innovation capacity and erodes the sectoral diversity that SMEs sustain. The result is a de facto market‑selection mechanism that filters actors by resource endurance rather than risk behavior.
To address this asymmetry, the paper grounds its argument in the proportionality principle, which requires that liability intensity track risk level, harm potential, and realistic compliance capacity. Proportionality does not exempt SMEs from high‑risk obligations; rather, it prevents the imposition of high‑risk governance burdens on low‑risk, controlled deployments. SME fine‑tuning typically involves narrow application domains, limited user populations, and contained harm scenarios—conditions that justify differentiated obligations without compromising safety.
A comparative analysis of the EU, United States, and China shows that differentiated governance is already emerging. The EU AI Act employs risk‑tiered obligations and regulatory sandboxes; the United States offers flexibility through voluntary frameworks but suffers from regulatory fragmentation; China combines resource subsidies with mandatory registration and ethics review, though without explicit linkage between support and liability mitigation.
Building on these insights, the paper proposes a tiered liability architecture incorporating layered duty structures, application‑side regulatory thresholds, graduated compliance transitions, and safe harbor provisions for SMEs that satisfy baseline requirements. It further argues for public compliance infrastructure—shared audit pools, standardized templates, and subsidized ethics review—to shift compliance from an individual burden to a shared institutional service.

The central claim is that protecting SMEs from structural compliance penalties is not regulatory leniency but a requirement of liability legitimacy. Responsibility must track risk, not organizational capacity, if innovation diversity and meaningful governance are to be preserved.

title: US–China Relations: Managed Competition as a Systemic Regime

detail.title: US–China Relations: Managed Competition as a Systemic Regime

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the United States' strategy towards China as a model of managed competition functioning as the baseline regime organising bilateral relations. Unlike other strategic directions, US-China interaction has acquired a relatively institutionalised character, allowing it to be interpreted as an institutionalised systemic regime. Within this model, competition is not a temporary phase but a permanent operational logic structuring interaction between states without escalation into open conflict. The system is shown to operate through the combination of three key components: institutionalised red lines, systemic competition, and conditional cooperation. Particular attention is given to the role of security-based containment and its instruments of implementation. It is concluded that US strategy towards China constitutes an institutionalised system of managed competition that ensures stability through balance management and the prevention of forceful revision, rather than through the elimination of rivalry itself.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ROI: A MEASUREMENT FRAMEWORK FOR ENTERPRISES

detail.title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ROI: A MEASUREMENT FRAMEWORK FOR ENTERPRISES
detail.abstract:
Digital transformation has become the defining strategic imperative for enterprises worldwide, with global spending projected to reach $3.9 trillion by 2027 (IDC, 2024). Yet despite massive investments, a persistent and troubling disconnect exists between digital transformation expenditure and measurable business value. Research indicates that 70% of digital transformation initiatives fail to achieve their stated objectives (McKinsey, 2023), and only 30% of organizations can quantify the ROI of their digital investments (Gartner, 2024). This "ROI measurement gap" represents one of the most significant challenges facing enterprise leaders, technology strategists, and academic researchers today  undermining investment confidence, misallocating resources, and obscuring the true value of digital innovation.


This white paper addresses this critical gap by introducing the DRIVE (Digital Return on Investment and Value for Enterprises) Framework, a comprehensive, multi-dimensional measurement architecture designed to quantify the full spectrum of value generated by digital transformation programs, with particular emphasis on AI-enabled transformation. The DRIVE Framework moves beyond traditional financial ROI metrics to encompass seven interconnected value dimensions: (1) Financial Value, (2) Operational Value, (3) Customer Value, (4) Innovation Value, (5) Strategic Value, (6) Human Capital Value, and (7) Social and Sustainability Value. Each dimension includes specific, measurable KPIs, calculation methodologies, and industry benchmarks.


The paper synthesizes research from 65+ academic and industry sources, analyzes digital transformation landscapes across the United States, European Union, and India, and presents six industry case studies spanning education technology, healthcare, retail and e-commerce, manufacturing, e-government, and IT services. A five-level DT ROI Maturity Model enables organizations to assess their measurement capabilities and chart improvement pathways.


Key findings demonstrate that organizations employing structured, multi-dimensional ROI measurement frameworks achieve 2.5x higher returns on digital transformation investments compared to those using ad-hoc or purely financial measurement approaches. Case studies reveal ROI ranging from 150% to 380% across industries when AI-enabled transformation is measured comprehensively, with documented outcomes including 35% cost reduction, 40% operational efficiency improvement, and significant stakeholder value creation.


This research contributes to both academic discourse on digital transformation value and industry practice by providing a validated, implementable measurement framework serving as a foundation for enterprise DT investment strategy and governance.

title: Selection Matters: Lessons from Two Decades of Immigrant Earnings
affiliations: University of Waterloo and University of Waterloo

detail.title: Selection Matters: Lessons from Two Decades of Immigrant Earnings
detail.abstract:
• This Commentary examines relative employment rates and hourly earnings of Canadian immigrants and non-permanent residents (NPRs) from 2005 to 2024, with particular attention to changes following the introduction of Express Entry in 2015 and the subsequent unprecedented rise in immigration levels.
  • Despite significantly higher intake levels after 2015, the labour market performance of new permanent residents improved. The gains are concentrated among university-educated immigrants, especially men, and are most consistent with the effects of Express Entry, which replaced a first-come, first-served system with one that prioritizes applicants with the highest expected earnings. Recent male cohorts appear on track to reach earnings parity with Canadian-born workers within five years of landing.
  • Nonetheless, the results also point to a sharp deterioration in the average hourly earnings of non-permanent resident men in 2020-2024, particularly among college-educated men. Policies that prioritize this population for permanent residency in the years ahead risk undermining the gains of the past decade.
  • To avoid this, the government should return to relying exclusively on the Comprehensive Ranking System for economic-class immigrant selection.

title: Fiscal Fantasy: Believe It or Not, Fiscal Reality Hasn’t Gone Away
affiliations: Queen's University, C.D. Howe Institute and C.D. Howe Institute

detail.title: Fiscal Fantasy: Believe It or Not, Fiscal Reality Hasn’t Gone Away
detail.abstract:
• Canada can no longer pride itself on its fiscal discipline. With the economy operating near capacity and growth in productive capacity weak, governments continue to run deficits and project rising debt ratios, undermining growth and living standards rather than supporting them.
  • Government projections understate the risks. Weak productivity, low business investment, and demographic pressures will hold back growth and revenues, while ageing, healthcare, and defence will push spending higher. Even modest changes in growth or interest rates could materially worsen the fiscal picture.
  • Restoring discipline will take a real change in direction. Governments must rein in spending, set a credible path to balance, and pursue reforms that boost investment and productivity, including shifting the tax mix away from income towards less distortionary taxes. The federal government must lead the way in its upcoming Spring Economic Update.

title: The Peer Review Paradox: How Scholarly Gatekeeping Systematically Excludes Paradigm-Shifting Research

detail.title: The Peer Review Paradox: How Scholarly Gatekeeping Systematically Excludes Paradigm-Shifting Research
detail.abstract:
1. Abstract

Contemporary peer review optimizes for disciplinary consensus rather than epistemic advancement, producing systematic Type II errors against high-novelty research.

 This paper documents structural patterns in scholarly gatekeeping using five historical cases where research initially rejected by journals subsequently received Nobel recognition.

 Analysis suggests peer review functions as a career filter rather than knowledge filter, exhibiting principal-agent problems, in-group preference, and diffusion of accountability. We do not advocate abolition of peer review but identify measurable costs of current implementation.

 Preprint mechanisms and post-publication review represent partial corrective measures. The historical record indicates these are not anomalies but structural features of institutional knowledge validation. [1]

title: Getting it Right -Lessons Learned from Regulating Limited Investment Advice

detail.title: Getting it Right -Lessons Learned from Regulating Limited Investment Advice
detail.abstract:
• Canada has outperformed many OECD peers in providing widespread, affordable access to limited investment advice for modest investors.
  • This success reflects a distinctive regulatory framework, most importantly a system of front-line self-regulation, alongside tailored mutual fund dealer rules and flexible compensation structures that have kept advice accessible at low cost.
  • Access to advice has delivered measurable benefits, with advised investors accumulating greater wealth and demonstrating more disciplined financial behaviour, though access for smaller accounts is increasingly under pressure.
  • This paper draws important lessons for policymakers: preserve effective self-regulatory approaches, place greater emphasis on competition and efficiency, carefully assess foreign reforms before adopting them, and apply these insights to other sectors like insurance.

title: Land Protection, Credit Access, and the Insurance Gap

detail.title: Land Protection, Credit Access, and the Insurance Gap
detail.abstract: Bolivia's Ley 1720 (April 2026) allows smallholders to voluntarily convert constitutionally protected pequeña propiedad ---land that cannot be seized by creditors---into pledgeable mediana propiedad, explicitly targeting the credit-access channel that Hernando de Soto popularized. This paper develops a dynamic model showing that such conversion creates a \emph{De Soto trap}: the households most likely to convert are those most desperate for liquidity, not those best positioned to benefit from credit, and these households face the highest default probability. Without complementary insurance, land flows irreversibly from vulnerable smallholders to those with capital to purchase foreclosed properties. The model yields three results: (i) adverse selection into conversion emerges endogenously from the threshold conditions; (ii) aggregate smallholder land decays exponentially toward zero---a ratchet that cannot reverse without policy intervention; (iii) mandatory insurance as a conversion requirement filters out non-viable applicants, bounds land loss, and raises net welfare by a factor of four. Calibrated to Bolivian agricultural census data, the model predicts that under current policy, 120,000 households will lose their land within 25 years. The law addresses the channel (credit) for which empirical evidence is weakest while removing a protection (implicit insurance through inalienability) whose value the risk literature suggests is large. Bolivia's reform inverts the optimal policy sequence.

title: Pocket Sales in the Housing Market: Selection, Outcomes, and Policy
affiliations: University of Georgia - Department of Insurance, Legal Studies, Real Estate

detail.title: Pocket Sales in the Housing Market: Selection, Outcomes, and Policy
detail.abstract: We investigate pocket sales-residential transactions negotiated privately and recorded in the Multiple Listing Service with zero days on market. Contrary to search-theoretic models where limited exposure necessitates a discount, we document a robust 1.7 percent price premium. The evidence is inconsistent with agency conflict explanations; the premium arises from avoiding the open-market negotiation tax. By immunizing sellers against the signal trap of public price adjustments, pocket sales achieve a sale/original list surplus of 1.6 percent. The premium is convex in asset complexity, quadrupling for luxury properties, and market-condition-dependent: it compresses toward zero in hot markets where competitive bidding has already eliminated the open-market negotiation discount, and expands to approximately 3.5 percent in cold markets where that discount is deepest. We exploit the May 2020 implementation of the Clear Cooperation Policy (CCP) as a regulatory shock to the private search window. By compressing the private matching window to a single business day, the CCP reduced the pocket premium by more than 70 percent to a level that is economically negligible and statistically indistinguishable from zero, while pocket sale volume showed no statistically significant decline. The policy eroded the pricing power of private placement without eliminating the practice.

title: Copper, Quietude, and the Kwacha: Reframing Peripheral Sovereignty in a Post-Hegemonic Order

detail.title: Copper, Quietude, and the Kwacha: Reframing Peripheral Sovereignty in a Post-Hegemonic Order
detail.abstract: This article advances a doctrinal and empirically grounded reassessment of Zambia’s position in international economic law. It argues that Zambia represents a distinct model of sovereign development characterised by mineral centrality, legal pluralism, macroeconomic recalibration, and enduring peace. Integrating international case law, domestic statutory frameworks, and macroeconomic datasets, the article contends that Zambia’s developmental trajectory—though historically constrained by asymmetrical external engagements—now reflects increasing structural autonomy. It concludes that Zambia’s governance architecture and sustainability orientation position it as a normative outlier capable of informing a post-hegemonic global order.

title: Sustainable valorization of lithium mine tailings into lightweight foamed ceramics driven by synergistic pore-forming mechanisms
