title: Cumulative Difference Adjustment Tax (CDAT) : A Design Hypothesis for Consumption Taxation Based on Real-Time Management of Cumulative Differences

detail.title: Cumulative Difference Adjustment Tax (CDAT) : A Design Hypothesis for Consumption Taxation Based on Real-Time Management of Cumulative Differences
detail.abstract: This paper proposes the Cumulative Difference Adjustment Tax (CDAT) as a design hypothesis that preserves the core principles of the Value Added Tax (VAT)—the suppression of cascading and the taxation of final consumption—while seeking to mitigate its operational burdens. While the current VAT is a highly developed system, it carries structural challenges, including the temporary holding of tax by businesses, refund delays, fraudulent refunds, and the administrative burden of filing and review. CDAT addresses these burdens by recording the tax portion directly in a Treasury Clearing Account without passing through the seller, by continuously managing each business’s cumulative difference, and by embedding automatic offsetting as the standard process and immediate settlement as an optional operation at the business’s discretion. The paper compares CDAT with related systems and reforms, examines tax revenue equivalence under a simplified closed model, analyzes specific cases including capital investment, exports, mid-course exit, long-term transactions, and B2C transactions, and considers technical implementation with a distributed ledger as the standard implementation model. In conclusion, CDAT is presented not as an immediate replacement for the current VAT but as a verifiable design hypothesis that, under explicitly stated assumptions, may achieve equivalent cumulative tax revenue outcomes. The further refinement of fraud detection mechanisms, the specification of transition paths, the legal examination of international consistency, and the quantitative analysis of economic impact remain subjects for future research.

title: Inflation Dynamics and Impact of Demand and Supply Shocks: Evidence from India.
affiliations: Ghani Khan Choudhury Institute of Engineering & Technology

detail.title: Inflation Dynamics and Impact of Demand and Supply Shocks: Evidence from India.
detail.abstract: This present article tries to comprehend the dynamics of inflation with respect to both core and headline measures of inflation. To understand the dynamic movement in both the measures of inflation, first core inflation is calculated using the traditional exclusion measure (excluding food and energy), and statistical measure using the trimmed mean approach by considering monthly Combined Consumer Price Index (CPI) yoy cross-sectors headline distribution of data from January 2012 and December 2018. Next, a comparative study is attempted to know the reaction of both core and headline inflation measures to different demand and supply shocks by the Structural Vector Autoregressive Techniques. Based on empirical analysis, it is proved that 20 per cent trimming of the extremely volatile components from the headline inflation can be considered as a better proxy for core inflation series

title: MÉTODOS MATEMÁTICOS KASIAN DE DEPRECIACIÓN DE ACTIVOS TANGIBLES

detail.title: MÉTODOS MATEMÁTICOS KASIAN DE DEPRECIACIÓN DE ACTIVOS TANGIBLES
detail.abstract:
La valuación de activos tangibles enfrenta una limitación estructural derivada de la incorporación de componentes subjetivos en la estimación de la depreciación, lo que compromete la consistencia y reproducibilidad de los resultados. Este trabajo plantea una transición hacia la modelación cuantitativa mediante la formulación de métodos matemáticos que representen con mayor precisión el comportamiento funcional de la pérdida de valor.

Se desarrollan cuatro métodos originales de depreciación —Kasian Geométrico, Kasian Logarítmico, Kasian Logarítmico Normalizado y Kasian-Fibonacci— construidos a partir de progresiones geométricas, funciones logarítmicas y la serie de Fibonacci, con el propósito de capturar patrones matemáticos inherentes al proceso de depreciación. La investigación se fundamenta en un análisis crítico de métodos tradicionales, como línea recta, Kuentzle y Ross-Heidecke, identificando debilidades en su fundamentación teórica y en la ponderación subjetiva del estado de conservación.

Los resultados muestran que los métodos propuestos mejoran la coherencia matemática y la estabilidad de las trayectorias de depreciación. En particular, el método Kasian Geométrico destaca por su equilibrio entre sensibilidad y estabilidad, su consistencia con los principios de capitalización del enfoque de ingresos y su viabilidad de implementación operativa. Asimismo, la reformulación del modelo que prescinde del valor residual como variable incierta contribuye a reducir la variabilidad en la estimación.

Se concluye que esta propuesta constituye una contribución metodológica relevante para el campo de la valuación, al establecer una base formal para la modelación matemática de la depreciación. Su adopción abre una línea de investigación orientada a su validación empírica y a su integración en sistemas computacionales, incluyendo herramientas basadas en inteligencia artificial, con potencial para elevar los estándares de objetividad, eficiencia y estandarización en la práctica valuatoria.

title:
Pass-First-Pay-Later

A Structural and Comparative Analysis of the Deferred-Fee Prop Trading Model

detail.title:
Pass-First-Pay-Later

A Structural and Comparative Analysis of the Deferred-Fee Prop Trading Model
detail.abstract:
Pass-First-Pay-Later (PFPL) is a deferred-fee evaluation structure in which the trader pays a nominal access fee to begin a one-phase challenge and settles the remaining evaluation fee only after passing. Adoption has accelerated through 2025–2026: at least ten mid-tier prop firms now operate an active PFPL track, and industry commentary characterises the model as a 2026 industry standard. This paper benchmarks AIProp's PFPL product against nine competitor programmes across four dimensions: access-fee affordability for new traders, professional-grade infrastructure including analytics, training, and AI-assisted decision support, total commitment and rule surface, and affiliate programme economics including commission tier structure and multi-tier override architecture.

AIProp's access fee of $19–$199 represents 0.02–0.19% of the funded capital at each tier, placing every AIProp PFPL account within the low-barrier band on a capital-normalised basis, though the absolute fee is 2.1–19× higher than the lowest-cost competitor at the $10K entry tier. AIProp's total commitment of $1,388 at the $100K tier is 3.6–5.7× above the PFPL competitor field; AIProp is the most expensive PFPL product in the $10K–$100K band and the only PFPL product available at the $200K–$1M capital tier.

On infrastructure, AIProp's weighted score of 9.05 (across execution, analytics, and behavioural tool layers) leads the PFPL benchmark field by 47–53%. The advantage is concentrated in the behavioural layer: AI Coach, AI Journal, live Behavioral Bias Index and Risk Adherence Index dashboard metrics, and blockchain-verified payout publication have no equivalent among PFPL-active competitors. On affiliate economics, AIProp's 15% entry commission is 1.9–3.0× the nearest competitor's entry rate; its three-tier override architecture (10% Tier 2, 5% Tier 3) is structurally unique in the benchmark set. A sensitivity analysis places AIProp's year-1 affiliate earnings at $50K referral volume 54–131% above the field average.

AIProp's weighted competitive scorecard total of 8.25 leads the field by 31–44% over the next-highest competitor (Goat Funded Trader at 6.25), driven by infrastructure (30% weight) and affiliate economics (20% weight). AIProp trails the field on affordability (6/10 vs 8–9/10 for lower-cost entrants). Four areas where AIProp does not lead are explicitly documented: access fee level, total commitment in the $10K–$100K band, operating history and cumulative payout volume, and the absence of independent third-party validation of AI feature claims. Strategic implications are drawn across positioning, pricing, go-to-market, affiliate strategy, and a prioritised evidence-building roadmap.

title: Paxpacte: Reclassifying Value and Restructuring Housing Systems

detail.title: Paxpacte: Reclassifying Value and Restructuring Housing Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it did not involve human participants, patient data, or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Contemporary housing systems are typically evaluated through price dynamics, affordability indicators, and supply constraints. However, a growing body of research suggests that these systems exhibit persistent structural distortions that cannot be fully explained within conventional frameworks. Housing prices increasingly reflect financial conditions, spatial concentration, and capitalized expectations rather than functional provision. As a result, price signals fail to distinguish between fundamentally different forms of value embedded within housing systems. This paper argues that the core issue underlying these distortions is not merely market imbalance, but a misclassification of value. Housing systems collapse distinct forms of value-including functional, socially produced, and capitalized value-into a single price signal, thereby obscuring their differences and enabling structurally divergent processes to be interpreted as equivalent. Drawing on contemporary developments in value theory, urban political economy, and economic geography, this paper introduces Paxpacte as a framework for reclassifying housing value. The framework does not reject markets, but seeks to reinterpret price as a composite signal that requires decomposition. By distinguishing between different forms of value, Paxpacte provides a basis for understanding how housing systems transform, redistribute, and obscure value across economic and spatial dimensions. The paper contributes by extending modern value theory into the domain of housing systems and by offering a conceptual foundation for analyzing housing beyond price-based metrics.

reference: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1532
title: Overconfident forecasters and the impact of inflation information: evidence from a randomized survey experiment

detail.title: Overconfident forecasters and the impact of inflation information: evidence from a randomized survey experiment

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1532
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We exploit a randomized information intervention in a quarterly survey of Italian firms to study how access to recent inflation data affects deviations from the full-information rational expectations (FIRE) benchmark in managers’ inflation forecasts. Treated firms receive the latest inflation reading before submitting their forecasts and, relative to non-treated firms, display less underreaction at the consensus level and less overreaction at the individual level, moving forecasts closer to the FIRE benchmark. A model that combines noisy information with overconfidence in private information provides the best overall fit to the data, outperforming alternative frameworks featuring diagnostic expectations, internal cognitive constraints, or over-extrapolation. Intuitively, with noisy information, average forecasts react sluggishly to news, so an informative public signal speeds up aggregate updating and reduces consensus underreaction. With overconfidence, managers overweight private signals and the public signal shifts weight away from private information, attenuating individual overreaction.

title: Dual-Chokepoint Crisis in the Red Sea

detail.title: Dual-Chokepoint Crisis in the Red Sea
detail.abstract: This analysis examines the emergence of a dual-chokepoint constraint in global trade and energy systems driven by simultaneous disruption at the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb in the Red Sea. With the Strait of Hormuz already under sustained pressure from the ongoing war in Iran, Houthi activation of maritime strike capability in the Red Sea risks extending disruption into a second critical corridor, linking both into a single, increasingly integrated operational system. The paper maps the structural mechanics through which localized maritime disruption generates outsized systemic effects: the Red Sea-Suez axis carries approximately 12 percent of global trade and nearly 30 percent of container traffic, while Bab el-Mandeb handles between six and seven million barrels of oil per day, concentrating systemic exposure within a narrow geographic corridor. The analysis traces three escalation phases-from initial market adjustment and rerouting, through interactive dual-corridor pressure, to a third phase of dual-chokepoint constraint in which rerouting capacity, insurance markets, and defensive systems are simultaneously stretched beyond their ability to absorb disruption. The paper further assesses how Houthi maritime capability functions as a scalable extension of Iran's broader escalation framework, enabling controlled disruption to be activated, sustained, or intensified in calibration with developments across other theaters. It concludes that system normalization in global logistics and energy distribution may only become possible within a broader de-escalation framework for the Iran conflict, as persistent dual-chokepoint pressure fundamentally alters the cost, reliability, and risk profile of global maritime trade.

title: Systematic backtesting of Probability of Default Models with regulatory data
affiliations: European Banking Authority, European Banking Authority, European Banking Authority and European Banking Authority

detail.title: Systematic backtesting of Probability of Default Models with regulatory data
detail.abstract: Internal ratings-based models play a central role in bank risk man-agement and regulatory capital determination, yet their validation remains methodologically challenging and operationally resource-intensive. In this paper, we contribute to the quantitative valida-tion of probability of default models through a systematic backtesting exercise using a new proprietary dataset collected by the European Banking Authority between 2017 and 2024. We propose a generalised correction to the canonical binomial test that simultaneously accounts for both asset and serial correlation and is supported by extensive simulations. Acknowledging the it-erative nature of model validation, we use order statistics to iden-tify persistent miscalibrations over time. We present an approach to aggregate the results of backtesting procedures, which are typ-ically designed for bank-level evaluation, whereas our focus is to provide evidence on the performance of the models across EU banks. Empirically, we find that the share of miscalibrated expo-sures of the small and medium-sized enterprises corporates asset class ranges from around 3.0% under realistic assumptions to a conservative upper bound of 16.7% implied by the canonical bi-nomial test. We also quantify the impact on capital requirements and show that prudent model re-calibrations would reduce sys-tem-wide Tier 1 capital ratios by 4 to 10 basis points. By offering scalable backtesting tools and enhancing transparency, we sup-port more effective supervisory oversight and contribute to re-storing market confidence in internal models.

reference: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1533
title: Deposit funding, market power and monetary policy transmission
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Banca d'Italia and Bocconi University

detail.title: Deposit funding, market power and monetary policy transmission

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1533
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of banks’ deposit funding and deposit market power as potential drivers of the intensity of the pass-through from monetary policy to bank funding costs and broader financing conditions. We document that during the ECB’s unprecedentedly forceful monetary tightening cycle in 2022–23, the pass-through from policy rates to overnight deposit rates was extremely muted compared with historical regularities, highlighting a disconnect in monetary policy transmission. Using confidential bank-level data, state-dependent panel local projections and high-frequency monetary policy shocks, we find that higher deposit funding is associated with a lower pass-through to overnight deposit rates, mainly in the short term. The dampening effect of deposit market power is more persistent and extends to lending rates for households and non-financial corporations.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1007
title: A composite indicator of systemic risk related to the Italian financial cycle

detail.title: A composite indicator of systemic risk related to the Italian financial cycle

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1007
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Financial cycles, i.e. the boom-bust dynamics that characterize modern decentralized economies, are a key driver of financial crises and subsequent economic downturns. Countercyclical macroprudential policy aims to mitigate these risks by strengthening the resilience of the financial system during the expansionary phases, mostly using the countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) as an instrument. While the credit-to-GDP gap is the standard reference guide used for calibrating the CCyB, its limitations in capturing the full spectrum of financial cycle dynamics have become increasingly apparent. A growing number of macroprudential authorities are supplementing the credit gap with additional indicators to inform CCyB rate decisions, placing increasing emphasis on composite indicators of the financial cycle. This paper proposes a composite indicator of systemic risk related to the Italian financial cycle (Cyclical Risk Indicator, CRI). The CRI is constructed as a weighted average of the best performing financial cycle indicators, offering a comprehensive assessment of systemic cyclical risk. Empirical analysis shows that the CRI provides additional information for the early warning of financial distress and of tail macroeconomic outcomes relative to the credit gap. By adopting the CRI, the Italian macroprudential authority may gain a more nuanced understanding of financial cycle dynamics, enabling more informed and timely policy decisions. This, in turn, would lead to a more resilient financial system and mitigate the impact of future financial crises.

title: Profitability and Prudence in Practice: Measuring Efficiency in Saudi Islamic and Conventional Banks using DEA and Tobit Regression
affiliations: Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) - Department of Commerce and Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Profitability and Prudence in Practice: Measuring Efficiency in Saudi Islamic and Conventional Banks using DEA and Tobit Regression
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the efficiency of Islamic and conventional banks in Saudi Arabia from 2017-2024 using a two-stage DEA-Tobit framework. DEA results show that conventional banks consistently outperform Islamic banks in technical and scale efficiency, while Islamic banks achieve perfect managerial efficiency under variable returns to scale. Tobit findings reveal that capital adequacy significantly enhances efficiency in Islamic banks, whereas profitability exerts a negative effect. For conventional banks, profitability remains insignificant. Overall, the results underscore the central role of scale optimisation and prudential strength in shaping efficiency outcomes within Saudi Arabia's dual banking system.

title: The Prompt is the Analytic Choice: Specification Curve Analysis for LLM-based Social Science

detail.title: The Prompt is the Analytic Choice: Specification Curve Analysis for LLM-based Social Science
detail.abstract: When researchers use large language models as synthetic survey respondents, the prompt is an analytic choice-subject to the same undisclosed researcher degrees of freedom that drove the replication crisis in psychology and economics. We introduce Prompt Specification Curve Analysis (P-SCA): a framework that maps conclusions across the full space of defensible prompt designs and decomposes outcome variance by dimension. We instantiate P-SCA on a 1,728-cell multiverse of model, persona format, question framing, system prompt, temperature, and few-shot count, sampling 600 specifications via Latin Hypercube Sampling and administering each to 20 demographic profiles on three ANES opinion items (160,035 responses). The partisan signal is genuine and survives the multiverse (p < 0.0001; 83-95% directional consistency), but its sensitivity structure is topic-contingent in ways uniform robustness checks cannot detect: question framing dominates for gun control (η 2 = 0.160, CI [0.131, 0.192]) while model choice dominates for immigration and government spending. Two model-framing combinations drive nearly all instability-Llama 3.3 70B with Likert framing inverts the partisan gap entirely (∆ =-1.92)-while frontier models are order-invariant. For well-posed items, LLM partisan gaps exceed ANES 2024 ground truth by 1.71-2.17× with both poles inflated symmetrically; gun control compresses under the LLM median due to framing-driven inversions pulling the distribution toward zero. We propose a three-element Prompt Specification Reporting Standard and release an open-source toolkit at https://github.com/YCRG-Labs/psca

title: The U.S. Credibility Gap Across Theaters

detail.title: The U.S. Credibility Gap Across Theaters
detail.abstract: This analysis examines the structural nature of the United States credibility gap across three simultaneous theaters of strategic engagement: Iran, Ukraine, and the Indo-Pacific. The central argument is that the United States does not face a deficit of military power but a growing inability to convert that superiority into durable political outcomes. Across each theater, a distinct variant of this problem is visible. In Iran, tactical military success does not translate into stable post-conflict order when adversaries retain asymmetric instruments of cost-imposition. In Ukraine, substantial and sustained material support erodes in strategic effect when it is not anchored to a credible theory of war termination. In the Indo-Pacific, deterrence against China depends not only on the forward disposition of American forces but on whether allied capitals in Tokyo, Seoul, and Taipei read U.S. conduct elsewhere as strategically coherent. The paper further assesses four plausible strategic scenarios-controlled coherence, tactical competence without integration, attritional erosion, and managed disengagement-and evaluates the conditions under which each is likely to obtain. It concludes that the most probable near-term trajectory is tactical competence without strategic integration: an environment in which American military effectiveness remains real but insufficiently embedded in a coherent framework of priorities, limits, and political conversion. The analysis argues that credibility is ultimately determined not by the existence of power but by whether that power operates within a recognizable logic-and that without clearer definition of vital interests, political end-states, and burden-sharing arrangements, strategic flexibility risks becoming indistinguishable from reactive policymaking.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1008
title: Bounds for timely estimates of average household income
affiliations: Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: Bounds for timely estimates of average household income

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1008
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a novel set identification approach to produce timely estimates of average household income that are robust to the sample selection bias driven by item non-response, which may affect surveys. Our method covers a large number of practical situations and considers several, increasingly restrictive assumptions. Extensions to other functionals beyond average income are possible. As a practical example, we use data from Banca d’Italia’s Household Outlook Survey. Starting from wide nonparametric bounds based solely on brackets, we progressively narrow the identified set by exploiting additional information: unfolding brackets, exact income responses, and monotonicity assumptions leveraging the panel and cross-sectional dimensions of the data. Our method identifies bounds that contain the official EU-SILC estimate of average Italian household income and are available almost one year earlier than the EU-SILC release. The economically plausible assumptions we impose narrow the initial bounds by 25%. The method is simple, transparent, and broadly applicable to other contexts where timely, unbiased income measures are needed.

reference: MPI Behavioral Economics Discussion Paper No. 2026/5
title: Ein verhaltensökonomischer Blick auf Gehaltsunterschiede zwischen Frauen und Männern
affiliations: Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Economics

detail.title: Ein verhaltensökonomischer Blick auf Gehaltsunterschiede zwischen Frauen und Männern

publicationDetails.detailsText: MPI Behavioral Economics Discussion Paper No. 2026/5
publicationDetails.journalName: Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Economics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Frauen verdienen im Schnitt nach wie vor weniger als Männer. Obwohl in den vergangenen Jahrzehnten große Fortschritte in der Gleichstellung von Männern und Frauen gemacht wurden, gibt es immer noch Ungleichheiten. Matthias Sutter wirft einen verhaltensökonomischen Blick auf mögliche Ursachen für die ungleichen Gehälter von Männern und Frauen. Dabei konzentriert er sich auf Geschlechterunterschiede im Wettbewerbsverhalten, im Verhandlungsverhalten und in der Wahl, in welchen Branchen jemand arbeiten möchte. All diese Faktoren können einen wichtigen Teil der Gehaltsunterschiede zwischen Männern und Frauen erklären, entziehen sich aber einfachen politischen (bzw. gesetzlichen) Interventionen. Abschließend wird auch die Bedeutung von Kindern für Gehaltsunterschiede zwischen den Geschlechtern diskutiert.

title: Iran Operation Raises Stakes For North Korea

detail.title: Iran Operation Raises Stakes For North Korea
detail.abstract: This analysis examines the strategic implications of the joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran for North Korea's nuclear posture, alliance calculations, and the prospects for denuclearization on the Korean Peninsula. The central argument is that the Iran operation has functioned as a powerful validating signal for Pyongyang's nuclear maximalism: by demonstrating that a state subjected to sustained international pressure and lacking a credible nuclear deterrent remained vulnerable to preemptive military action, the campaign has reinforced Kim Jong Un's conviction that nuclear saturation-not diplomatic engagement-is the only reliable guarantee of regime survival. The paper traces three interconnected effects. First, the operation accelerates North Korea's existing trajectory toward expanded and survivable nuclear capabilities, including solid-fuel ICBM development designed to make preemptive counterforce strikes mathematically implausible. Second, it deepens Pyongyang's alignment with Beijing and Moscow, consolidating a trilateral security architecture in which China's strategic interest in buffer-state preservation and Russia's post-Ukraine isolation intersect to provide North Korea with a permissive environment for continued proliferation. Third, the operation eliminates the residual trust and political conditions necessary for meaningful denuclearization negotiations, reinforcing the JCPOA's failure as a cautionary precedent and hardening Pyongyang's demand for de facto recognition as a nuclear state. The analysis concludes by presenting two plausible scenarios: stabilized confrontation within a deepened bloc structure, and a miscalculation-driven escalation that breaks the stalemate through crisis rather than diplomacy. In both, the Iran operation's proliferation paradox is central: a campaign designed to prevent nuclear weapons acquisition in one region may have structurally accelerated it in another.

title: Differential Measurement of Proxy Discrimination
affiliations: City St George's, University of London, Bayes Business School (formerly Cass), City, University of London and University of London

detail.title: Differential Measurement of Proxy Discrimination
detail.abstract: Excluding protected attributes from insurance pricing models does not guarantee the absence of discrimination, as remaining covariates may still act as proxies. This paper develops a differential framework for measuring proxy discrimination in fitted pricing models. The approach decomposes the sensitivity of prices to a covariate into components reflecting the direct impact on predictions and the proxying of a protected attribute. In applications with predominantly categorical features, we use Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) to obtain a continuous latent representation that supports differential sensitivity analysis. In that setting, we decompose discrete price changes due to policyholder profile perturbations into direct and proxy effects, using Aumann-Shapley attributions. Two empirical illustrations on insurance claims datasets reveal weak but detectable proxy effects related to gender. The proposed approach provides a diagnostic framework for assessing the presence and magnitude of proxy-discriminatory effects at both the individual and portfolio level, which is applicable to differentiable pricing models, without requiring model refitting.

title: Financing Fragility and the Valuation of Platform Growth: Evidence from Fintech Firms
affiliations: University of Exeter and University of Salford

detail.title: Financing Fragility and the Valuation of Platform Growth: Evidence from Fintech Firms

publicationDetails.journalName: Finance, Economics & Banking (FEB-RN) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We document that firm information-processing architecture is associated with a persistent enterprise-value premium for algorithmic (hard-information) fintech firms relative to relationship-based intermediaries. This premium holds across thirteen consecutive years and is robust to standard firm characteristics, including size, profitability, leverage, and sustainability performance. We argue that hard-information intermediaries better scale network effects through algorithmically processable data, enabling more effective translation of user growth into enterprise value under varying financing conditions. To examine this mechanism, we employ a diagnostic proxy capturing the interaction between platform growth, sustainability alignment, and capital stability. The results indicate that financing fragility weakens the growth-to-value relationship, consistent with investor discounting of growth signals under unstable financing conditions. Sustainability performance amplifies valuation efficiency at moderate growth levels but exhibits diminishing marginal effects at higher levels. Additional evidence suggests that data-intensive investment reduces short-term valuation efficiency but supports longer-term platform scalability.

title: Understanding Firms' AI Efforts and Their Economic Impact

detail.title: Understanding Firms' AI Efforts and Their Economic Impact

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
This paper reviews firm-level data on artificial intelligence and the emerging evidence on AI's economic effects. It argues that measurement is central: different AI datasets capture different objects (including invention versus use, internal capability building versus outsourcing, and realized activity versus investor perceptions) and can therefore lead to different conclusions. The paper develops a framework for choosing among these measures and surveys available data sources on firm AI efforts. It synthesizes evidence on AI's effects on firm growth, valuation, productivity, risk, labor, competition, financial markets and applications. The paper concludes by suggesting some ideas for future research.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: FACTORS AFFECTING TOBACCO YIELD AND ITS EFFECTS ON HOUSEHOLD INCOME IN TEHSIL RAZAR, DISTRICT SWABI BY

detail.title: FACTORS AFFECTING TOBACCO YIELD AND ITS EFFECTS ON HOUSEHOLD INCOME IN TEHSIL RAZAR, DISTRICT SWABI BY
detail.abstract: Farming communities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa depend considerably on tobacco farming as a source of livelihood because it is a significant cash-crop activity and source of household income. This research explores the major factors that influence the tobacco production and examine how tobacco production contributes to the household income in Tehsil Razar, District Swabi. A semi-structured questionnaire was used to collect primary data from 109 tobacco-growing households. The socio-demographic and economic attributes of the respondents were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Multiple linear regression was used to determine the determinants of tobacco yield. Also, a tobacco profit model was estimated to determine that the tobacco yield has affects on household income or not. The empirical findings show that, education of the farmer, gender of household head, availability of credit and availability of agricultural extension services have positive and statistically significant effects on tobacco yield. On the other hand, production cost was determined to exert negative and strong impact on yield indicating the inefficiencies in the use of inputs. Other independent variables like farming experience, size of landholding and availability of water was not statistically significant perhaps because of the insufficient variation among the sampled households. The profit function analysis showed that the total revenue and quantity produced play a significant and positive role in the profitability of tobacco whereas production costs play a negative role in the net income. The results confirm a positive and significant relationship between productivity of tobacco and income of the household in the research area. The study finds that the development of human capital, institutional support, and effective management of resources are essential in increasing tobacco production, household income and bring economic sustainability to tobacco-growing households in Tehsil Razar, District Swabi.

title: NEUROENGINEERING OF COGNITIVE ARCHITECTURE: CONCEPTUAL SUBSTANTIATION OF A NEW INTERDISCIPLINARY FIELD

detail.title: NEUROENGINEERING OF COGNITIVE ARCHITECTURE: CONCEPTUAL SUBSTANTIATION OF A NEW INTERDISCIPLINARY FIELD

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial conflicts of interest or personal relationships that could have influenced the work presented in this manuscript. The research was conducted independently as part of a theoretical and conceptual study on neuroengineering of cognitive architecture. The author has no financial or commercial affiliations with any organization that could be perceived as affecting the objectivity, interpretation, or conclusions of this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: **Ethics Approval Statement** This study is a conceptual and theoretical work and does not involve experiments with human or animal subjects, clinical trials, or collection of identifiable personal data. Therefore, formal ethics committee approval was not required. No patients or participants were recruited, and no intervention, psychological testing, or medical procedures were conducted. The work is based exclusively on theoretical analysis and synthesis of existing scientific literature.

detail.abstract: Contemporary individuals operate under conditions of persistent informational, emotional, and managerial overload. In such environments, decision quality depends not only on knowledge or intelligence but also on the structural organization of thinking. Despite extensive research in psychology, neuroscience, and cognitive science, a unified framework describing thinking as an integrated and architecturally organized system remains insufficiently developed. This article proposes neuroengineering of cognitive architecture as a new interdisciplinary field focused on structural organization, analysis, and transformation of thinking. Cognitive architecture is defined as an integral system combining perceptual, interpretive, emotional, semantic, regulatory, and behavioral components. Particular attention is given to cognitiveemotional integration as a key parameter of architectural maturity. A structural model of cognitive architecture is proposed, and distinctions between discipline, methodology, and technique are established. The engineering perspective enables conceptualization of thinking as a system subject to modeling and reconfiguration. The proposed framework has theoretical and applied significance for leadership development, decision-making, resilience, and cognitive restructuring. The study outlines directions for further operationalization, empirical validation, and interdisciplinary integration.

title: Political Accountability and the Returns to Peace
affiliations: Queens University Belfast, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU), National University of Singapore (NUS) and University of Strathclyde

detail.title: Political Accountability and the Returns to Peace

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Why do some economies recover from armed conflict much better than others? We provide evidence that political accountability determines whether post-conflict societies realize the peace dividend. We study Cambodia, where a nationwide landmine clearance campaign created large local potential surpluses by freeing arable land and reducing victimization by 48%. Whether these surpluses translate into realized development depends on accountability. Using a staggered difference-in-differences strategy, we show that clearance raises the probability of any nightlights by 7.3 percentage points in areas with strong pre-existing demand for checks and balances on political elites. Where such demand is weak, the effect is close to zero. Elite capture explains the divergence. In low-accountability areas, clearance increases land concessions, deforestation, land disputes, and labor displacement. Where accountability is strong, clearance instead raises household consumption by 22%. Post-conflict recovery requires not just the existence of a peace dividend but political constraints on its capture.

title: Warranting Words: Ai-Drafted Patents And The Written Description Requirement

detail.title: Warranting Words: Ai-Drafted Patents And The Written Description Requirement

publicationDetails.journalName: University of North Carolina Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can now draft patent specifications in minutes, producing dense technical prose, hypothetical examples, and seemingly authoritative data. But large language models optimize for linguistic plausibility rather than empirical accuracy. As a result, AIassisted specifications may include detailed yet fictitious embodiments-molecular sequences, experimental results, or algorithmic performance claims-that appear credible while resisting detection by examiners and practitioners. Existing commentary has treated this problem primarily through downstream doctrines such as enablement. This Article argues that generative drafting also creates a distinct and underappreciated risk for the written-description requirement, particularly for broad, functionally defined genus claims that permit predictive disclosure without requiring working prototypes. The Article develops a limited doctrinal response: patent disclosures should contain "warranting words"-empirical teachings sufficient to make patentability-relevant assertions answerable to testing. Drawing on an account of written description as a doctrine of communicated possession and on recent work on model hallucination, the Article shows why purely linguistic disclosure is an increasingly unreliable indicator of possession at filing. It reframes the "reasonably conveys" standard as requiring a disclosure that provides a reasoned basis for treating the claimed genus as an empirically grounded class of embodiments.

title: Workforce Stratification as a Cancer Research Equity and Capacity Intervention: A Policy and Implementation Framework for Oncology Clinical Trial Sites

detail.title: Workforce Stratification as a Cancer Research Equity and Capacity Intervention: A Policy and Implementation Framework for Oncology Clinical Trial Sites
detail.abstract: Equitable access to clinical trials is a recognised determinant of cancer outcomes, yet participation rates remain highly stratified by institutional research capacity. A primary structural barrier is the shortage of qualified clinical research personnel — sustained partly by an organisational model that conflates advanced data management competencies with routine data entry, inflating the qualification threshold for trial activation at under-resourced sites.This article argues that a formal distinction between a Data Entry Operator (DEO) and a Data Manager/CRC represents a cancer policy intervention capable of expanding trial access, reducing oncologist administrative burden, and creating a sustainable entry-level workforce pipeline.A tiered model is proposed: DEOs perform protocol-driven data entry under DM supervision; DMs/CRCs concentrate on regulatory compliance, adverse event management, and quality assurance. DEOs progress to full CRC qualification through concurrent work-based academic pathways, compatible with ICH-GCP E6(R3) and EU CTR 536/2014 without legislative change.By lowering the staffing threshold for trial activation, the model may expand the institutional base of cancer research participation and strengthen workforce sustainability. Implementation requires coordinated engagement from professional associations and national cancer policy bodies. Prospective evaluation is required to confirm anticipated effects on site activation rates and trial access equity.

title: The AI workforce and firm maturity: Old firms, new tech
affiliations: Sasin GIBA, Pennsylvania State University - School of Graduate Professional Studies (SGPS), Mahidol University International College (MUIC) and Thammasat University

detail.title: The AI workforce and firm maturity: Old firms, new tech

keywords: JEL Classification Codes: O33 (Technological Change: Choices and Consequences

detail.abstract: We examine how firm age affects the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) within the workforce. Drawing on a novel dataset developed by Babina et al. (2024) combining resume and job posting data for U.S. firms, we find that older firms often encounter difficulties integrating AI talent, possibly due to entrenched practices, outdated systems, and resistance to change. Specifically, a rise in firm age by one standard deviation reduces the share of AI workers by 5.2%. However, investments in R&D and infrastructure can mitigate these challenges, enabling modernization and attracting skilled AI professionals. Importantly, our analysis reveals that board composition, particularly the presence of female and minority directors, impacts AI adoption. In older firms, risk-averse decision-making and slower consensus-building among diverse boards may hinder the integration of AI talent. Firms that successfully integrate AI talent achieve significant improvements in market valuation and operational efficiency. Our study provides practical insights for managers and policymakers aiming to guide mature organizations through the challenges of technological transformation. Our findings relate to internal AI capability development and may not fully capture firms' reliance on external AI solutions.

title: BAM Unified Behavioral Amplification Model: An Integrative Framework for Altruistic and Harmful Behavior — Based on Chinese Indigenous Cases and Mathematical Modeling

detail.title: BAM Unified Behavioral Amplification Model: An Integrative Framework for Altruistic and Harmful Behavior — Based on Chinese Indigenous Cases and Mathematical Modeling
detail.abstract: Do altruistic behavior and harmful behavior share the same psychological mechanism? Existing behavioral models focus either on altruism or on harm, leaving the two long divided without a unified explanatory framework. This study adopts a theory-building multiple case study approach, selecting nine Chinese indigenous altruists under the maximum variation principle, utilizing multi-source secondary data, and incorporating Milgram's obedience experiment and the Stanford Prison Experiment for reverse validation. This paper proposes the Behavioral Amplification Unified Model (BAM), comprising three sub-mechanisms: SEMA (Resonance into Action) explains the first occurrence from 0 to 1; AOMDA (Endless Generation) explains the self-sustaining cycle from 1 to N; WARM (Meaning Co-dance) explains the interpersonal transmission of meaning. The integration of the three sub-mechanisms converges on the unified formula A=S×E^(S×M)×M, revealing the symmetric structure of altruism and harm: the exponent S×M constitutes the "Moral Switch" — when positive, empathy drives altruism; when negative, empathy deficiency accelerates harm. Cross-situational validation of nine cases, two types of failure cases, boundary cases, and two classic reverse experiments collectively support the predictive power of the unified formula. The theoretical contributions of this paper lie in: constructing an integrative framework covering the full behavioral spectrum from altruism to harm; integrating Fogg's Behavior Model, Social Cognitive Theory, and the "banality of evil" literature into a single mathematical expression; and transforming traditional Chinese cultural wisdom such as "Xiu Qi Zhi Ping" and "Jian Xian Si Qi" into operable analytical constructs.

title: Governmentality, Fragmentation, and Visibility: Rethinking Intelligence-Led Regulation and Informal Rules in Australia

detail.title: Governmentality, Fragmentation, and Visibility: Rethinking Intelligence-Led Regulation and Informal Rules in Australia
detail.abstract: Intelligence-led regulation (ILR) has become central to contemporary regulatory practice, yet existing regulatory theories struggle to explain how intelligence is produced, how visibility is constructed, and how power operates within data-saturated governance systems. This paper argues that ILR is best understood as a post-modern regulatory practice shaped by fragmented knowledge, distributed power, and the productive force of intelligence itself. Drawing on Foucauldian governmentality, the paper reframes intelligence not as a neutral input into decision-making but as a constitutive element that shapes the realities regulators seek to govern. Using a case study of the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, the paper shows how intelligence systems create uneven fields of visibility, how tacit organisational assumptions and hidden infrastructures structure regulatory action, and how ILR capability varies across domains. To account for these dynamics, the paper introduces two complementary conceptual models. The Layered Regulatory Intelligence Architecture provides a vertically integrated account of the structural, institutional, operational, technological, informal, and epistemic layers through which regulatory intelligence is produced. The ILR Tier/Maturity Model adds a developmental dimension, conceptualising ILR capability as a progression from descriptive, reactive intelligence practices to strategic, system-shaping intelligence. Together, these models offer a unified framework for understanding both the architecture and evolution of ILR, addressing a significant gap in regulatory governance scholarship and providing a foundation for future empirical, comparative, and capability-building work.

title: Rent seeking as a response to multisided market collapse: the case of Australia's news media bargaining regime
affiliations: Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University) and Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University)

detail.title: Rent seeking as a response to multisided market collapse: the case of Australia's news media bargaining regime
detail.abstract: This paper develops a public choice theory of firm response to multi-sided market collapse and illustrates it through Australia’s news media bargaining regime. Multi-sided firms depend on cross-side network effects, asymmetric price structures, and commercial cross-subsidies between distinct groups of users. When one side of the market is unbundled, disintermediated, or competed away, the resulting shock can propagate across the platform’s entire business model. We argue that this multi-sided market collapse creates a unique rent-seeking incentive for incumbent firms to seek to reconstruct lost market sides politically by compelling adjacent firms to become substitute funders. We illustrate this mechanism through Australia’s evolving news media bargaining regime. Twentieth-century newspapers are multi-sided markets that bundled readers, advertisers, classifieds, content, and local political attention, but digital platforms and specialist online services eroded the advertising revenues that had subsidised journalism and low reader prices. Incumbent news firms then translated this business-model failure into claims about bargaining power, fair remuneration, and public interest journalism. Those incumbents have successfully induced or compelled adjacent digital platforms — namely large social media and search platforms — to fund them, whether through direct regulatory compulsion or the credible threat of it. Because adjacency is a political construction rather than an economic relationship, the resulting regime is unstable: as targeted firms respond, the basis on which they are made to pay must be rebuilt on different grounds. The evolution from the earlier News Media Bargaining Code to the latest Albanese government’s News Bargaining Incentive exhibits the kind of regulatory drift such rent seeking regimes produce.

title: Extreme Equilibria: The Benefits of Correlation *
affiliations: Analysis Group, Princeton University and Princeton University

detail.title: Extreme Equilibria: The Benefits of Correlation *
detail.abstract: Correlated equilibria arise naturally when agents communicate or rely on intermediaries such as recommendation systems. We study when a given Nash equilibrium can be improved within the set of correlated equilibria for general objectives. Our key insight is a detail-free criterion: any Nash equilibrium with three or more randomizing agents is generically improvable. We refine this insight to specific classes of games and objectives, including Pareto and utilitarian welfare, and provide constructive methods to obtain improvements. Our findings underscore the ubiquity of improvable Nash equilibria and the crucial role of correlation in enhancing strategic outcomes.

reference: To appear in Manufacturing & Service Operations Management
title: Newsvendor under Ambiguity and Misspecification
affiliations: School of Economics and Management, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Department of Decisions, Operations and Technology, CUHK Business School, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, University of Waterloo - Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science and School of Economics and Management, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

detail.title: Newsvendor under Ambiguity and Misspecification

publicationDetails.detailsText: To appear in Manufacturing & Service Operations Management

detail.abstract: We consider a newsvendor problem with unknown demand distribution, where we distinguish ambiguity under which the newsvendor does not differentiate demand distributions of common characteristics (e.g., mean and variance) and misspecification under which such characteristics might be misspecified (due to, e.g., estimation error and/or distribution shift). Methodology/results: The newsvendor hedges against ambiguity and misspecification by maximizing the worst-case expected profit regularized by a distribution's distance to an ambiguity set of distributions with some specified characteristics. Focusing on the popular mean-variance ambiguity set and optimaltransport cost for the misspecification, we show that the decision criterion of misspecification aversion possesses insightful interpretations as distributional transforms. We derive the closed-form optimal order quantity that generalizes the solution of the seminal Scarf model under only ambiguity aversion. We establish finite-sample performance guarantees that consist of two parts: an in-sample optimal value and an outof-sample effect of misspecification, which can be further decoupled into estimation error and distribution shift. We also extend the framework to multiple products, distributional characteristics specified via optimal transport, and misspecification measured by total variation distance, and derive analytical optimal solutions. Managerial implications: The closed-form solution highlights the impact of misspecification aversion: the optimal order quantity under misspecification aversion can decrease as the price or variance increases, reversing the monotonicity of that under only ambiguity aversion. Hence, ambiguity and misspecification, as different layers of distributional uncertainty, can result in distinct operational consequences. The finitesample performance guarantee theoretically justifies the need to incorporate misspecification aversion in a non-stationary environment, as demonstrated in our experiments with real-world data.

title: From Micro Filters to the Macro Slope

detail.title: From Micro Filters to the Macro Slope

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Sticky-price firms do not merely underreact to ambiguous competitor prices — they actively lean against them. Above an inflation threshold, signals clear and firms reverse to follow. Existing information-friction models restrict weights between zero and one, ruling out this negative pass-through. I show it reflects signal extraction from a public sufficient statistic — the sectoral price index — which collapses the Townsend (1983) hierarchy of beliefs. The Phillips curve separates: the expectations channel is state-dependent, the cost channel is not. Six million UK price observations confirm this asymmetry, delivering a state-dependent Phillips curve with an inflation dependent slope.

title: El Dividendo Universal y como garantizar su ejecución: 5 verdades contraintuitivas

detail.title: El Dividendo Universal y como garantizar su ejecución: 5 verdades contraintuitivas
detail.abstract: This article challenges the prevailing classification of training data as res nullius and reconstructs the Universal Dividend not as redistributive welfare but as the lawful collection of a royalty owed on a collectively held asset. Drawing on Roman-Justinian sources, Lockean property theory, and Nayebi's macroeconomic model of AI-funded UBI, it argues that (i) the aggregate of human knowledge is res communes omnium; (ii) AI laboratories' appropriation violates the Lockean proviso through an irreversible enclosure effected by computational infrastructure inaccessible to the individual; and (iii) the resulting Data Royalty is a property-grounded entitlement, doctrinally distinct from Gates-style robot taxes or land-value taxation. To prevent algorithmic exclusion from rendering the dividend nominal, the article proposes the Habeas Data of Subsistence (HDS): a procedural guarantee of algorithmic due process, instantiated as a Minimum Viable Record (MVR) with five mandatory fields — contract ID, calculation basis, append-only adjustment log, Standardized Basket of Abundance (SBA) index, and recourse endpoint — secured by an Unswitchable Protocol of decentralized execution. Applying Nayebi's capability thresholds, the article shows that an 11%-of-GDP dividend is feasible at 5–7× pre-AI productivity (or 3× under a 33% effective tax on AI capital), and outlines a three-phase prospective implementation: Stabilization, Cognitive Sovereignty, and Abundance. The dividend is reframed as constitutional title over the digital harvest, not fiscal generosity.

title: Fundraising Goals and Charitable Giving
affiliations: and Frankfurt School of Finance & Management

detail.title: Fundraising Goals and Charitable Giving

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study fundraising goals in two preregistered natural field experiments with regular donors of a large international charity (N = 109,945 and N = 47,864). Fundraising goals increase giving by 26%, comparable to the effect of lead donor information (17%). Combining both instruments increases giving by 42%, with effects close to additive. Variation in goal specifications, including progress levels from 9% to 91%, does not significantly affect total donations, consistent with goals operating as informational signals rather than through goal proximity. Failure to reach announced goals reduces subsequent giving by 28%.

title: Business and Non-Business Uses of Individual Foreign Remittances in Bangladesh

detail.title: Business and Non-Business Uses of Individual Foreign Remittances in Bangladesh
detail.abstract: The study attempts to identify the uses of foreign remittance in Bangladesh's business and non-business sectors. The researcher uses different financial and statistical techniques. A structured interview schedule is designed to collect the primary data. The study finds that almost 77% of remittance users do not use remittances in business sectors. A huge number of users (54.9%) are unemployed and housewives; hence, they only spend remittance purchasing daily necessities, luxuries, fashionable items, etc. Only 23% of remittances are used in the business and investment sectors. There is a negative correlation between business uses and non-business uses of remittance. Finally, the study recommends that both senders of remittance and the government should motivate the remittance receivers to save and invest a portion of remittance in business sectors for economic development. Remittance receivers should control their expenses for unnecessary or least required items.

title: On the Matter of Consciousness and Its Equivocation: Toward a Physical Framework for the Properties of Conscious Mass

detail.title: On the Matter of Consciousness and Its Equivocation: Toward a Physical Framework for the Properties of Conscious Mass
detail.abstract:
The ancient principle preserved in the Emerald Tablet, attributed to Hermes Trismegistus and foundational to centuries of philosophical inquiry, holds that the structure of what is above mirrors the structure of what is below. The Apostle Paul, writing to the Corinthians, observed that celestial bodies differ from one another in glory, as terrestrial bodies differ from one another in kind, and that the splendor of each is its own. These are not merely poetic observations. They are, this paper proposes, early articulations of a structural claim that physics has since made precise and that the study of human consciousness has not yet followed to its logical conclusion.

This paper proposes a first formal framework for treating conscious human beings as mass bodies subject to the same class of structural laws that govern physical mass systems. The proposal is not that human beings are literally stars, or that consciousness is reducible to matter. The proposal is more precise and more limited: that the properties which define the behavior of physical mass bodies, their mass, energy output, directional momentum, decay frequency, wavelength character, probability space, and resonance coupling with other bodies, have genuine analogs in the properties of conscious human actors, and that these analogs are in principle observable, measurable, and formally expressible.

The framework draws on the established physical classification of stellar bodies, most rigorously developed through the spectroscopic work of Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin, whose 1925 dissertation demonstrated that stars could be classified by measurable wavelength signatures into a coherent system of spectral types. This paper proposes an analogous classification for conscious mass bodies: a first attempt at mapping the qualitative properties of human actors onto a formal typology grounded in the same physical variables that govern stellar classification, and expressible through a proposed decay wave function W(t) whose components are identified, whose relationships are proposed, and whose full mathematical formalization is offered as an invitation to future research.

The paper makes no claim to have completed this formalization. It claims something more modest and more useful: that the mapping is internally consistent, that the proposed variables are the right variables, that the physical analogs are genuinely analogous rather than merely illustrative, and that the framework generates testable predictions about how conscious actors accumulate influence, attract compatible others, approach critical life events, and transition into new forms. The full mathematical specification of these relationships requires empirical calibration, computational modeling, and collaboration across physics, cognitive science, and the social sciences that exceeds the scope of this paper. What this paper provides is the architecture for that collaboration and an argument for why it is worth pursuing.

The question this paper opens is not only whether consciousness follows structural physical regularities. It is what that means for what mankind can become, what the limits of conscious becoming are, if any exist at all, and what the path looks like from nothing to something to the approach of becoming one with everything.

title: Exploring the intellectual capital efficiency: Measurement and impact on firm performance in the MEDA region

detail.title: Exploring the intellectual capital efficiency: Measurement and impact on firm performance in the MEDA region
detail.abstract: The study examined the relationship between intellectual capital efficiency (ICE) and firm performance across the MEDA region using the World Bank Enterprise Surveys (WBES) collected in 2019 and 2020 and estimating LSDV-regressions via OLS-models for a pooled cross-sectional dataset. Based on the resource-based view and knowledge-based theory, the empirical research adopted a conceptual approach consistent with the widely recognized value-added intellectual coefficient (VAIC) model to examine the impact of human capital efficiency (HCE), structural capital efficiency (SCE), and relational capital efficiency (RCE) on firm performance proxied by EBITDA value, and the principal component analysis (PCA) technique has been employed to obtain a consistent and unbiased value of ICE. The lack of studies on ICE in emerging and developing economies – especially with a focus on MEDA countries – makes this exploratory research noteworthy, filling a gap in the ICE literature. The findings highlight that improving knowledge-based resources can be crucial for gaining a competitive advantage in MEDA transitional economies, especially since firms with higher HCE tend to perform better. Finally, the study provides practical insights for business decision–makers and underlines the pivotal role of knowledge investments in improving firm performance.

title: The Paradox of Protection: Complacency Decay as a Catalyst for Structural Fragility

detail.title: The Paradox of Protection: Complacency Decay as a Catalyst for Structural Fragility

title: The Economic Dimension of Power for a Small Open Economy in the Age of Machine Knowledge Capital

detail.title: The Economic Dimension of Power for a Small Open Economy in the Age of Machine Knowledge Capital
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the evolving economic dimension of national power for a small open economy, focusing on Canada’s position in the transition to the age of machine knowledge capital (MKC). The analysis situates current dynamics within a broader historical sequence of technological epochs, emphasizing the shift from the data-driven economy to MKC following the 2022 inflection point marked by generative AI.

Building on the traditional Mundell-Fleming framework, which demonstrates that small open economies respond differently to policy measures than do large, quasi-closed economies, it argues that small open economies face constraints in exercising geoeconomic power due to their greater reliance on trade and ipso facto their greater vulnerability to retaliation for a geoeconomic play. Accordingly, small open economies are drawn to rules-based systems and collective action rather than geoeconomic adventures.

The paper develops a “theory of the case” to explain Canada’s relative decline in the data-driven era, highlighting the failure to capture data rents, the outflow of high-potential firms, and the resulting erosion of domestic value-added along the “smile curve.” It argues that in the MKC era, which is characterized by capital intensity and enormous appetite for data and compute, these weaknesses translate into diminished economic and geopolitical power, including a diminished capacity to benefit economically from the imperatives of building enhanced defence capabilities.

The central conclusion is that, for small open economies, economic power in the MKC age hinges less on traditional factor endowments and more on the ability to retain and scale firms, capture data rents, and embed these capabilities in dual-use industrial strategies. Without these, conventional strengths in material resources, human capital and institutional quality do not translate into effective national power.

As the digital economy expands, the gap between higher education and industry requirements remains a critical challenge, particularly in emerging markets such as Indonesia. This study is conducted within the Magang Berdampak 2025 program, a national internship initiative funded by Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi, Sains, dan Teknologi (Kemdiktisaintek), which aims to strengthen the link between education and industry through structured, impact-driven learning.

Within this context, PT Vidio Dot Com implemented an AI-enabled internship model by integrating generative AI (Gemini) into daily workflows. Using data from 91 interns, this study examines the relationship between AI enablement, measured through usage frequency, depth of use, and perceived impact, work readiness, including digital skills, communication, and professional competencies.

The findings show statistically significant positive relationships between AI enablement and all dimensions of work readiness, with the strongest association observed in digital readiness. Qualitative insights further indicate that AI functions as “scaffolded expertise,” accelerating learning, improving output quality, and enhancing professional behavior.

These results highlight the role of AI in workforce development and suggest that integrating AI literacy into internship programs is a critical strategy for accelerating digital talent development and bridging the education–industry gap.

title: Human-centered barriers to green supply chain management in fossil fuel-dependent logistics systems: an ISM-based analysis
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN and Effat University

detail.title: Human-centered barriers to green supply chain management in fossil fuel-dependent logistics systems: an ISM-based analysis
detail.abstract:
Introduction: Green supply chain management (GSCM) barriers are widely documented, yet prior studies often treat them as isolated constraints rather than interdependent drivers within transition systems. This limitation is particularly relevant in fossil-fuel-dependent logistics systems. 

Methods: This study employs a mixed-method design combining survey data from logistics professionals in Saudi Arabia with interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and MICMAC analysis to identify hierarchical relationships among GSCM barriers. 

Results: The results reveal that human capability, training, and managerial support function as primary driver barriers influencing technological, financial, and policy-related constraints. Technological and financial barriers act as linkage factors, while policy-related barriers emerge as dependent outcomes. 

Discussion: These findings demonstrate that sustainability challenges in fossil-fuel-dependent logistics systems are structurally interdependent rather than independent obstacles. The study highlights the importance of addressing human and organizational capabilities as upstream drivers to enable effective sustainability transitions.

title: The Impact of Privacy Regulation on User-Platform Interaction in Recommendations and Search
affiliations: , Hong Kong Polytechnic University - Department of Logistics and Maritime Studies, Hong Kong Polytechnic University - Department of Logistics and Maritime Studies, Hong Kong Polytechnic University - Department of Logistics and Maritime Studies and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School

detail.title: The Impact of Privacy Regulation on User-Platform Interaction in Recommendations and Search
detail.abstract: Content platforms rely heavily on user data to support services like recommendations and search. However, the widespread exploitation of user data has raised increasing privacy concerns among users, prompting both industry and regulatory efforts to safeguard user privacy. Motivated by these observations, we examine the impact of privacy regulation on platform service design and its interaction with users by comparing preand post-regulation scenarios. While privacy regulations are intended to protect user privacy by restricting data exploitation, our analysis reveals that they may also generate unintended consequences, especially when users are eager to explore diverse content. Specifically, in the absence of regulation, the platform must provide sufficiently good service to justify data exploitation and persuade users to stay on the platform. It accommodates users’ demand for content diversity by recommending novel content and investing in its service to facilitate user exploration. However, with regulation, the platform may shift toward recommending historically preferred content to users reluctant to search, while deliberately withholding investment in its service to nudge users toward passive consumption of such “safe” recommendations. Paradoxically, user-centric regulation can inadvertently deteriorate user experience in both recommendations and search, reducing overall user welfare. Furthermore, we identify conditions under which win-win and lose-lose outcomes for both the platform and users can be achieved under regulatory policies, thereby providing nuanced guidance for designing privacy regulations that balance platform profitability and user welfare while avoiding unintended adverse outcomes.

detail.abstract: The global administrative landscape is traversing an unprecedented inflection point, shifting from passive digital assistance toward what this paper terms "Agentic Artificial Intelligence" (Agentic AI)-autonomous systems capable of multi-step reasoning, self-directed planning, and independent task execution across complex organizational environments. This research investigates the "inception phase" of this transition, examining how institutional management structures, professional hierarchies, and regulatory frameworks must co-evolve to accommodate the rise of algorithmic decision-making. Through a systematic qualitative review of the 2021-2026 literature, complemented by a multi-case comparative analysis spanning the financial services, public administration, and healthcare sectors, this study develops AGENTIC AI IN ADMINISTRATIVE GOVERNANCE 2 and validates a novel "Integrative Governance Framework" (IGF). The IGF is structured around three interdependent dimensions: Technical Reliability, Organizational Synergy, and Ethical Integrity. Empirical case analysis indicates that well-governed agentic deployments reduce administrative latency by approximately 32%, improve auditing accuracy by 15%, and reduce operational overhead by up to 22%, while simultaneously preserving institutional accountability. However, this paper argues that these gains are neither automatic nor guaranteed; they are contingent upon the disciplined implementation of transparency protocols, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) governance, and continuous bias auditing. The study concludes with a phased strategic roadmap for administrators seeking to achieve operational excellence in the agentic era.

title: Dynamic Constraint Optimisation for Home-to-School and Patient TransportRouting: Safeguarding, Accessibility, and Regulatory Requirements inSpecialised Passenger Fleet Operations

detail.title: Dynamic Constraint Optimisation for Home-to-School and Patient TransportRouting: Safeguarding, Accessibility, and Regulatory Requirements inSpecialised Passenger Fleet Operations
detail.abstract: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) literature is dominated by goods logistics, leaving specialised passengertransport—particularly home-to-school (HTS) and patient transport services (PTS)–without formal treatment of itsdistinctive constraint set. This paper presents the Regulated Passenger Vehicle Routing Problem (RP-VRP), a for-mally specified extension of the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (CVRPTW) developedfrom and validated against a production deployment at a UK SME transport operator providing HTS and PTS underlocal authority contracts.The RP-VRP augments CVRPTW with nine constraint families that, within a unified OR-Tools model, encodethe full regulatory and safeguarding context: weather-adjusted transition costs; optional stop handling with explicitinfeasibility surfacing; multi-dimensional vehicle feature compatibility; multi-dimensional capacity; pickup-deliveryprecedence with configurable interleaving modes; time windows and per-parcel maximum journey duration; priorityand precedence ordering with three enforcement modes; safeguarding-driven conflict separation with three specifica-tion modes; and circular-zone geographic arc restrictions.Large operational instances are handled through an iterative clustering strategy using an intensity-based parcelsorting heuristic, conflict-aware three-stage cluster assignment, and randomised cluster-size reduction. A two-phasedynamic reassignment mechanism operates intra-solve (improving assignment completeness) and post-solve (enablingoperational reactivity after schedule publication).A domain-specific experimental evaluation comprising 30 experiments across five categories validates each con-straint family in isolation and in combination, the sequential pickup-delivery interleaving mode, trip reoptimisa-tion effectiveness (40.1% distance reduction on a school pickup route), and scalability to enterprise problem sizes(52,671 parcels, 2,331 vehicles). Solver correctness is further validated against all 56 Solomon VRPTW benchmarkinstances, achieving feasible solutions on 49 of 56 (87.5%) within a 10-second budget with distance gaps of +1.5%(C1) and +0.6% (C2) for clustered instances most representative of real-world HTS/PTS demand. Deployed acrosstwo operational branches over two months, the system achieves 19.3% route distance reduction, 14.7% vehicle utilisa-tion improvement, 23% scheduling time reduction, 98.6% SLA compliance, and zero feature compatibility violations.

title: Europe's Security, Korea's Arsenal

detail.title: Europe's Security, Korea's Arsenal
detail.abstract: This analysis examines the rapid emergence of South Korea as a strategic defense supplier for NATO and European nations, tracing the structural drivers, competitive advantages, and systemic vulnerabilities of what has been termed the "K-Defense" wave. The paper argues that the war in Ukraine has exposed deep structural deficiencies in Western defense industrial capacity-particularly in the high-volume, conventional munitions and heavy land systems required for sustained peer-to-peer conflict-creating a procurement window that South Korea, with its 70-year hot-production-line posture driven by the enduring threat from North Korea, is uniquely positioned to fill. Drawing on case studies from Norway's acquisition of the Chunmoo Multiple Launch Rocket System, Canada's submarine competition between the German Type 212CD and South Korea's KSS-III, and Poland's transformative "Polonization" deals for K2 tanks, K9 howitzers, and FA-50 fighters, the analysis maps how South Korea has shifted from a niche regional exporter to a competitive structural alternative within NATO's procurement architecture. The paper then assesses three classes of strategic vulnerability that accompany this integration: the homeland-first contingency risk, in which a Korean Peninsula escalation could abruptly redirect South Korean production away from European contracts; the geographic concentration of South Korea's defense industrial base within North Korean missile range; and South Korea's over-90-percent import reliance on Chinese critical minerals-including gallium, germanium, and antimony-that underpin its most advanced export platforms. The analysis concludes with two scenario projections: deeper South Korean integration producing a specialized NATO-Seoul technology partnership, and a Chinese mineral moratorium triggering a homeland-first diversion that leaves NATO's eastern flank strategically exposed. The central finding is that the growing reliance on South Korean systems structurally ties NATO's readiness to East Asian geopolitical stability-a dependency that procurement planners have not yet fully priced in.

detail.abstract: We introduce a choice-set approach to defining markets and a novel method to empirically recover geographic markets using machine learning, Spatial and Categorical Bayesian Clustering (SCBC). SCBC leverages the identity of the seller for each observation to capture market structures in a novel way that is not captured by purely distance-based methods. Finally, we investigate the correct number of clusters and find that the optimal number of clusters is close to the validation set based on industry knowledge.
