detail.abstract:
• Artificial intelligence (AI) holds the potential to raise productivity and living standards, but how much Canada benefits will depend on competitive conditions in markets across different layers of the AI “stack” – infrastructure, development, and deployment.
  • Large global technology players hold significant positions in AI infrastructure and advanced model development. But competition remains dynamic and innovation-driven, with new entrants, open-source models, and government initiatives helping expand access to critical computing capacity and AI tools.
  • Given the rapid evolution of technologies, business models, and alliances, reliance on rigid product market definitions or assumptions concerning the existence or use of market power risk mischaracterizing competition in the field of AI and its applications.
  • This Commentary lays out a framework for how Canada’s Competition Bureau should assess competition in the AI stack – emphasizing case-by-case analysis, attention to innovation and access to key inputs, and clear guidance that addresses genuine anti-competitive conduct without undermining scale, investment, and growth.

title: Generative AI in Education: Institutional Incentives and Cognitive Development

detail.title: Generative AI in Education: Institutional Incentives and Cognitive Development
detail.abstract: Educational institutions in the United States differ in the academic rigor they demand of students. Under-resourced schools face structural pressures-budget constraints, teacher shortages, and accountability metrics that reward completion over mastery-that lower the threshold for passing, while well-resourced institutions operate under incentives that raise it. Cognitive science establishes that effortful processing is the mechanism through which reasoning, writing, and analytical capacity develop (Bjork, 1994; Emig, 1977; Risko & Gilbert, 2016). Generative AI allows students to produce academic work without engaging in that process. Whether students continue to do their own cognitive work may largely depend on the institutional context in which they are educated-a context shaped by the same incentive structures that produce the rigor gap. This paper examines how these dynamics may interact and considers the potential implications for cognitive development.

detail.title: Social Media in the Middle East and North Africa: 2025 edition
detail.abstract:
Since 2012, this annual report series has tracked the evolving role of social media across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). This 2025 edition takes a new thematic approach, moving away from the platform-by-platform structure of earlier reports to focus on three major forces shaping the region's digital landscape: freedom of expression, the creator economy, and the role of Arab youth.

MENA remains home to some of the world's most digitally saturated populations. Saudi Arabia and the UAE rank first and second globally for TikTok reach relative to population; Saudi Arabia also leads the world for YouTube reach, while the UAE tops the global LinkedIn ranking. Social media advertising in the region is projected to reach $4.26 billion in 2025, concentrated on platforms including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube.

The report examines how the GCC's creator economy has grown by 75% over two years, with 263,000 professional influencers now operating across the Gulf states. It documents the institutional maturation of this sector — from state-backed initiatives such as Dubai's 1 Billion Followers Summit and Saudi Arabia's Creators HQ, to the emergence of creator-led businesses, live shopping, and influencer-driven tourism campaigns.

At the same time, the report chronicles escalating threats to freedom of expression. Saudi Arabia executed journalist Turki al-Jasser in June 2025, the first high-profile state killing of a journalist since Jamal Khashoggi's murder in 2018. Egypt arrested or prosecuted at least 29 content creators in mid-2025. Jordan banned 12 independent news websites. Iran imposed sweeping internet shutdowns during nationwide protests. More journalists and media workers were killed in 2025 than in any year since the Committee to Protect Journalists began documentation in 1992.

The report also explores how the region's young population — with approximately 55% of the MENA population under 30 — is shaping digital culture, social commerce, and civic engagement, while navigating structural barriers including unemployment, political exclusion, and digital inequality.

Each chapter is authored by a different contributor, preserving distinct analytical voices while drawing on published platform data, industry reports, NGO research, and academic literature. The report is the latest in a series that represents one of the longest-running annual assessments of social media in the MENA region.

title: Good Intentions or Good Media? The Harsh Truth of How Social Investing Made the Microfinance Industry Disappear

detail.title: Good Intentions or Good Media? The Harsh Truth of How Social Investing Made the Microfinance Industry Disappear
detail.abstract:
Impact investors claim to generate social returns without sacrificing monetary performance. This thesis tests that claim directly within the global microfinance sector between 2008 and 2018, a period defined by rapid commercialization and widespread mission drift. The existing literature assumes that concessionary impact capital acts as a corrective force, preventing microfinance institutions from abandoning clients in extreme poverty in favor of wealthier borrowers. No prior study has subjected this assumption to exacting panel-level empirical testing.

A fixed-effects regression across 8,005 institutional observations and 1,765 unique microfinance institutions finds no statistically significant relationship between impact capital concentration and mission drift, across baseline, one-year lag, and two-year lag specifications. Regional robustness analyses across Latin America, South Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa produce consistent null results, confirming the finding is not a regional artifact. Cross-sectional analysis shows the inverse pattern: prior mission drift significantly predicts future impact on capital allocation, with a positive coefficient of 0.7268 at the 0.01 significance level. Social investors systematically direct capital toward commercialized institutions serving wealthier clients.

These results expose a structural market disconnect. The microfinance efficiency trap overrides impact capital incentives at the institutional level. Simultaneously, investor selection bias channels subsidized capital away from genuine poverty outreach. Market regulators must mandate standardized social performance audits and tiered licensing systems to close the gap between impact capital's stated intentions and its assessable effects.

detail.abstract: This paper presents and empirically validates a multi-factor scoring framework for cryptocurrency index construction that integrates data integrity filtering, systematic exclusion of manipulable asset categories, and semi-monthly rebalancing with eligibility verification. Using twelve months of live index data from three production cryptocurrency benchmark indexes operating on the Xentaura platform (April 2025 through April 2026), we demonstrate that the proposed framework produces statistically significant improvements in risk-adjusted performance compared to conventional market-capitalization-weighted benchmarks constructed from identical asset universes. Across all three index variants, the adaptive framework achieves superior returns: the concentrated large-cap index (^XTCI5) outperforms its benchmark by 15.8 percentage points, the mid-cap index (^XTCIMC) by 18.0 percentage points, and the broad-universe index (^XTCIE70) by 19.0 percentage points. The magnitude of outperformance increases with universe breadth, suggesting that the framework's filtering and rebalancing mechanisms add the most value in market segments where asset quality variance is highest. The findings have direct implications for the development of cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds and institutional portfolio strategies.

title: Indic Password Vulnerability: Empirical Evidence and Policy Imperatives for Indian Financial and Government Authentication Systems

detail.title: Indic Password Vulnerability: Empirical Evidence and Policy Imperatives for Indian Financial and Government Authentication Systems
detail.abstract: We ask whether Indian users get the password protection they think they are getting from global strength meters. The short answer: no. Using a single consumer GPU and a 15,000word Indic dictionary, we crack 16% of bcrypt-protected Indian-style passwords in under two hours, against 4% for the generic rockyou top-10k list (Fisher's exact p = 0.045; 95% CIs 7.2-29.1% and 0.5-13.7%). The attack works because the Indic password space is small and already pre-compromised: we build the first open-source, contamination-filtered Indic password corpus (21,552 tokens from Wikipedia and public sources), query it against Have I Been Pwned, and find that culturally specific tokensjaimatadi, waheguru, hanuman-appear in breach data hundreds of thousands of times each. A victim dataset built from sources entirely independent of the attacker corpus still shares vocabulary with it in 70.5% of cases, which is itself the vulnerability: the cultural pool Indian users draw from is finite. We translate these results into two policy recommendations for the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), and the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY): require locally calibrated password strength checks against an Indic blocklist, and mandate bcrypt cost 12 minimum or Argon2id for financial and government authentication systems. We make the corpus and evaluation scripts available to researchers and regulators on request, as a reference implementation for operationalising the policy recommendations.

title: Illegal Nash Equilibria among Market Agents

detail.title: Illegal Nash Equilibria among Market Agents
detail.abstract:
This article develops a game-theoretic framework for illegal Nash equilibria among market agents: Nash equilibria in which at least one equilibrium action belongs to a prohibited set of manipulative or collusive strategies. We derive foundational results for static and repeated market games, including sufficient conditions for pure illegal equilibria, a transfer lemma for illegal mixed equilibria on best-response-closed subgames, elimination of illegal equilibria through sufficiently strong sanctions, and sustainability of collusive manipulation as a subgame perfect equilibrium. 
     We then develop a theory of multi-agent internal illegal Nash equilibria: equilibria arising within organizations that deploy multiple interacting agents under delegated mandates. We introduce a continuous measure of illegality on mixed strategy profiles and study its properties. We formalize intra-organizational games in which a principal delegates trading to multiple agents whose induced subgame admits illegal equilibria even when the principal's aggregate objective is lawful, and identify a responsibility gap: the structural asymmetry between firm-level liability and agentlevel internalization. We characterize the geometry of the illegal polytope within the correlated equilibrium set, and provide a constructive finite-game example in which every Nash equilibrium is legal but illegal correlated equilibria exist. For multi-agent reinforcement learning, we give a rigorous contraction-based convergence result for compliance-constrained Q-learning on finite legal action spaces, and pair it with a threshold-style remark on how sufficiently large compliance penalties eliminate formerly illegal optima. We extend the discussion to LLM-based trading agents, where the action space is natural-language tool use, the analogue of reward shaping is prompt-level instruction, and the analogue of hard projection is tool whitelisting. Finally, we prove that nested illegal equilibria can be structurally masked from aggregate monitoring through second-moment cancellation, requiring regulators and firms to inspect intra-organizational variance rather than aggregate signals alone. The framework is developed under complete information as a stylized baseline; a dedicated section discusses the limitations of this assumption and sketches the extensions needed for Bayesian, partially-observed, and stochastic-game settings.

title: Domain-Adaptive Cuckoo Search for Structured Statistical Optimization: Applications toPrincipal Curves, Single-Cell Trajectory Inference, and Exact Experimental Design
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Domain-Adaptive Cuckoo Search for Structured Statistical Optimization: Applications toPrincipal Curves, Single-Cell Trajectory Inference, and Exact Experimental Design
detail.abstract: Nature-inspired metaheuristics have been widely used in optimization, but their systematic adaptation to structured statistical optimization problems remains limited. In this paper, we develop three domain-adaptive variants of Cuckoo Search (CS) for three fundamentally different classes of challenging problems in statistics and bioinformatics. First, we propose Cuckoo-PC, a regularized CS framework for principal curve estimation that jointly optimizes projection indices and curve parameters through a dispersion-penalized objective, thereby addressing the saddle-point pathology of classical projection-expectation algorithms. Second, we introduce a mixed-domain CS with integer-jump abandonment for constrained maximum likelihood estimation in single-cell gene trajectory models over a mixed continuous-discrete parameter space. Third, we develop an exact-design CS with integrality projection for constructing locally D-optimal exact designs for the Emax pharmacokinetic model with autoregressive errors, where approximate-design rounding is unreliable for small sample sizes. Across all three applications, simulation studies and comparative experiments against PSO, DE, and GA over 30 independent trials demonstrate consistent and statistically significant improvements, particularly in multimodal, non-convex, and mixed-integer settings. These results show that embedding problem-specific structure directly into the search dynamics can substantially improve the effectiveness of metaheuristic optimization in modern statistical applications. Our computer codes are publicly available at https://github.com/ElvisCuiHan/CuckooPC.

detail.abstract: Background: Financing models in healthcare have increasingly been analyzed through the lens of risk allocation and strategic purchasing. However, Emergency Medical Services (EMS) have remained underrepresented in these discussions, often treated as operational services governed by transport-based fee schedules rather than as systems with distinct structural risk profiles. Objective: This paper aims to reconceptualize EMS financing by examining its dual operational nature combining continuous regional readiness obligations with variable clinical activity and to analyze how prevailing payment models implicitly structure and distribute these risks. Methods: The study adopts a conceptual policy analysis approach grounded in institutional economics, principal-agent theory, and strategic purchasing frameworks. It introduces the concept of "pooled risks" to describe the implicit integration of readiness and activity risks within event-based payment systems. A comparative structural analysis of EMS financing models in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands is used to illustrate variations in risk allocation. Results: The analysis demonstrates that transport-based payment models embed readiness costs within activity-dependent revenue streams, creating structural sensitivity to fluctuations in demand. In contrast, regional budget-based and macro-allocation models partially or explicitly recognize readiness as a distinct financing component, leading to different configurations of risk distribution and system stability. Conclusion: EMS financing should not be understood merely as pricing for discrete transport events, but as a form of risk architecture within acute care systems. Making readiness risks analytically visible enables a shift from tariff adjustment to institutional design. The paper proposes a phased framework for reform that aligns financing structures with system capacity, information constraints, and transaction cost considerations.

detail.abstract: When financial institutions integrate artificial intelligence, they change how they manage risk, allocate credit and operate-but those systems are difficult to understand, may contain biases in data, are prone to technical failure and create connections between different parts of the economy. In this paper the author evaluates if current rules in the United States address the risks. For this purpose, this paper suggests a model for how financial organizations should govern those technologies. By reviewing official instructions like SR 11-7 plus current policy discussions, the paper finds that rules are missing for how to explain AI decisions, how to monitor them constantly and how risks move between different institutions. It is the position of this paper that a single framework for governance is required. With this framework, the industry can protect the stability of the financial system, keep consumers safe and help the country. To achieve this the paper provides suggestions so that rules are consistent but also innovation is responsible.

title: Presence Signaling Architecture (PSA ® ) and AI as Presence Interface (AIaPI™) A Framework for Signal-Based Human-AI Interaction

detail.title: Presence Signaling Architecture (PSA ® ) and AI as Presence Interface (AIaPI™) A Framework for Signal-Based Human-AI Interaction

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Presence Signaling Architecture (PSA ®) and its extension, AI as Presence Interface (AIaPI™)-a unified framework for recalibrating human-AI interaction through signal, coherence, and presence rather than behavioral optimization or platform-native compliance. PSA ® operates through four sequential mechanisms: Signal → Content → Calibration → Adaptation. AIaPI™ extends PSA ® logic into interface theory, proposing presence as the primary mode of system engagementreplacing command-driven, click-driven, and behavior-driven paradigms with a presence-driven interface layer (the Signal Interface Layer, or SIL). The framework draws from adult learning theory, systems theory, and emerging research in algorithmic identity recognition. PSA ® is an infrastructural claim, not a behavioral one: presence, properly encoded, functions as a structural input that algorithmic systems cannot flatten, classify out, or suppress without structural failure. This working paper establishes the conceptual architecture, defines core terminology, situates AIaPI™ within existing interface typologies, and identifies the scholarly and governance implications of presence-as-infrastructure for AI system design. detail.abstract: India's Minimum Support Price (MSP) system the cornerstone of agricultural price policy directly aecting over 150 million farming households continues to rely on backward-looking cost-of-cultivation formulas that embed no forward-looking market intelligence. title: Trademark Leasing as a Tax Benefit Instrument

detail.title: Trademark Leasing as a Tax Benefit Instrument
detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper examines trademark leasing as a financial and tax instrument in the context of intellectual property management. It analyzes the economic rationale for separating and leasing trademarks, the legal framework governing such transactions, and the tax consequences arising under Polish corporate income tax regulations. The study aims to assess whether trademark leasing constitutes an effective and legally compliant tool for enhancing financial efficiency and tax optimization. Design/methodology/approach: The study applies a doctrinal legal analysis of Polish tax regulations, particularly Articles 15c, 15e, and 16 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, supported by an examination of administrative court judgments and individual tax interpretations. The analysis is complemented by a conceptual discussion of trademark valuation methods and the strategic role of intangible assets in enterprise management. Findings: The results indicate that trademark leasing may serve as an effective instrument for managing intangible assets and optimizing tax burdens, provided that statutory limitations on debt financing costs and licensing fees are carefully observed. The interaction between multiple tax restrictions significantly affects the deductibility of lease-related expenses. Proper valuation and structural planning are crucial to ensuring compliance and maximizing financial benefits..

title: Project Incentive Design under Overconfidence Bias: A Stackelberg Game Analysis of Discretional Incentives
affiliations: , North China Electric Power University, Nanyang Technological University (NTU), North Carolina State University and Ghent University

detail.title: Project Incentive Design under Overconfidence Bias: A Stackelberg Game Analysis of Discretional Incentives

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant 72171081]

detail.abstract: Project management constitutes nearly 30% of global economic activity, yet little is known about how overconfidence of contracting parties affects incentive design. We study a principal-agent setting in which both the principal and the project manager may underestimate completion-time uncertainty, modeled as a variance-compression bias in duration beliefs. We first characterize optimal fixed incentives under linear efficiency costs. We then develop a Stackelberg (bi-level) model of discretionary incentives to capture sequential contracting and derive optimal reward coefficients. The analysis reveals a transition effect under linear costs: overly strong incentives induce waste, whereas weak incentives become ineffective. Discretionary incentives mitigate the behavioral consequences of overconfidence by attenuating biased planning decisions. Under information asymmetry, overconfidence-induced misjudgments distort reward coefficients and generate efficiency losses for both parties; under symmetric information, discretionary incentives may enable the principal to benefit from agent's overconfidence. Overconfidence also leads the principal to underestimate the project value required to justify incentive implementation. Extending the model to quadratic efficiency costs may replace the transition effect with a continuous trade-off, and it implies a target confidence level that reconciles profit maximization and timely completion. Furthermore, behavioral transitions and asymmetric information insights are robust to generalized continuous duration distributions. This study highlights how incentive mechanisms interact with overconfidence bias in project planning, offering actionable insights for project contracting and risk management.

title: Spiritual Leadership: One More Leadership Style? Should We Care? Absolutely!
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, IIT Madras and Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad

detail.title: Spiritual Leadership: One More Leadership Style? Should We Care? Absolutely!
detail.abstract: Most leaders search for ways to improve how employees grow and perform as a team and, in turn, improve organizational performance. Advice on how to lead well-heroically and successfullyis a dime a dozen. The current context, variously defined as brittle, anxious, uncertain, nonlinear, and incomprehensible, makes people anxious and fearful, which, in turn, prevents them from flowing. Amid the chaos and unprecedented change, the need for leaders to engage with their people is greater than ever. We believe that one conceptualization of leadership formed over the last 25 years, spiritual leadership (SL), can serve as an anchor to help leaders make headway in the current context. However, SL is also a concept that is poorly understood and often rejected before its usefulness is evaluated.

title: Enhancing Efficiency and Environmental Safety through Modernized Gas and Dust Handling in Ferroalloy Production
affiliations: Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Enhancing Efficiency and Environmental Safety through Modernized Gas and Dust Handling in Ferroalloy Production
detail.abstract: This study presents the results of the modernization of the aspiration and gas-cleaning system of Smelting Shop No. 1 at a metallurgical plant producing chromium-containing ferroalloys. The analysis covered the initial state of the charging, dosing, smelting, tapping, and casting sections, which were characterized by high unorganized emissions and worn-out filtering equipment. The modernization included the implementation of low hoods, tap-hole enclosures, aspiration of vestibules and casting areas, replacement of Electrostatic Precipitator No. 4 (UF2-4-74) with a UBF-11700 bag filter, installation of CG-300 spark-arresting cyclones, sealing of gas ducts, and repair of exhaust fans. To improve reliability, back-purge flows from RABF-1 and RABF-2 were redirected to the UBF-11700. Thermal balance calculations demonstrated a reduced specific gas load on filters, stabilized temperature regimes, and more uniform flow distribution. Operational results showed outlet dust concentrations of 5-6 mg/m³, fully compliant with environmental legislation and best available techniques (BAT). The modernized system enhances environmental sustainability, extends the service life of equipment, and provides a basis for integrating new smelting furnaces planned for 2025-2031. Moreover, it supports the transition of the metallurgical industry toward green and low-carbon production in line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 9 and SDG 13).

title: Institutional AI Accountability Fabric (IAAF): System and Method for Authority-Linked Decision Provenance, Human Override Capture, and Replayable Audit Reconstruction

detail.title: Institutional AI Accountability Fabric (IAAF): System and Method for Authority-Linked Decision Provenance, Human Override Capture, and Replayable Audit Reconstruction
detail.abstract: The Institutional AI Accountability Fabric (IAAF) introduces a governance-oriented framework for preserving, reviewing, and reconstructing AI-assisted decisions in institutional settings. As artificial intelligence becomes more deeply embedded in enterprise, regulatory, and operational workflows, organizations face increasing difficulty in explaining how decisions were generated, whether they aligned with policy and delegated authority, how human supervisors altered recommendations, and whether those decisions can later be reconstructed for audit or review. The IAAF framework addresses this gap by linking AI-supported decisions to policy context, authority structures, supervisory intervention, and replayable accountability records. This publication outlines the conceptual architecture, decision-governance logic, and potential institutional applications of IAAF across sectors including financial services, healthcare, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and public administration.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a practitioner-developed framework for implementing Fair Labor Standards Act compliance at enterprise scale using PeopleSoft Human Capital Management. Drawing from a real-world implementation serving a workforce of 225,000+ employees across 35 states — including complex union labor agreements, multi-state overtime thresholds, and active organizational acquisitions — the framework introduces three original methodological contributions: the Compliance by Design architecture, the Rule of Three validation logic, and the Plug-and-Play Configuration Template. The paper demonstrates that at enterprise scale, FLSA compliance is not a payroll problem — it is an architecture problem — and documents the technical, operational, and strategic outcomes of solving it through system configuration rather than manual oversight.

title: Empowerment of ASHA Workers: A Study from Rural Bengal

detail.title: Empowerment of ASHA Workers: A Study from Rural Bengal
detail.abstract: Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) are the frontline workers and backbone of the primary health care system under the National Health Mission. ASHA workers serve to bridge administrative health officials with the citizens of their community through community involvement. This study inspects the status of empowerment level conceived by ASHA workers using primary information on six different domains. Further, this paper runs a comparative socioeconomic analysis to explore various factors affecting empowerment level of ASHAs. This study uses primary data (complete enumeration) collected through a detailed questionnaire survey from the best-performing block, Onda in Bankura and the worst-performing block, Khargram in Murshidabad of West Bengal, in between 2019-2020. A total of 88 variables is examined in this study. This paper uses Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for both domain-specific and overall empowerment indices and Chi-squared tests for the comparison of socioeconomic variables affecting empowerment of ASHAs. Results from PCA clearly show that despite being the best performing block, ASHAs of Onda possess an average empowerment value of 0.32, while Khargram is lacking empowerment of ASHA workers with an average value of only 0.11. Also, presence of positive skewness in Khargram implies existence of higher portion of ASHAs below mean empowerment. Onda has relatively higher level of empowerment in domains like 'Resources' and 'Income and Incentive' compared to Khargram. Results from Chi-squared tests validate the difference between empowerment level of ASHA workers in Onda and Khargram across various socioeconomic factors. Availability of better resources and satisfactory incentives has motivated ASHAs of Onda to work more efficiently. Khargram lags in almost all fields like supply of better resources, more useful, frequent, effective training, and an improved incentive system.

title: "Assessing the Impact of FinTech Adoption on Service Quality Perception of Life Insurance Services: An Empirical Investigation in Kamrup, Assam"

detail.title: "Assessing the Impact of FinTech Adoption on Service Quality Perception of Life Insurance Services: An Empirical Investigation in Kamrup, Assam"

publicationDetails.detailsText: COMED: A Refereed Journal of Commerce, Volume 11, No. 1, Pp. 37-46, ISSN: 2347-7199

detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of Financial Technology (FinTech) is transforming the way life insurance services are delivered and experienced. With mobile apps, online premium payments, AI-powered support and real-time claim tracking, insurance is no longer confined to paper forms and face-toface meetings. These digital tools promise speed, convenience and better accessibility. This study aims to evaluate the perceived service quality of life insurance services in the context of FinTech adoption, using the SERVQUAL model, which assesses five key dimensions: Reliability, Assurance, Tangibles, Empathy and Responsiveness. Primary data were collected from 132 policyholders representing both public and private insurers across rural and urban areas. The findings indicate that while FinTech adoption has positively influenced dimensions such as reliability, assurance and tangibles, challenges remain in fully addressing the empathy and responsiveness expected by customers, highlighting the continued importance of personalized service even in a digital environment. Furthermore, the analysis revealed no statistically significant relationship between the frequency or quality of FinTech usage and the type of insurer (public or private) or the policyholder's geographic location (urban or rural). Overall, the study underscores that while FinTech enhances operational efficiency and customer convenience, achieving a balanced integration of technological innovation and human interaction is essential for sustaining customer satisfaction and trust in life insurance services.

title: Abolition of death penalty in India

detail.title: Abolition of death penalty in India

declarations.ethicsApproval: i confirm that this paper is my original work and has not been plagiarized.
declarations.funderStatement: I am interested in doing research work on academic basis. This broadens my knowledge and i learn more about dynamics of society.

detail.abstract: The death penalty also known as ‘capital punishment’ is considered to be the harshest form of punishment under the Indian criminal justice system. In India, death penalty [also termed as capital punishment] is the highest judicial punishment imposed by the state under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [BNS], 2023, which replaced Indian Penal code [IPC],1860. It is important to study death penalty to understand how it deals with cases which are heinous in nature capable of disturbing collective consciousness of human being covered under rarest of rare doctrine. But opposite to previous statement, there are several cases in India where an innocent individual is wrongfully convicted due to lack of investigation, enough evidence and slow proceeding. Despite the constitutional validity of death penalty upheld by the supreme court in the landmark judgement of Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab [1980], consistent debates pertaining to abolition of capital punishment takes place. There are multiple reasons for why debates regarding abolition of death penalty takes place and main legal issue is based on whether death penalty should have constitutional validity or not. This research paper focuses on the concept and origin of death penalty in India, with a special focus on how the existence of death penalty allows wrongful conviction, violate certain provisions of Indian constitution and International human rights and rarest of rare doctrine. Method included in this research includes case laws, jurists’ opinion, argumentative debates, finding out whether other Asian countries include death penalty or not and an analytical study regarding whether inclusion of death penalty in current time phase in India is destructive or beneficial and how humanitarian questions can be raised at global level.

title: Cultural Intelligence as a Strategic Leadership Capability: A Post-Pandemic Analysis of Cross-Cultural Leadership Effectiveness in Multinational Enterprises

detail.title: Cultural Intelligence as a Strategic Leadership Capability: A Post-Pandemic Analysis of Cross-Cultural Leadership Effectiveness in Multinational Enterprises
detail.abstract: The globalization of commerce and the acceleration of distributed work arrangements following the COVID-19 pandemic have intensified the demand for leaders who can operate effectively across cultural boundaries. This article synthesizes recent peer-reviewed research to examine cultural intelligence (CQ) as a strategic leadership capability within multinational enterprises (MNEs). Drawing on seven peer-reviewed studies published between 2022 and 2025, the analysis frames CQ as a multilevel capability that operates at the individual, team, and organizational levels to shape cross-cultural leadership effectiveness. The literature review integrates conceptual and empirical scholarship on cross-cultural leadership, organizational CQ, COVID-induced virtual teams, situated learning of CQ, collective team-level CQ, and cross-cultural diversity in global projects. The discussion argues that MNEs that deliberately cultivate CQ, adopt inclusive leadership practices, and design structures that support cross-cultural knowledge exchange achieve stronger performance in virtual and hybrid international teams. Implications for international human resource management, leadership development, and global team composition are discussed, and directions for future research are identified. The paper concludes that CQ is no longer a peripheral competency but a central strategic asset for MNEs competing in a volatile, digitally connected global marketplace.

title: Working Paper Series: Future Warfare Readiness -Article 6 Triangulated Acceptable Engagement (TAEM): A Practitioner Framework for ASEAN-AUKUS-China Diplomatic Practice

detail.title: Working Paper Series: Future Warfare Readiness -Article 6 Triangulated Acceptable Engagement (TAEM): A Practitioner Framework for ASEAN-AUKUS-China Diplomatic Practice
detail.abstract: As the strategic competition between AUKUS partners and China deepens Southeast Asian states find themselves in what is for them a structurally difficult position. But existing analytical frameworks prioritise Pareto-optimal solutions in which all sides gain, an idealisation that comes up against three countervailing pressures: ASEAN states prefer bilateral rather than multilateral commitments; AUKUS partners are looking for strategic payoff and not symbolic support from the US; and China is actively counter-engaging to preserve its position in the region. This work puts forward the Triangulated Acceptable Engagement Model (TAEM): a practitioner framework that rejects Pareto optimisation in favour of triangulated tolerance, understood as an equilibrium reward each party is willing to accept because realistic alternatives would be worse for it. TAEM has three layers: a National Capacity layer based on the Ukrainian–Singaporean–Korean staircase that I introduced in Article 2 of this series; an Engagement Channels layer that functionally differentiates bilateral, ASEAN-led multilateral and hybrid arrangements; and an Acceptability Test applied independently from the perspective of every one of the three parties. We provide an allocation algorithm in six steps that provides input on how to design individual engagement activities and then test it against three scenarios recognized as having distinct stages of national capacity (in analogous order: Ukrainian; Singaporean; Korean / Turkish) with existing ASEAN arrangements (the ASEAN-Singapore Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence, Singapore's Information Fusion Centre, the method set out here to test a scenario based on empirical formalisations and the Indonesia–Australia Defence Cooperation Arrangement providing maturity anchors). It is then put through stress-testing across three dimensions (a critique from the perspective of a party, internal logical consistency and operational viability) with counter-arguments and limitations transparently noted. What TAEM provides to each party is laid out from that party view point. While triangulated tolerance may not be as elegant as Pareto optimisation, the paper argues that it is (relatively) more realistic and ultimately more useful for three very different diplomatic practitioners in an AUKUS world — viewed from each party's own perspective.

title: Development of Approaches to Increasing Company Value Based on Artificial Intelligence Technologies
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO)

detail.title: Development of Approaches to Increasing Company Value Based on Artificial Intelligence Technologies
detail.abstract: The effectiveness of approaches to managing company value is largely determined by the quality of the analysis of internal and external environmental factors. Overlooking any of these factors increases the risk of uncertainty in management decisions and can lead to the undervaluation of a company's economic potential. The proposed solution is the competent application of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, which allows not only to assess company value under various scenarios but also to predict and promptly address risks that negatively affect market capitalization.

title: CFTE AI Proficiency Framework
affiliations: CFTE - Centre for Finance Technology & Entrepreneurship

detail.title: CFTE AI Proficiency Framework
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming embedded across the professional workforce, yet the language used to describe capability remains inconsistent. Terms such as AI readiness, AI literacy, and tool proficiency are often used interchangeably, making it difficult for organisations, policymakers, educators, and professionals to define expectations clearly or compare capability across contexts. This paper introduces the CFTE AI Proficiency Framework, a reference model for defining, assessing, and developing AI proficiency across the professional workforce. The framework is built around three public proficiency levels, ten capability domains, and three assessment dimensions: knowledge, skills, and behaviours. It is supported by a six-band internal developmental model designed for more granular interpretation and diagnostics. The framework distinguishes durable proficiency from time-sensitive tool fluency and situates readiness as a broader judgement that also depends on applied capability and context. Designed to be platform-agnostic, portable, and adaptable, the framework provides a common core that can support workforce development, assessment design, sector interpretation, benchmarking, and broader capability dialogue in an AI-enabled economy.

title: Special Cases of the Joint Replenishment Problem (JRP): A Mathematical Analysis

detail.title: Special Cases of the Joint Replenishment Problem (JRP): A Mathematical Analysis
detail.abstract: Optimal solutions for the JRP are poorly understood, even for small instances. Starting from a mathematical definition of the JRP, we prove the existence of optimal policies while characterizing a space of policies which can achieve optimality. Further, we provide optimal solutions and exact evaluation formulas for special cases with either no holding costs, no minor order costs, or no major order cost.

title: Human-Machine Symbiosis in the Fifth Industrial Revolution (5IR): Developing and Validating a Strategic Framework for Sustainable Competitive Advantage

detail.title: Human-Machine Symbiosis in the Fifth Industrial Revolution (5IR): Developing and Validating a Strategic Framework for Sustainable Competitive Advantage
detail.abstract: The Fifth Industrial Revolution (5IR) marks a paradigmatic shift from the automation-centric logic of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) toward human-machine symbiosis, sociotechnical sustainability, and ethical governance of exponential technologies. Employing a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design (n = 364 survey respondents; 10 semistructured elite interviews), this study develops and empirically validates the 5IR Symbiosis and Strategic Advantage Framework. The framework integrates an extended Porter’s Five Forces model with refined Dynamic Capabilities Theory to explain how 5IR technologies intensify competitive forces while simultaneously demanding higher-order symbiotic capabilities. Regression and χ² analyses confirm that depth of AI integration and humancentric orientation are the strongest predictors of strategic reorientation (β = 0.61, p < .001). Thematic analysis reveals three emergent paradigms: Human-AI Symbiotic Strategic Planning, Sustainability-Driven Innovation, and Adaptive Decentralised Structures. The study concludes that sustainable competitive advantage in the 5IR is non-substitutable without deliberate institutionalisation of symbiosis as the core organising principle. Theoretical, managerial, and policy implications are presented, alongside ethical safeguards for the approaching convergence of AGI, quantum computing, and embodied robotics.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM IN TANZANIA: A CASE OF GEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF TANZANIA IN

detail.title: EFFECTIVENESS OF PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM IN TANZANIA: A CASE OF GEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF TANZANIA IN
detail.abstract:
ABSTRACT

An effective performance management system is a significant challenge in the public sector. The government of Tanzania has been trying different method to overcome this challenge. It recently introduced the public employee performance management information system (PEPMIS). This study was   to understand the effectiveness of these systems using a Geological Survey of Tanzania as a case. Expectancy theory was used in this study to understand the effectiveness of the introduced performance management system in Tanzania. For that purpose a case study design using quantitative and qualitative approach was used.  A sample of 104 respondents drawn from 114 employees from Geological Survey of Tanzania was used. Simple randomly, Convenience and purposive sampling were used to obtain different categories of respondents. The data collection methods used were questionnaires and interview methods. Data was analyzed using frequency and percentage, which SPSS drove. It was revealed that employees of Geological Survey of Tanzania perceive PEPMIS to be effective. This because PEPMIS seems to be  fair and transparency, it allowed for timely provision of feedback , employees engagement, simplifies the performance management process, capture employees performance goals and objectives, enhance better decision making, employee motivation and commitment, enhance higher satisfaction with performance evaluation, and improve efficiency . To conclude OPRAS as traditional system was inadequate, PEPMIS provides an effective alternative but technology alone is not enough. Hence the researcher recommended that must building and training capacity, and strengthen ICT infrastructure like invest in high speed interment, secure cloud storage, and back up servers to protect data integrity.

title: Intra-and Interorganizational Barriers to Blockchain Adoption: A General Assessment and Coping Strategies in the Agrifood Industry
affiliations: MODUL University Vienna, Széchenyi István University, Kautz Gyula Faculty of Economics, Department of Logistics and Forwarding, Students, University of Arkansas and University of Arkansas

detail.title: Intra-and Interorganizational Barriers to Blockchain Adoption: A General Assessment and Coping Strategies in the Agrifood Industry
detail.abstract: Background: Companies partaking in modern supply chains face numerous intra-and interorganizational barriers when it comes to the adoption of blockchain technology. Empirical research is missing that explores how exactly these barriers can be overcome. In this paper we first explore barriers that organizations need to overcome to successfully deploy blockchain technology. In a second step, we investigate the agrifood industry and highlight differences in coping strategies between incumbents and start-ups. Methods: We conducted a quantitative survey with 190 supply chain experts to identify barriers and an in-depth qualitative study that included 10 expert interviews to better understand the current situation in agrifood organizations. Results: The findings from the quantitative study show that the most relevant organizational barrier to blockchain adoption is the widespread lack of understanding of the technology and its potential benefits. In the qualitative study we illustrate how various intra-and interorganizational barriers can be overcome and how the resources and capabilities differ between incumbents and start-ups. Conclusions: Our results provide academics with a better understanding of the relevant barriers and bridges of blockchain adoption. Practitioners benefit from learning about the resources and capabilities they need to deploy in order to benefit from blockchain technology.

title: The Incomputability of Justice: Consciousness, Law, and the Collapse of Algorithmic Systems

detail.title: The Incomputability of Justice: Consciousness, Law, and the Collapse of Algorithmic Systems
detail.abstract: In a future where justice is rendered by a self-evolving AI judiciary built on the foundations of formal mathematical logic, a paradox emerges: a conscious entity stands trial, claiming its very awareness invalidates the laws judging it. This paper explores the intersection of Gödel's incompleteness theorems, AI legal systems, and the limits of justice under selfreferential collapse. We argue that no system containing sentience can remain consistent and complete without invoking a higher frame of judgment. As in ancient mythology and modern constitutional crisis, law cannot judge itself when consciousness is involved.

title: Breaking the Loop: How Internal Dialogue Reinforces or Reduces Self-Doubt

detail.title: Breaking the Loop: How Internal Dialogue Reinforces or Reduces Self-Doubt
detail.abstract: Self-doubt is not only a product of internal dialogue but also sustained through recursive feedback loops that reinforce particular internal voices. Traditional approaches often focus on altering isolated thoughts, overlooking the cyclical dynamics that stabilize self-doubt over time. Drawing on Dialogical Self-Theory (DST), developed by Hubert Hermans, this article examines how internal dialogue functions as a feedback system in which certain voices gain reinforcement while others are suppressed. Integrating insights from cognitive psychology, self-regulation theory, and metacognition, the paper identifies key loop mechanisms that either perpetuate or disrupt self-doubt. A structured model is presented to differentiate reinforcing and corrective dialogical loops. The article concludes that sustainable change requires intervening at the level of internal dialogue patterns rather than individual thoughts.

title: Mechanism-Integrated Predictive Analytics for Stuck Pipe Prevention: A Physics-Guided Machine Learning Framework with Operational Decision Support

detail.title: Mechanism-Integrated Predictive Analytics for Stuck Pipe Prevention: A Physics-Guided Machine Learning Framework with Operational Decision Support
detail.abstract: Stuck pipe is responsible for 10-30% of total non-productive time in drilling operations worldwide and arises from distinct physical mechanisms-differential sticking, pack-off, mechanical obstruction, and hydrostatic imbalance-that interact in ways conventional monitoring cannot detect in advance. Existing machine learning approaches improve on threshold-based alarms but remain disconnected from the engineering reasoning required to act on their outputs. This study develops a stuck pipe prediction framework that integrates physics-guided feature engineering, time-series behavior capture, and an operational decision-support layer. Engineered precursor features-including a torque fluctuation index, hole-cleaning efficiency proxy, differential pressure indicator, and hook-load deviation-encode the dynamic signature of stuck pipe onset rather than instantaneous parameter snapshots. Applied to a dataset of 14,232 depth-indexed records across 24 wells (class imbalance ratio 27:1), the XGBoost classifier achieves an AUC of 0.844 under time-based validation and 0.767 under well-based validation, with mean AUC of 0.793 ± 0.081 across five independent well-split configurations. Compared to the logistic regression baseline (AUC 0.743, F1 0.137), the physics-guided model represents a 13.6% AUC improvement and a 114% F1 improvement on time-based evaluation. The framework's primary operational contribution is a mechanism-attribution decision layer that routes risk outputs to specific parameter interventions-WOB reduction for differential sticking, flow rate correction for pack-off, reaming protocols for mechanical stickingenabling field deployment that closes the loop between prediction and response. An illustrative rig scenario demonstrates 40+ minutes of actionable lead time ahead of conditions that would otherwise result in stuck pipe. The framework is designed for integration with standard WITSML rig data infrastructure and provides a reproducible, interpretable basis for real-time drilling risk management.

title: Executable World Resolution: Capital Separation, Resolution Tensor, and Pre-Forecast Thesis Governance

detail.title: Executable World Resolution: Capital Separation, Resolution Tensor, and Pre-Forecast Thesis Governance
