detail.abstract: We introduce Executable World Resolution (EWR), a capital-indexed market metrology system that measures the installed ability of the current tradable instrument menu to distinguish future worlds under real liquidity, margin, financing, and concentration constraints. The primitive is the capital separation function κₜ,ₕ(ω,ω′) defined as the minimum deployable cost to construct a portfolio whose payoff discriminates two future worlds inside a convex admissible set. From κ we derive a pairwise capital matrix Kₜ,ₕ, a local resolution tensor Gₜ,ₕ(z), a budget-indexed executable partition Πₜ,ₕ(B), and an institutional memo with ACCEPT / REROUTE / KILL / UNIDENTIFIED thesis decisions. The frictionless limiting case recovers classical market completeness and payoffspan rank as degenerate special cases. We validate the framework on a 30-snapshot synthetic stressregime study spanning March 2020 COVID and April 2025 tariff-stress windows, yielding 6 matched pairs with identical instrument menus and identical classical rank diagnostics but materially different EWR: maximum EWR divergence 25.85, maximum benchmark divergence 1.37, maximum excess divergence 24.87, mean contamination improvement 0.38. All seven preregistered hard-kill criteria clear on the flagship study. A free-source real-data bridge (LEAN archives plus cached Yahoo chains with an append-only daily orchestrator) is documented as a first-class production path; the real-data flagship threshold awaits accumulated Yahoo history and is not claimed. We commit to honest reporting of all pre-registered failure states: the synthetic flagship passes, and two free-source real-data studies correctly emit UNIDENTIFIED with densitylimited hard fails, which are reported as findings rather than suppressed.

title: Optimal Monetary Policy under Rational Inattention and a Cost Channel
affiliations: University of Hong Kong, Shandong University and Shandong University

detail.title: Optimal Monetary Policy under Rational Inattention and a Cost Channel
detail.abstract: This paper examines how monetary authorities should balance inflation and output stabilization when firms face rational inattention and working capital requirements. In our environment, monetary expansion both stimulates aggregate demand and lowers marginal costs, yet rational inattention endogenously determines the net transmission: limited information capacity strictly governs the policy sensitivity of the price level. We identify an endogenous regime-switching property in optimal policy: as information capacity improves, the focus shifts from price to output stability, a transition strictly accelerated by the cost channel. For natural rate shocks, this implies a shift from aggressive to restrained policy responses. For markup shocks, the cost channel generates a supply-side subsidy that makes an accommodative policy optimal in high-information environments, overturning the conventional "lean against the wind" prescription. Furthermore, we establish that financial frictions amplify welfare losses from natural rate disturbances but can endogenously mitigate the costs of markup shocks. We analytically and numerically confirm the robustness of these mechanisms under elastic attention, generalized signal structures, and persistent shocks.

title: The Post-Iran Order: A Blueprint for the Ultimate Global Hegemony

detail.title: The Post-Iran Order: A Blueprint for the Ultimate Global Hegemony

declarations.ethicsApproval: For a better world

detail.abstract: In this piece, I argue that the current global instability—from Tehran to Sudan—is the final funeral for the failed "international consensus" model. I propose a "New Realism": a centralized global authority led by a decisive American mandate to replace the "symphony of the deaf" in modern diplomacy.

title: Factor Models Can't Read Financial Statements

detail.title: Factor Models Can't Read Financial Statements
detail.abstract: The Fama-French five-factor model assumes homogeneous capital, independently sorting firms on accounting scalars without regard to capital type. Prior literature attempts to correct the resulting distortions by capitalizing missing intangibles, but these corrections fail by retaining the flawed assumption that intangible and physical assets are fungible risk equivalents. Using R&D as a diagnostic case, I decompose the model's pricing failure: 37% stems from the independent sorting architecture discarding capital-type information, and 63% from the homogeneous-capital assumption itself. The within-industry, out-of-sample alpha for large-cap R&D performers is 79.7 basis points per month (t = 8.26) over 628 months. Mechanically, HML and RMW fail by omitting R&D from book equity and misclassifying R&D expense as a homogeneous operating cost. CMA suffers structural irrelevance: its loading reverses sign within industry, confirming it functions merely as a sector proxy. FASB already differentiates capital through its recognition hierarchy; the factor model ignores this by treating the resulting scalars as fungible.

title: Physics of Software Systems -Part V: A Theoretical Foundation for Structural Adaptive Intelligence (SAI) and Structural Resilience Index (SRI) in General Systems

detail.title: Physics of Software Systems -Part V: A Theoretical Foundation for Structural Adaptive Intelligence (SAI) and Structural Resilience Index (SRI) in General Systems
detail.abstract: We develop a rigorous theoretical framework for Structural Adaptive Intelligence (SAI) as an emergent property of dynamical systems under stress. We generalize SAI beyond software systems into a universal formulation applicable to organizational and socio-technical systems. We derive the Structural Resilience Index (SRI) from first principles and introduce an axiomatic foundation governing adaptive systems. The formulation unifies reliability and resiliency into a measurable construct of system trust.

title: Intermediary Rents in Incentive Contracts

detail.title: Intermediary Rents in Incentive Contracts
detail.abstract: A principal hires an intermediary to incentivize an agent's unobservable effort. Although the intermediary extracts rents, strengthening the agent's outside option allows the principal to reclaim surplus. Consequently, the principal's value and optimal contracts differ markedly from those in standard principal-agent models. Under intermediation, the principal's value strictly increases over a range of the agent's outside option and attains its maximum when that outside option is positive. Furthermore, equilibrium contract payments and effort are non-monotonic and discontinuous in the agent's outside option. My results speak to welfare in labor markets and to the formation of contractual relationships within organizations.

title: Digital Twins as Strategic Assets: Valuation Frameworks for Simulation-Driven Decision Making in Heavy Industry

detail.title: Digital Twins as Strategic Assets: Valuation Frameworks for Simulation-Driven Decision Making in Heavy Industry
detail.abstract: Digital twins-dynamic simulation models that mirror physical assets, processes, or systems in real time-have evolved from engineering visualization tools into strategic decision-making infrastructure across energy, mining, and heavy manufacturing. Yet despite their growing operational significance, digital twins remain conspicuously absent from corporate balance sheets, investment analyses, and board-level strategic discussions. They are budgeted as engineering expenses rather than valued as strategic assets. This paper argues that this accounting and strategic invisibility produces systematic underinvestment in digital twin infrastructure, and proposes a three-layer valuation framework to correct it. The Digital Twin Valuation Model (DTVM) captures value across three layers: (1) replacement cost-the capital required to reconstruct the simulation infrastructure and recalibrate against physical assets; (2) operational value-the measurable decision quality improvements and efficiency gains the digital twin enables in day-today operations; and (3) option value-the strategic flexibility that a well-calibrated digital twin provides for evaluating future capital investments, process changes, and risk scenarios without physical experimentation. Drawing on real options theory and evidence from energy, mining, and heavy manufacturing deployments, the paper demonstrates that option value typically exceeds direct operational savings by 3-5x, fundamentally changing the investment calculus for CFOs and boards. The paper concludes with implications for CFOs structuring digital twin investments, Chief Digital Officers positioning digital twins in enterprise strategy, and board directors exercising oversight on simulation infrastructure as a strategic asset class.

title: Leveling the Field or Stacking the Deck? The Implications of Market Analytics for Content Positioning, Quality, and Information Inequality on UGC Platforms
affiliations: , Fudan University, City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Information Systems and Tsinghua University, School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Leveling the Field or Stacking the Deck? The Implications of Market Analytics for Content Positioning, Quality, and Information Inequality on UGC Platforms
detail.abstract: Market analytics have emerged as an important tool for creators on user-generated content platforms, providing data-driven insights into consumer preferences and market trends. This paper examines how such analytics shape creators’ strategic decisions, particularly content positioning and quality, across two market environments: concentrated markets, characterized by low consumer preference variation, and dispersed markets, characterized by high variation. Using a game-theoretic model, we analyze how creators with heterogeneous prior information adopt and respond to platform-provided analytics in competitive settings. We identify two effects of analytics: a market insight effect, through which analytics improve creators’ understanding of market conditions, and a strategic response effect, through which improved market inference changes competitive behavior. These effects generate opposite outcomes across market environments. In concentrated markets, analytics induce greater content homogeneity and intensify quality competition. In dispersed markets, they promote content differentiation but may reduce overall content quality. Our analysis also shows that analytics do not necessarily mitigate information inequality. Instead, they may stack the deck in favor of more-informed creators, allowing them to capture greater value from adoption. Finally, we examine the welfare implications for creators and consumers and show that both may suffer welfare losses under certain conditions. These findings highlight that platform analytics are not uniformly welfare-enhancing and underscore the importance of designing and governing such tools to balance ecosystem efficiency and equitable access to information.

title: The Entry of Platform Enterprises and Rising Housing Prices: Evidence from Beike Group
affiliations: Hebei University of Technology and Hebei University of Technology

detail.title: The Entry of Platform Enterprises and Rising Housing Prices: Evidence from Beike Group
detail.abstract: With the continuous advancement and widespread adoption of digital technology, online real estate platforms like Beike Group have rapidly emerged and gained extensive use. These platforms have reshaped the traditional business structure and operational models of the real estate market, subsequently affecting housing prices. This study focuses on Beike Group, utilizing data from 219 cities at the prefecture level and above in China from 2016 to 2023. A multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model is employed to empirically assess the net effect of platform entry on new and second-hand housing prices, as well as the underlying mechanisms. The findings reveal that platform entry significantly elevates both types of housing prices to varying degrees. The analysis of moderating mechanisms indicates that the level of digital economic development and marketization amplifies this impact. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the platform's effect is more pronounced in peripheral cities (excluding municipalities, sub-provincial cities, and provincial capitals). During the COVID-19 pandemic, the impact of platform entry on second-hand housing prices weakened, while its effect on new housing prices disappeared. The "three red lines" policy reduced the impact of platform entry on new housing prices but did not significantly affect second-hand housing prices. In cities experiencing population inflow, the positive impact of platform entry on second-hand housing prices is more evident.

title: Powerful Friends and Unwanted Attention: The Effect of Political Connections on Corporate Data Breaches
affiliations: University of Virginia - McIntire School of Commerce, University of Virginia - McIntire School of Commerce, University of Virginia - McIntire School of Commerce and University of Virginia - McIntire School of Commerce

detail.title: Powerful Friends and Unwanted Attention: The Effect of Political Connections on Corporate Data Breaches
detail.abstract: Building political connections is an important strategic investment for corporations in today’s political and economic environment. Prior research highlights the benefits of political connections, but we document an important downside: increased risk of corporate data breaches. Drawing on Routine Activity Theory, we argue that the symbolic value and visibility of political connections make firms more attractive targets for cyber attackers. Using a sample of public companies, we find that politically connected firms are more likely to experience data breaches. These results are robust to alternative model specifications and samples. The association is stronger in more recent years and among firms with highly visible political connections, consistent with heightened public exposure amplifying the effect of political connections. We also find that politically connected firms disclose more cybersecurity risks and invest more in information technology, consistent with firms recognizing and taking action to mitigate elevated cyber risk. Our study broadens understanding of firms’ nonmarket strategies by highlighting an important cybersecurity cost of political ties and offers insights for managers and policymakers considering the risks of political engagement.

title: Political Bias in Crowdchecking and an Algorithmic Remedy
affiliations: University of Rochester - Simon Business School and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Gies College of Business

detail.title: Political Bias in Crowdchecking and an Algorithmic Remedy
detail.abstract: Social media platforms are increasingly replacing professional fact-checking with crowdchecking systems to combat misinformation. While this shift from centralized expert verification to decentralized peer evaluation improves the scalability and speed of content moderation, this paper argues that such a transformation is not without risks. Focusing on X’s Community Notes program, we empirically investigate whether political bias exists in crowdchecking and whether the algorithmic aggregation can mitigate it. We find that notes on politically divisive tweets receive 2.7% fewer helpfulness ratings and have 6.6% lower odds of receiving raters' support compared to notes on non-divisive tweets. As confirmed by a randomized online experiment, this disparity stems from individual-level political bias among raters, activated by divisive content that contradicts raters’ ideological leanings. These individual biases further aggregate into politically biased crowdchecking outcomes, where notes on divisive tweets are 35.2% less likely to become public, thereby undermining the effectiveness of crowdchecking systems in correcting divisive misinformation. Importantly, the bridge-based aggregation algorithm, designed to incorporate cross-ideological consensus, not only fails to mitigate the individual political bias, but also exhibits excessive conservatism, leaving a considerable amount of misinformation uncorrected. To address this vulnerability, we propose a discernment-based algorithm that prioritizes consensus among raters who can make good judgments of note helpfulness, and introduce an entropy-guided rotation to resolve the interpretability challenge in high-dimensional matrix factorization. The proposed algorithm substantially increases misinformation labeling rate while maintaining precision, greatly improving the effectiveness of crowdchecking. This study highlights the ineffectiveness of crowdchecking systems in addressing divisive misinformation that is prevalent and harmful on social media. It underscores the need for more careful algorithm design and provides a promising path to improve the reliability of these systems.

reference: arXiv preprint, arXiv:2604.03844 [cs.CR], April 7, 2026. DOI: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2604.03844
title: Safety and Liveness of Cross-Domain State Preservation under Byzantine Faults: A Mechanized Proof in Isabelle/HOL

detail.title: Safety and Liveness of Cross-Domain State Preservation under Byzantine Faults: A Mechanized Proof in Isabelle/HOL

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is affiliated with Oraclizer and Horizen Korea, and conducts research on the formal verification of cross-domain state synchronization protocols. This paper presents mechanized proofs developed as part of the Oraclizer project. The author declares no direct financial conflicts of interest related to this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as part of the Oraclizer project at Horizen Korea. No external funding was received for this work.

publicationDetails.detailsText: arXiv preprint, arXiv:2604.03844 [cs.CR], April 7, 2026. DOI: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2604.03844

detail.abstract: Formally guaranteeing the safety and liveness of regulatory state transitions in cross-domain state synchronization systems is a problem of growing importance as tokenized assets are increasingly operated across heterogeneous blockchain networks and off-chain ledgers. This paper presents a mechanized proof of 2,348 lines in Isabelle/HOL establishing two complementary properties. First, cross-domain state preservation (safety): a regulatory state transition performed on one domain is faithfully reflected across all connected domains with structural preservation. This guarantee encompasses bidirectional roundtrip preservation, consistency across an arbitrary finite set of domains, and per-asset isolation. Second, liveness under Byzantine faults: in the presence of up to f < n/3 Byzantine nodes, we prove deterministic resolution of conflicting regulatory actions, deadlock freedom, and starvation freedom. In the combination of these two properties, the liveness proof discharges the honest-node assumption of the safety proof under Byzantine faults, promoting conditional safety to an unconditional guarantee. The seven generic locales derived in this process are domain-independent and reusable for arbitrary domains via Isabelle/HOL's interpretation mechanism. The application context is a regulatory state transition model based on the RCP framework (arXiv:2603.29278), which systematizes 31 requirements from 15 global financial regulatory authorities. All proof artifacts build in Isabelle/HOL without sorry or oops, have been submitted to the Archive of Formal Proofs (under review), and are publicly available on GitHub.

title: From Tool Use to Evaluative Judgment: A Readiness Framework for Generative AI in Higher Education
affiliations: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology - Karlsruhe Service Research Institute and University of Nebraska at Omaha

detail.title: From Tool Use to Evaluative Judgment: A Readiness Framework for Generative AI in Higher Education

declarations.ethicsApproval: This has been reviewed and approved by the NU system IRB under TITLE:Workforce readiness of university students considering Generative AI use IRB#:0038-25-EX PI:Hall, Magie

detail.abstract:
Generative AI (GenAI) tools are rapidly reshaping higher education, yet institutional responses often oscillate between prohibition and permissiveness without a clear theory of student readiness. This white paper advances a multidimensional framework of GenAI readiness grounded in established readiness scholarship and empirical student data collected through focus groups and survey responses at a large public university. Rather than defining readiness as tool familiarity or prompt proficiency, the report conceptualizes GenAI readiness as a composite capacity spanning cognitive strategies (evaluative judgment under uncertainty), academic skills (disciplinary competence independent of automation), academic behaviors (self-regulation and delegation literacy), and contextual awareness (policy literacy and ethical norms).

Student findings reveal that their dominant workflow is verification and that they routinely triangulate AI outputs against authoritative sources, adjust use based on task stakes, and express concern about dependency and skill erosion. At the same time, ambiguity around disclosure, paraphrase boundaries, and detectability creates anxiety and inconsistent behavior. These findings align with contemporary literature identifying both the pedagogical promise of AI-supported learning and the “performance paradox,” wherein short-term output gains may not translate into durable competence.

This white paper argues that the central institutional question is not whether GenAI should be allowed or banned, but under what design conditions it strengthens learning rather than substitutes for it. It proposes a readiness-centered institutional strategy that includes standardized policy vocabulary, explicit verification literacies, assessment redesign that makes reasoning visible, and structured professional development for faculty and staff. By reframing GenAI integration as a readiness problem rather than a compliance problem, the report offers a coherent path for aligning academic integrity, instructional design, and workforce preparation in AI-mediated learning environments.

title: Empowering Sustainable Growth Through Emerging Technologies in Serbia and North Macedonia
affiliations: International Balkan University, Institute of Economic Sciences Belgrade and Institute of Economic Sciences Belgrade

detail.title: Empowering Sustainable Growth Through Emerging Technologies in Serbia and North Macedonia
detail.abstract: This study explores the perceived economic, social, and environmental impacts of emerging technologies (including artificial intelligence, IoT, and big data) on sustainable growth in Serbia and North Macedonia. Drawing on survey responses from participants across professional sectors, the analysis employs descriptive statistics, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis H tests to assess motivational factors, barriers to adoption, and sectoral differences. Findings indicate that innovation an competitiveness are dominant motivators, especially in North Macedonia, while high costs, skill shortages, and limited awareness remain key barriers. Economic benefits such as cost savings and operational efficiency are widely recognized, though environmental outcomes, particularly renewable energy adoption, are less developed. Sectoral comparisons reveal that business organizations lead in benefit realization, whereas government entities lag behind. The study highlights the need for contextspecific policies and inclusive digital strategies to ensure that the adoption of emerging technologies supports long-term, sustainable development across varying institutional and sectoral environments.

title: Generational Evolution and Phase Transition Models of Managed Service Providers in IT Operations: A Socio-Technical Systems (STS) Approach

detail.title: Generational Evolution and Phase Transition Models of Managed Service Providers in IT Operations: A Socio-Technical Systems (STS) Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author, Akihiro Ito, is currently employed as a Technical Support Engineer at New Relic, Inc. Products developed by New Relic (specifically, the New Relic SRE Agent) are discussed conceptually in this paper as an example of socio-technical implementation. This research was conducted independently by the author and does not represent the official views, strategies, or endorsements of New Relic, Inc. The author received no specific financial support or grants from any organization for the submitted work.

detail.abstract: In modern cloud-native environments, the complexity (entropy) of IT systems is expanding exponentially. This paper redefines the evolution of Managed Service Providers (MSPs)—responsible for the stable operation and optimization of systems—not merely as a change in outsourcing formats, but as a "Phase Transition" within a physical state diagram. First, we prove the mechanism by which the conventional MSP 1.0 (Solid) inevitably collapses due to "Time Delay" in control engineering, pointing out the "Co-dependent Stagnation" that occurs between MSPs and user companies. Second, we model Agentic AI as "Maxwell's Demon" that lowers entropy, and formulate the requirements (Error Budget, minimization of MTTT, and Potentialization of Decision-making) necessary for the phase transition to MSP 3.0 (Gas) to govern the autonomy of AI. This research provides the foundational theory for a next-generation Socio-Technical Systems (STS) architecture where humans and AI collaborate.

title: The J-Curve of Change A Practitioner Framework for Managing Organisational Performance During Technology-Driven Transformation

detail.title: The J-Curve of Change A Practitioner Framework for Managing Organisational Performance During Technology-Driven Transformation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Alchemy Consulting Services Limited, a consultancy providing AI transformation and change management advisory services. The J-Curve framework described in this paper predates the establishment of Alchemy Consulting and is not a commercial product of that firm.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper presents a conceptual practitioner framework and literature review. No primary research involving human participants, patients, or personal data was conducted. Ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research. The work was self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: The J-Curve of Change is a practitioner framework, first published in 2005, describing the characteristic trajectory of organisational performance during technology-driven transformation. It proposes that performance reliably deteriorates following the introduction of change before recovering and surpassing the prior baseline-forming a 'J' shape when plotted against time. The framework identifies three management imperatives for leaders seeking to navigate this period successfully: managing stakeholder expectations, minimising the depth of the performance dip, and ensuring the organisation recovers fully. Originally developed from the author's experience leading major intranet portal implementations at two of the United Kingdom's largest organisations, the model has since been applied widely across change management, project management, healthcare, education, agile methodology, and AI transformation contexts. This paper formalises the framework, situates it within the change management literature, and documents its subsequent adoption and citation across academic and practitioner communities.

title: AI Tools in Higher Education: Design, Impact, and Challenges

detail.title: AI Tools in Higher Education: Design, Impact, and Challenges

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no competing interests, financial or personal, that could have influenced the work reported in this paper
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a review of existing literature and does not involve human participants or animals. Therefore, ethical approval was not required
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education through tools that support teaching, learning, assessment, and institutional decision-making. This paper reviews major categories of AI-powered educational tools, including intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning platforms, automated assessment, chatbots, generative AI, and predictive analytics. The review analyzes key design considerations such as learner-centered design, pedagogical alignment, usability, transparency, and fairness, and examines their impact on learning outcomes, student engagement, feedback quality, teacher workload, and institutional processes. The findings show that AI tools can enhance learning and efficiency, but their effectiveness depends on proper design and implementation. Several challenges remain, including infrastructure limitations, lack of training, privacy concerns, bias, cost, and resistance to adoption. The paper highlights the need for human-centered, ethical, and context-aware AI systems. Overall, a balanced approach that integrates technology with pedagogy is essential for achieving meaningful and sustainable impact in higher education.

title: The Ceiling Above Power Artificial Intelligence and the Return of Human Fragility

detail.title: The Ceiling Above Power Artificial Intelligence and the Return of Human Fragility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known personal relationships, financial interests, or affiliations with any individuals or organizations that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it is a theoretical and philosophical analysis that does not involve human participants, patient data, interviews, surveys, or experimental procedures.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that the deepest significance of artificial intelligence may lie not merely in technological acceleration, productivity gains, or computational power, but in the way it intensifies a specifically human error: the tendency to confuse expanded capacity with ontological elevation. As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into decisionmaking, interpretation, coordination, and control, it may encourage human beings to misread their own position in the world. The central claim of this paper is that the real danger of advanced artificial intelligence is not simply that machines may become powerful, but that human beings may begin to interpret their own technical success as evidence of sovereign mastery. In that process, use turns into appropriation, appropriation into delegated agency, delegated agency into intoxication, and intoxication into a misguided desire to test the limits of one's own constructed power. Yet the expansion of capacity does not abolish the structure of human finitude. Human beings may enlarge their reach, but they do not thereby overcome their fragility, mortality, or epistemic incompleteness. For that reason, artificial intelligence should be understood not only as an instrument of expansion, but also as a stage upon which the limit of human power is revealed. The endpoint of this process is not necessarily annihilation, but collision: a return to human fragility after the illusion of completed control.

title: When Metric Choice Amplifies Reification Fallacies

detail.title: When Metric Choice Amplifies Reification Fallacies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: Within the text-as-data framework, words are not merely letters on a blank page; they convey expression and intention and, for researchers, provide a basis for measuring abstract concepts and theoretically defined constructs, including authorial representation and alignment, psychological states and orientations, social and financial behavior, and individual or environmental characteristics. Yet the validity of dictionary-based measurement depends not only on dictionary design, but also on the metric used to quantify dictionary matches. This paper examines how metric choice shapes classification accuracy, robustness, and interpretation in computer-aided text analysis. Comparing frequency counts, relative frequencies, tf-idf-weighted frequencies, and an expected-value-adjusted metric (EST), we show that these measures are not interchangeable. In synthetic classification tasks, frequency counts achieve the highest overall accuracy and are particularly effective in detecting category presence. Relative frequencies apply a stringent decision rule, producing highly reliable positive classifications at the cost of a large number of false negatives. EST-adjusted frequencies perform especially well in short-document and single-label settings, but decline in more complex multi-label long-document conditions. Overall, the study shows that metric choice must be aligned with the inferential purpose of the analysis, as unreflective reliance on conventional metrics can amplify double reification fallacies in text-based research.

title: Modernizing On-Prem Government Systems to Cloud-Native Architectures: A U.S. Public Sector Case Study

detail.title: Modernizing On-Prem Government Systems to Cloud-Native Architectures: A U.S. Public Sector Case Study
detail.abstract: The US public-sector agencies have been using the old on-premises systems that were initially built to support a fixed workload, a limited number of users at a given time, and rare reporting. With the changes in service expectations to mobile access, fast data accessibility, and uninterrupted access, studies report that such environments are creating increasing maintenance costs, limiting scalability, and making it di cult to meet changing security and audit objectives. Modernization was able to realize 78% less manual reconciliation, 82% higher accuracy in anomaly detection, better data quality by 11.7%, and reduced business costs by 81%. Such restrictions are most obvious at the time of economic disruption, when unemployment mechanisms should be scaled in a very short time and at the same time maintain the accuracy of the data and trust of the population. The case study focuses on cloud-native transformation and analyzes the modernization of a state-level workforce services platform operated by a U.S. public-sector labor agency. The project substituted a single-edi ce, on-premise system of labor exchange with a Microsoft Azure-based infrastructure, which is based on serverless computing, administered data services, and code as infrastructure. Using peer-reviewed studies and government structures, the work records the choices of the architecture, sequencing of migration, and controls of governance. It relates the results to quantified performances in terms of efficiency of cost, reporting velocity, reliability of systems, and participation of citizens. As the case shows, the process of cloud-native modernization can deliver operational benefits and address the compliance and accountability demands of the public sector when implemented in stages, based on a defined migration and policy-respecting design.

title: An Onto-Epistemological Approach to the Being–Knowledge Relation: The DuruVizyon Analytical Plane

detail.title: An Onto-Epistemological Approach to the Being–Knowledge Relation: The DuruVizyon Analytical Plane

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, financial, or institutional relationships that could have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, the research presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required, as this study is a theoretical/philosophical research paper and does not involve human participants, patients, animals, or experimental procedures.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently and received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This study proposes the DuruVizyon Analytical Plane, a model that enables the systematic and comparable analysis of the relationship between being and knowledge. The model defines ontological and epistemological modes as two independent axes and integrates these modes within a single analytical structure. Within this framework, distinctions such as “actual–possible” and “known–unknown” can be positioned on a coordinated plane. The proposed approach makes it possible to evaluate states of being not only in terms of their ontological status, but also on the basis of their epistemological accessibility. In this way, different states of being can be systematically analyzed and compared within a unified framework. The study argues that ontological inquiry should be conducted by taking into account the conditions of epistemological constructability and demonstrates that the relationship between these two domains can be structurally modeled. In this respect, the Analytical Plane functions not only as a conceptual representational tool, but also as a framework for the systematic analysis of the being–knowledge relationship. Consequently, the study aims to demonstrate that the relationship between ontology and epistemology can be analytically examined within a coordinated structure, thereby offering an original contribution to the literature. In the existing literature, the relationship between being and knowledge has predominantly been addressed through fragmented, reductionist, or one-sided approaches; as a result, a comprehensive model enabling their simultaneous and coordinated analysis has remained lacking. This study brings these dispersed approaches together within a single analytical plane, thereby providing conceptual coherence while preserving the irreducibility of both domains, and proposes an original framework for their integrated analysis.

title: Echo Chamber Dynamics and Influence-Aware Evidence Aggregation: A Formal Model for Epistemic Integrity in Intelligence Analysis

detail.title: Echo Chamber Dynamics and Influence-Aware Evidence Aggregation: A Formal Model for Epistemic Integrity in Intelligence Analysis
detail.abstract: Correlated corroboration can masquerade as independent confirmation, inflating confidence through a false independence assumption. We design and analyze an influence-aware aggregation component within an expert system architecture for intelligence analysis that makes dependence explicit, aggregates conservatively under partial knowledge, and supports deterministic replay. We formalize an influence-aware evidence graph (EIIG), define Effective Independent Evidence (EIE) as a discounting proxy for partial dependence knowledge, and introduce CONFPROP, an anti-cascade confidence propagation rule with damping and temporal buffering. We analyze parameter sensitivity and illustrate how the approach limits cascade amplification while preserving monotonicity and saturation properties under uncertainty.

title: The Buy-or-Build Decision, Revisited: How Agentic AI Changes the Economics of Enterprise Software

detail.title: The Buy-or-Build Decision, Revisited: How Agentic AI Changes the Economics of Enterprise Software
detail.abstract: Advances in generative artificial intelligence, particularly agentic coding systems capable of autonomous software development, are disrupting the economics of the makeor-buy decision for enterprise applications. The "SaaSocalypse" narrative predicts that AI will render large segments of the Software-as-a-Service market obsolete by enabling firms to build software in-house at a fraction of historical cost. This paper adopts a conceptual research approach, combining transaction cost economics and the resource-based view with an assessment of current AI capabilities, to systematically re-evaluate the factors underlying the make-or-buy decision. It makes three contributions. First, it provides a factor-level analysis of how AI reshapes seven canonical decision determinants: cost, strategic differentiation, asset specificity, vendor lock-in, time-to-market, quality and compliance, and organizational capability. Second, it develops a typology of enterprise applications by their sensitivity to AI-induced shifts in make-or-buy economics. Third, it demonstrates that AI fundamentally transforms the governance properties of the Make option, shifting it from Williamson's pure hierarchy to a hybrid governance form that combines code ownership with external AI infrastructure dependency, with qualitatively different economics, capability requirements, and governance structures than pre-AI in-house development. The analysis finds that the SaaSocalypse thesis is overstated for most enterprise application categories; Make is most compelling for commodity utilities and differentiating custom applications in the AI era, while regulated and mission-critical systems remain predominantly in the buy domain.

detail.abstract: Structured data markup, particularly JSON-LD implementations of the Schema.org vocabulary, has become a critical factor in how search engines interpret, classify, and surface web content. Despite growing recognition of schema markup's role in search engine optimization (SEO), there has been limited empirical investigation into its adoption within specific professional service verticals. This study presents a systematic analysis of schema markup implementation across 500 personal injury (PI) law firm websites operating in the United States. Through automated crawling and programmatic code inspection, we examine the prevalence of key schema types, including LegalService, Attorney, Organization, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, and WebPage, and assess the completeness, accuracy, and semantic richness of deployed structured data. Our findings reveal significant gaps: 67.6% of sampled firms implement some form of JSON-LD markup, yet only 40.0% deploy the LegalService schema type specifically designed for legal service providers. The mean Schema Completeness Index (SCI) across sites with structured data was 11.8 out of a possible 25. Entity disambiguation remains the weakest dimension: only 84.0% of sites with schema include @id properties and 81.4% include sameAs references. These findings have implications for legal services discoverability in both traditional search engine results pages (SERPs) and emerging AI-mediated answer engines. We propose a Structured Data Maturity Model for legal service websites and outline directions for future research.

detail.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in recruitment has significantly transformed hiring processes by enhancing efficiency and reducing manual effort. However, concerns regarding bias, fairness, and the limitations of AI systems have gained increasing attention. This paper critically examines the presence of bias in AI-based recruitment systems, explores their functional limitations, and compares their effectiveness with human judgment. Drawing upon existing literature and case study evidence, particularly the Amazon AI recruitment system, the study highlights how algorithmic bias emerges from historical data and system design. Furthermore, the paper evaluates human-AI collaboration and argues that while hybrid approaches offer potential improvements, they must be carefully implemented. The study concludes that AI should be used as a supportive tool rather than a replacement for human decision-making to ensure fairness, transparency, and ethical hiring practices.

detail.abstract: As organizations migrate to cloud-native serverless models, the ephemeral nature of Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) environments renders traditional perimeter-based security obsolete. This research proposes a lightweight, AI-driven Intrusion Detection System (IDS) optimized for serverless environments (Node.js/Flask). Utilizing a behavioral anomaly detection model based on semi-supervised machine learning, the system establishes a baseline of normal function behavior through API request metadata. Our findings demonstrate high detection accuracy for event-injection and Denial-of-Wallet attacks with minimal computational overhead, preserving the cost and latency benefits of serverless computing.

title: Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types for Neural Network Model Merging: A Two-Layer Architecture Enabling CRDT-Compliant Model Merging Across 26 Strategies

detail.title: Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types for Neural Network Model Merging: A Two-Layer Architecture Enabling CRDT-Compliant Model Merging Across 26 Strategies
detail.abstract: All 26 neural network merge strategies we tested-including weight averaging, SLERP, TIES, DARE, Fisher merging, and evolutionary approaches-fail the algebraic properties (commutativity, associativity, idempotency) required for conflict-free distributed operation [29]. We prove that this failure is structural: normalisation-based merges cannot simultaneously satisfy all three properties. To resolve this, we present a two-layer architecture-CRDTMergeStatethat wraps any merge strategy in a CRDT-compliant (Conflict-Free Replicated Data Type) layer. Layer 1 manages contributions via OR-Set CRDT semantics [28], where the merge operation is set union-trivially commutative, associative, and idempotent. Layer 2 applies merge strategies as deterministic pure functions over a canonically-ordered contribution set, with randomness seeded from the Merkle root [26]. We prove that this separation guarantees Strong Eventual Consistency [29]: all replicas receiving the same contributions compute identical merged models, regardless of message ordering. Empirical validation spans three tiers: controlled 4 × 4 tensors (104/104 tests pass), production-scale models up to 7.24 B parameters (208 strategy-level tests, 43,368 layer-level property checks at capped tensor resolution), and multi-node convergence under gossip and partition healing (100 nodes, 20 orderings), with CRDT overhead below 0.5 ms. Because the wrapper is transparent, downstream performance is identical by construction, confirmed via byte-identical output verification. The reference implementation is available as crdt-merge v0.9.4.

title: Constrained Actionable Counterfactuals with Economic Cost Optimization for Credit Scoring
affiliations: Ibn Zohr University, Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University and Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University

detail.title: Constrained Actionable Counterfactuals with Economic Cost Optimization for Credit Scoring
detail.abstract: Automated credit scoring systems increasingly rely on black-box machine learning models, raising critical concerns about transparency and the right to algorithmic recourse under the EU AI Act and GDPR. Counterfactual explanations offer a promising path by answering “what should change for a different outcome?”, yet existing methods often generate recommendations that violate real-world constraints—suggesting modifications to immutable attributes such as age or gender, or ignoring the heterogeneous economic costs of different feature changes.This paper introduces CA-CF (Constrained Actionable Counterfactual Explanations), a gradient-based optimization framework that simultaneously addresses four objectives: prediction validity, proximity to the original instance, realistic economic cost, and distributional plausibility. CA-CF enforces actionability through a dual constraint mechanism combining a preventive gradient mask—which eliminates wasted optimizer momentum on immutable dimensions—with a corrective post-step projection onto the feasible set. The economic cost function employs heterogeneous penalties: -weighted costs for freely adjustable features and -weighted costs for monotonically constrained features, reflecting the increasing marginal difficulty of larger changes.We evaluate CA-CF through a rigorous ablation study comprising six methods, two benchmark credit datasets (German Credit, Adult Census), five random seeds, five-fold cross-validation, and 12 evaluation metrics across 105,000 generated counterfactuals. Results demonstrate that CA-CF achieves the best multi-objective trade-off: 95.1% validity on German Credit and 99.9% on Adult Census with zero constraint violations, median latency under 25 ms, and economic costs competitive with unconstrained baselines. Statistical significance is confirmed via Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction (). The ablation study reveals that each component contributes measurably, with the gradient mask recovering +2.82% validity lost to cost pressure on German Credit. Sensitivity analysis demonstrates robustness across hyperparameter ranges, particularly on Adult Census where validity remains at 100% across the entire  grid.

title: From Erosion to Retention: How Platform Misconduct Erodes User Stickiness and The Mitigation Strategies
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Erosion to Retention: How Platform Misconduct Erodes User Stickiness and The Mitigation Strategies
detail.abstract: As the digital economy shifts from an era of traffic-driven growth to one centered on retention-based competition, user stickiness has emerged as a pivotal asset underpinning platform competitiveness. Nonetheless, the frequent occurrence of platform misconduct has severely eroded user trust. Addressing the paradox of persistent user engagement amidst recurrent platform misconduct, this study draws on trust theory to develop an integrated analytical framework that incorporates multidimensional moderators at the user, technological, and cultural levels. The aim is to investigate both the mechanisms through which platform misconduct influences user stickiness and the boundary conditions shaping this relationship. A mixed-methods approach is employed, combining empirical analysis of 763 survey responses with supplementary robustness tests utilizing objective secondary data from user reviews on the App Store. The findings reveal that: (1) Platform misconduct significantly reduces user stickiness, with user trust serving as a key mediating mechanism—suggesting that misconduct primarily induces user churn by undermining trust; (2) Personalization, transparency in data sharing, and corporate digital responsibility (CDR) significantly attenuate the detrimental effect of misconduct on user trust. Specifically, the perceived benefits derived from high personalization, the sense of control afforded by high transparency, and the corporate reputation cultivated through high CDR collectively constitute a buffering mechanism that mitigates trust erosion. This study not only advances understanding of user churn resulting from platform governance failures but also provides theoretical insights and practical implications for platform enterprises aiming to cultivate a responsible digital ecosystem.

title: Third-Party Checkout and SME E-Commerce: Heterogeneous Effects on Transactions and Customer Relationships
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, College of Business, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Third-Party Checkout and SME E-Commerce: Heterogeneous Effects on Transactions and Customer Relationships
detail.abstract: Conventional online checkout in e-commerce requires consumers to complete multiple procedural steps, including account creation, shipping and payment information entry, and final confirmation, creating checkout-stage friction that can prevent intended purchases from becoming completed transactions. Third-party checkout infrastructure (TPCI) reduces this bottleneck by allowing consumers to complete purchases using credentials pre-stored with an external provider. For retailers, however, this convenience creates a strategic tension, since native checkout also serves as a gateway to retailer account creation. By compressing this process, TPCI may recover lost transactions while weakening incentives to enter the retailer’s own membership system, a key channel for direct customer relationships and retailer-controlled customer information. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design with monthly transaction data from 110 South Korean SME apparel retailers, we examine whether TPCI adoption improves transaction realization and whether it affects retailer-controlled enrollment. TPCI significantly increases orders, units sold, and net units sold, with gains concentrated among customers without retailer accounts; registered customers show no robust response. Monthly new membership signups do not meaningfully decline after adoption, and sales become less concentrated across a broader product range, primarily among unregistered customers. Drawing on technology affordance theory, we interpret these findings as evidence that TPCI expands a low-friction transactional affordance for previously constrained customers without substituting for the relational affordance of retailer membership. More broadly, externally supplied checkout infrastructure can produce functionally selective consequences within retailer-owned e-commerce systems, recovering transactions and broadening realized sales where native friction was greatest while leaving adjacent retailer-controlled outcomes comparatively stable.

detail.abstract: Cybersecurity experts mostly prioritize the evaluation of risk profiles and the creation of effective mitigation strategies. The main objective in this field is to come up with strong ways that will enhance security measures. Modern cyber defenses now have more options thanks to machine learning. The primary causes of the rapid use of cloud services, sophisticated networks, and adaptive programs are storage, processing power, and networking limitations. As digital transformation progresses at an accelerated pace globally, the number of raised privacy and security issues keeps increasing very fast, thus calling for the application of stronger protections against the new threats. The rise in cyberterrorism activities worldwide has been aided by the increasing vulnerabilities in computer systems. For instance, machine learning methods have been used to find ransomware and detect malware, detect online fraud, and validate phishing attempts in order to more effectively handle the worldwide cybersecurity concerns. In order to provide a knowledge of cyber hazards through learning tools and techniques, this study examines the practical use of online behavior modelling for both attack and safety scenarios. It examines common cybersecurity risks and highlights how machine learning helps with vulnerability assessment, open-source risk analysis, and attack detection and prevention.

title: The First Constitution of Digital Space within the Legal Model of Open Environments

detail.title: The First Constitution of Digital Space within the Legal Model of Open Environments
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the applicability of a minimal legal model of open environments to digital space. In prior work (the full version of the paper is available on the SSRN website: https://papers.ssrn.com/abstract=6446698), the concept of an open environment was introduced as a space in which exclusive control cannot be sustainably established, access is potentially universal, and activity develops ahead of its legal formalization. Based on these characteristics, a set of fundamental principles was formulated and expressed in the First Constitution of Space.

The present study extends this framework to digital space. Despite differences in form, digital space exhibits the same structural properties as other open environments, including its distributed nature, transboundary interactions, and resistance to centralized control. At the same time, existing regulatory approaches remain largely grounded in territoriality and centralized authority, leading to persistent inconsistencies between the nature of the environment and the legal mechanisms applied to it.

The paper argues that the principles previously derived for outer space are directly applicable to digital space without modification. On this basis, the First Constitution of Digital Space is formulated as a normative expression of these principles in a different manifestation of an open environment.

The analysis demonstrates that the proposed model does not constitute an additional layer of regulation but reflects a minimal set of conditions required for the sustainable functioning of open environments. In this sense, digital space is not treated as an exceptional case but as further evidence of the broader applicability of the model.

title: Cross-Sectional Return Prediction Using Machine Learning: A Practitioner Pipeline

detail.title: Cross-Sectional Return Prediction Using Machine Learning: A Practitioner Pipeline
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates three machine learning (ML) modelsRidge Regression, XGBoost, and LightGBMfor cross-sectional equity return prediction using real daily price and volume data for 473 U.S. large-cap stocks over November 2018November 2023, sourced from Yahoo Finance. We implement a strict walk-forward pipeline: training on December 2019December 2021, validating on JanuaryJune 2022, and testing on July 2022October 2023a period spanning the 2022 bear market and 2023 recovery. Ten price-based and liquidity features are constructed with strict no-leakage temporal discipline. Ridge Regression achieves the highest out-of-sample R 2 (0.80%), outperforming XGBoost (0.39%) and LightGBM (0.38%), consistent with linear models performing competitively on short data panels with limited signal-to-noise ratios. All three models generate positive mean Information Coecients (0.0520.058), with XGBoost maintaining the highest proportion of positive-IC months (60%). Long-short quintile portfolios yield net annualised Sharpe ratios of 0.66 (Ridge), 0.80 (XGBoost), and 1.49 (Light-GBM) after 15 bps transaction costs. The Deated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) framework reveals that no model achieves DSR > 1.0 under the 16-month test windowa nding driven by the short sample length rather than absence of predictive contentwith Light-GBM nearest at DSR = 0.985. Volatility features (retvol60, retvol20) dominate feature importance across all three architectures, followed by 12-month momentum. All data and results are fully reproducible from freely available Yahoo Finance data using the provided pipeline.

title: Policy-as-Configuration in Immigration Compliance Automation: Architecture for Deterministic, Auditable, and Attorney-Validatable Governance Signals

detail.title: Policy-as-Configuration in Immigration Compliance Automation: Architecture for Deterministic, Auditable, and Attorney-Validatable Governance Signals
detail.abstract: Automated compliance tools are increasingly being introduced into employment-based immigration workflows, generating risk signals, filing recommendations, and adjudication predictions. These systems typically embed regulatory logic directly in application code, making it opaque to legal review, resistant to version control, and impossible to audit at the rule level. When immigration policy changes-through new USCIS memoranda, DOL guidance updates, AAO decisions, or executive action-systems with hardcoded logic require engineering intervention to update, creating a gap between the effective date of a policy change and the system's awareness of it. This paper introduces a policy-as-configuration architecture for immigration compliance automation. In this architecture, policy rules are externalized as structured, versionable data objects with explicit metadata: legal authority, Federal Register citation, effective date, supersession chain, enforcement priority, and evaluation logic. Each policy object carries an independent lifecycle (draft, under review, approved, superseded) enforced by a state machine. A deterministic evaluation engine consumes only approved policies at runtime, producing per-policy verdicts with full evidence provenance. The architecture further specifies mechanisms for attorney validation workflows, append-only policy modification audit trails, and hallucination prevention gates that bound AI-generated intelligence signals to encoded, validated policy rules. The architecture is implemented in a production system governing H-1B sponsorship compliance, currently encoding five active governance policies across employer trust scoring and compliance evaluation. The system ingests signals from seven federal data sources comprising approximately 13.6 million records and produces employer trust-2-scores and employee compliance signals that are fully traceable to their governing policy rules. The paper presents the schema design, state machine specification, evaluation engine architecture, and operational metrics, and argues that the policy-as-configuration pattern is a necessary precondition for trustworthy immigration compliance automation.

title: Distant Writing Journalism: Epistemology, Method, and Accountability of Journalistic Writing in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Distant Writing Journalism: Epistemology, Method, and Accountability of Journalistic Writing in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract:
The growing adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in journalism has so far been examined mainly in terms of automation, ethical concerns, and audience perceptions. While these perspectives are important, they remain insufficient to account for a more fundamental transformation: the epistemological status of journalistic writing when textual production is mediated by automated processes. The central issue is not simply who writes, but how journalistic claims are justified, verified, and rendered accountable in the public sphere.

Building on Luciano Floridi's concept of distant writing and integrating scholarship from journalism studies, epistemology of news, and computational journalism, this article introduces the paradigm of Distant Writing Journalism (DWJ). DWJ reconceptualizes journalistic writing as a design-oriented practice in which journalists are responsible for the processes that lead to the production of texts, rather than for the mechanical act of writing itself.

The article makes three main contributions. It provides a theoretical foundation for DWJ by rethinking authorship, intention, and operational truth in the context of AI-mediated writing. It formalizes an operational method based on claim mapping, verification-by-design, and process disclosure, conceived as replicable and open to empirical assessment. It examines the implications of DWJ for newsroom organization, editorial governance, and public trust, arguing that transparency of method can strengthen journalistic accountability.

The article concludes that Distant Writing Journalism is not a marginal option but a necessary condition for preserving journalism's role as a practice of responsible public knowledge production in the age of generative artificial intelligence.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is being deployed across the electric sector at a pace that existing governance frameworks were not designed to address. Utilities, grid operators, and power generators are integrating AI into load forecasting, grid optimization, contingency assessment, predictive maintenance, and anomaly detection in OT and ICS environments. These are not low-stakes applications. AI systems influencing operational decisions on the Bulk Electric System carry direct consequences for grid reliability, operational safety, and national security.
This paper introduces AAIGF-E, a structured governance and assurance framework comprising domain-specific controls, audit-ready requirements, and a concurrent lifecycle model designed for AI systems in electric sector environments.

title: THE SENTINEL SYSTEM: A FIRST OPERATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION OF EXTERNAL, TRAJECTORY-AWARE AI OVERSIGHT

detail.title: THE SENTINEL SYSTEM: A FIRST OPERATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION OF EXTERNAL, TRAJECTORY-AWARE AI OVERSIGHT

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or personal data. No ethics approval was required.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has reached a stage where its rapid increase in capability is no longer matched by equally advanced mechanisms of oversight and control. In the foundational work "The Sentinel System: A Global Architecture for AI Governance and Safety," Sentinel was introduced as a conceptual and architectural framework designed to provide external, realtime oversight of advanced AI systems. That work established the theoretical, regulatory, and infrastructural foundations required to govern increasingly autonomous and complex artificial intelligence. However, the definition of a global architecture represents only the first phase of system development. The practical viability of such a framework depends on its progressive translation into operational components that can be implemented, tested, and observed under controlled conditions. This paper opens the technical implementation series of the Sentinel System. It does not attempt to disclose the entire architecture in a single document, but initiates its progressive construction by presenting the first operational core of the system. The prototype described in this work implements an external decision-layer capable of analyzing proposed actions, assigning risk levels, and enforcing structured outcomes, including allow, modify, and block. Initial results demonstrate that such a layer can operate consistently in the regulation of individual interactions. However, experimental observation reveals a critical limitation shared by existing oversight approaches: the inability to account for behavioral evolution across sequences of interaction. AI risk does not emerge from isolated outputs alone, but from the progressive transformation of intent over time. This work identifies that limitation and introduces a trajectory-aware extension of the system, incorporating session continuity, cumulative risk evaluation, and escalation detection mechanisms. This enables the system to interpret behavior not as a set of discrete events, but as a continuous process subject to evolution. The results presented in this paper suggest that trajectory-based governance represents a necessary shift in the design of AI oversight systems. Rather than operating on single outputs, control must extend across behavioral sequences, enabling earlier detection of misalignment and more effective intervention. This paper constitutes the first step in a structured series dedicated to the complete technical development of the Sentinel System. Subsequent works will progressively expand the architecture, introduce additional modules, and provide large-scale experimental validation. Together, these contributions aim to transform Sentinel from a conceptual framework into a fully operational, verifiable, and scalable infrastructure for the governance of advanced artificial intelligence.

title: Institutional Intelligence Architecture: Structural Architecture for Enterprise AI That Can Be Governed, Audited, and Trusted

detail.title: Institutional Intelligence Architecture: Structural Architecture for Enterprise AI That Can Be Governed, Audited, and Trusted
detail.abstract: Enterprise AI initiatives fail at scale not because the models are inaccurate, but because the structural architecture surrounding them is unstable. This paper identifies eight structural failure patterns organized into three categories of systemic instability — semantic, inference, and learning — and presents the Institutional Intelligence Architecture: a five-layer architecture that grounds every request in verified operational data, encodes institutional meaning in a formal ontology, embeds governance constraints as machine-checkable rules, separates the language model's interpretive function from the knowledge graph's authority validation function, and accumulates institutional knowledge from governed decisions. The architecture is demonstrated against a fabricated organization with a live Neo4j knowledge graph and a governed inference pipeline. A meta-ontological layer monitors alignment between the knowledge architecture and evolving operational reality, generating typed structural hypotheses when behavioral patterns signal governance drift. The paper distinguishes this approach from recent work on ontology-constrained neural reasoning (Tuan, 2026), arguing that output-side authorization validation — determining whether the requesting actor holds institutional authority — is a structurally different operation from the correctness checking the existing literature proposes. The working proof of concept is publicly available.

title: Governed Collaborative Whiteboard With Real-Time Analytics
affiliations: AnantraoPawar College of Engineering and Research

detail.title: Governed Collaborative Whiteboard With Real-Time Analytics

contentType.other: Latest Paper on Collaborative and Analytical Tool

detail.abstract: Growing reliance on digital collaboration has exposed fundamental weaknesses in existing whiteboard platforms, particularly their inability to enforce user governance or produce measurable insights from interaction data. This paper introduces a web-based collaborative whiteboard that embeds role-based access control, behavioral tracking, and a live analytics layer into a unified system. Built on contemporary web technologies, the platform sustains low-latency synchronization while continuously collecting session data for analysis. Preliminary observations confirm that governed access combined with real-time monitoring yields measurable improvements in collaboration quality and user accountability. The architecture is designed to scale, with planned extensions toward AI-assisted analytics and predictive modeling.

title: Adaptive Behavioral Governance for AI Agents: A Quantitative Risk Scoring Framework Derived from Trading Decision Tree Pruning

detail.title: Adaptive Behavioral Governance for AI Agents: A Quantitative Risk Scoring Framework Derived from Trading Decision Tree Pruning
detail.abstract: AI agents increasingly execute high-impact actions-communication, file operations, and financial workflows-yet current governance approaches often collapse to either static capability restriction or post-hoc monitoring. This paper proposes a quantitative governance framework that transfers a proven risk-control logic from trading decision systems to agent execution control. The framework combines: (i) a five-layer architecture with process-level separation between stochastic language understanding and deterministic adjudication, (ii) a six-dimensional risk model for action scoring, (iii) monotonic tiered execution policies with veto and circuit-breaker overrides, and (iv) bounded adaptive calibration using approval and outcome feedback. A shadow-mode deployment protocol is introduced to calibrate thresholds before enforcement, operationalizing a "backtest-before-live" principle for agent governance. In a preliminary singleuser deployment (157 decision records), the scoring outputs exhibit bimodal separation between routine read actions and higher-risk write/external actions, motivating a conservative tightening of the autonomous threshold from 0.25 to 0.20 prior to live enforcement. The contribution is practical rather than formal: the framework is configuration-driven, reproducible in a minimal open-source profile, and extensible to stricter organizational controls without code changes. Results provide preliminary evidence that quantitative, context-aware, and feedback-calibrated governance can improve the safety-utility trade-off relative to static permissioning and monitor-only paradigms.

detail.abstract: In modern cloud-native environments, the frequency of state changes (ω_c) in IT systems is expanding exponentially. This paper elucidates the functional limitations of Managed Service Providers (MSPs) using a Socio-Technical Systems (STS) approach combined with mathematical models from control engineering. By formulating the "Time Delay (e^-Ls)" caused by organizational boundaries within Japan's multi-layered subcontracting structure, we mathematically prove that entering high-frequency domains inevitably leads to a loss of phase margin and subsequent system divergence (operational collapse). Furthermore, to avert this physical collapse, financial imperatives—such as rigid Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and the necessity for MSPs to act as "payment buffers" accommodating traditional invoice-based billing—exert immense negative pressure. This pressure locks IT architectures into a "solid state" of virtualized on-premises environments, such as IaaS and VPS, preventing true cloud-native fluidity. We conclude that the stagnation in cloud migration is not merely a technological failure, but a "co-dependent stagnation" where social institutions and technical structures mutually restrict evolution. Achieving a phase transition to next-generation MSP 2.0/3.0 requires moving beyond technological updates to embrace paradigm shifts in contract models and minimize the Mean Time to Trust (MTTT) necessary for governing Agentic AI.

detail.abstract:
Abstract

The rapid advancement of military artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed modern warfare, shifting decision-making processes from exclusively human judgment to hybrid human–algorithmic systems. This evolution has generated a significant “compliance gap,” wherein traditional, retrospective legal frameworks—particularly those governing International Humanitarian Law (IHL)—are increasingly unable to keep pace with the speed, autonomy, and complexity of AI-driven operations.

In response, this research advances a novel regulatory paradigm based on Programmable Compliance, which entails embedding legal norms directly into the technical architecture of military AI systems. Rather than relying on post hoc legal assessments, this approach ensures ex ante compliance by design.

The proposed framework is structured around four integrated pillars: Red-Line Code, which encodes core IHL principles—distinction, proportionality, and precaution—into non-overridable software constraints; The Black Box, which ensures transparency through comprehensive recording of data inputs, algorithmic processes, and human interventions; Dual Accountability Model, which distributes legal responsibility between human actors and technical entities; and International Governance Mechanism (MAIA), a proposed authority to standardize and oversee global compliance while preserving state sovereignty.

The research concludes that the future of regulating military AI lies in operationalizing the principle of “Code as Law,” whereby systems are designed to be structurally incapable of violating international legal norms.

detail.abstract:
The United Kingdom's Making Tax Digital (MTD) program represents one of the most ambitious digital reforms in global tax administration. By requiring businesses to maintain digital records and submit returns using HMRC-approved software, MTD aims to close the tax gap, minimise human error, and modernise compliance processes. This study combines a quantitative analysis of a synthetic dataset of 500 small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with a critical policy evaluation of HMRC's reform strategy. Findings reveal that while MTD reduces error rates and improves on-time filing compliance, the initiative introduces notable financial and administrative burdens for micro and small enterprises. Correlation analysis highlights significant relationships between turnover, compliance error rates, administrative hours, and satisfaction levels. The study concludes with a set of recommendations to enhance the inclusivity and effectiveness of MTD, ensuring that benefits are equitably distributed across the UK's diverse SME landscape. Making Tax Digital (MTD) represents a major transformation in the UK tax system, led by HMRC to improve efficiency, transparency, and compliance through digitalisation. This study evaluates the impact of MTD on small business compliance and critically examines HMRC’s broader digital reform strategy.

The findings indicate that MTD has significantly enhanced record-keeping accuracy and reduced manual errors through mandatory digital submissions. Small businesses adopting cloud-based accounting systems demonstrate improved tax reporting consistency and real-time financial visibility. However, the transition has imposed notable challenges, particularly for micro and small enterprises with limited digital literacy, financial resources, and access to technological infrastructure.

Compliance costs have increased in the short term due to software adoption, training requirements, and system integration. Despite these barriers, long-term benefits include streamlined tax processes, reduced audit risks, and improved financial management practices.

HMRC’s digital reform strategy is largely effective in modernising tax administration but requires stronger support mechanisms. These include targeted training programs, financial assistance for digital adoption, and improved system usability. Without such measures, there remains a risk of widening the compliance gap among less digitally advanced businesses.

Overall, MTD is a progressive policy initiative with clear long-term advantages, but its success depends on inclusive implementation and continuous system refinement.

title: The State-Contingent Debt Premium: Evidence from French Public Bonds
affiliations: Santa Clara University - Leavey School of Business - Economics Department and ESCP Business School

detail.title: The State-Contingent Debt Premium: Evidence from French Public Bonds

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: State-contingent debt (SCD) instruments have been proposed as an improvement to sovereign debt markets, but their issuance costs are not well understood. We estimate the SCD premium at issuance and for more than a decade thereafter, employing a quasi-twin bond strategy that uses two very similar French government bonds issued in 1956: one conventional bond and one state-contingent bond with coupons linked to industrial production. At issuance, the expected yield on the SCD bond was 77 basis points higher than its twin. Due to robust growth in the French economy ex-post, the realized SCD premium at issuance was roughly twice as large (146 basis points). However, rising market prices of the state-contingent bond reduced both spreads to zero by 1964. They rose again in May 1968 following an unexpected general strike, which significantly reduced French industrial production; however, by 1970, the SCD premium had fallen to values close to zero.
